claims.statement: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) adalah novel Tiongkok yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en.
claims.quote: is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.

claims.statement: The opening part of the novel deals with the early exploits of Sun Wukong, a monkey born on Flower Fruit Mountain from a stone egg, who learns the Tao, 72 transformations, combat, and the secrets of immortality.
claims.statement_id: Bagian awal novel menceritakan petualangan awal Sun Wukong, seekor kera yang lahir di Gunung Bunga dan Buah (Flower Fruit Mountain) dari telur batu, yang mempelajari Tao, 72 transformasi, ilmu tempur, dan rahasia keabadian.
claims.quote: The beginning part of the story deals with the earlier exploits of Sun Wukong, a monkey born on Flower Fruit Mountain from a stone egg that forms from an ancient rock created by the coupling of Heaven and Earth, who learns the art of the Tao, 72 polymorphic transformations, combat, and secrets of immortality

claims.statement: Sun Wukong, also known as the Monkey King, is a literary and religious figure best known as one of the main characters of the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong, juga dikenal sebagai Raja Kera (Monkey King), adalah tokoh sastra dan keagamaan yang paling dikenal sebagai salah satu tokoh utama novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West.
claims.quote: also known as the Monkey King, is a literary and religious figure best known as one of the main characters in the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West.

claims.statement: In the novel Sun Wukong is an intelligent monkey (likely a rhesus macaque or a golden snub-nosed monkey) born from a stone who gains supernatural powers through Taoist practice and heavenly food.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong adalah kera cerdas (kemungkinan rhesus makaka atau monyet hidung pesek emas) yang lahir dari batu dan memperoleh kekuatan gaib lewat latihan Tao serta makanan surgawi.
claims.quote: In the novel, Sun Wukong is an intelligent monkey (likely a rhesus macaque or a golden snub-nosed monkey) born from a stone who acquires supernatural powers through Taoist practices and consuming heavenly victuals.

claims.statement: After rebelling against heaven he is imprisoned under a mountain by the Buddha. Five hundred years later he accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang, who rides the White Dragon Horse, with two other disciples, Zhu Bajie and Sha Heshang, to obtain Buddhist sutras in the West.
claims.statement_id: Setelah memberontak melawan surga, ia dipenjara di bawah gunung oleh Buddha. Lima ratus tahun kemudian ia menemani biksu Tang Sanzang, yang menunggang White Dragon Horse, bersama dua murid lain, Zhu Bajie dan Sha Heshang, mengambil sutra Buddha di Barat.
claims.quote: After rebelling against heaven, he is imprisoned under a mountain by the Buddha. Five hundred years later, he accompanies the monk Tang Sanzang riding on the White Dragon Horse and two other disciples, Zhu Bajie and Sha Heshang, on a journey to obtain Buddhist sutras in the West or Western Paradise, where Buddha and his followers dwell.

claims.statement: Sun Wukong has many abilities, including supernatural strength; he can support the weight of two heavy mountains on his shoulders.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong memiliki banyak kemampuan, antara lain kekuatan supernatural; ia mampu memikul beban dua gunung berat di bahunya.
claims.quote: Sun Wukong possesses many abilities. He has supernatural strength and is able to support the weight of two heavy mountains on his shoulders

claims.statement: Sun Wukong acquires the 72 Earthly Transformations, which give him 72 unique powers, including the ability to transform into animals and objects.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong memperoleh 72 Transformasi Duniawi, yang memberinya 72 kekuatan unik, termasuk kemampuan berubah menjadi hewan dan benda.
claims.quote: Sun Wukong acquires the 72 Earthly Transformations, which allow him to access 72 unique powers, including the ability to transform into animals and objects.

claims.statement: The cloud somersault is often portrayed as Wukong riding a cloud; his master Puti Zushi taught it to give him a style of flying suited to his love of jumping.
claims.statement_id: Kemampuan salto awan sering digambarkan sebagai Wukong menunggang awan; guru Puti Zushi mengajarkannya agar Wukong memiliki cara terbang yang cocok dengan kegemarannya melompat.
claims.quote: The ability, oft portrayed as Wukong riding a nimbus-like cloud, requires a magic hand sign, an oral spell, a fist clench, and a body shake. Wukong's master Puti Zushi taught this ability to the monkey to give him a style of flying that complements his penchant for jumping.

claims.statement: Sun Wukong is said to have gained immortality through nine different means and instances, making him one of the most immortal and invincible beings in all of creation.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong dikatakan memperoleh keabadian lewat sembilan cara dan peristiwa berbeda, yang menjadikannya salah satu makhluk paling abadi dan kebal di seluruh ciptaan.
claims.quote: Sun Wukong is said to have gained immortality through nine different means and instances, which together made him one of the most immortal and invincible beings in all of creation.

claims.statement: Guanyin gives Tang Sanzang a magical circlet from the Buddha that can never be removed once the Monkey King is tricked into wearing it; when Tang Sanzang chants a certain sutra the band tightens and causes an unbearable headache.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin memberi Tang Sanzang sebuah lingkaran gaib dari Buddha yang tidak dapat dilepas setelah Raja Kera dibujuk memakainya; saat Tang Sanzang melafalkan sutra tertentu, lingkaran itu mengetat dan menimbulkan sakit kepala tak tertahankan.
claims.quote: a magical circlet which, once the Monkey King is tricked into putting it on, can never be removed. When Tang Sanzang chants a certain sutra, the band will tighten and cause an unbearable headache.

claims.statement: The surname Sūn was given as an in-joke about the monkey, since monkeys are also called húsūn (猢猻), a word that can mean a monkey literally or figuratively.
claims.statement_id: Marga Sūn diberikan sebagai lelucon tentang kera, karena kera juga disebut húsūn (猢猻), kata yang dapat berarti kera secara harfiah maupun kiasan.
claims.quote: The surname Sūn was given as an in-joke about the monkey, as monkeys are also called húsūn (猢猻), and can mean either a literal or a figurative monkey (or a macaque).

claims.statement: The given name Wùkōng means "awakened to emptiness", sometimes translated as "aware of vacuity".
claims.statement_id: Nama pemberian Wùkōng berarti "tersadar akan kekosongan", kadang diterjemahkan "sadar akan kehampaan".
claims.quote: The given name, Wùkōng, means "awakened to emptiness", sometimes translated as "aware of vacuity".

claims.statement: Sun Wukong is pronounced Son Gokū in Japanese, Tôn Ngộ Không in Vietnamese, Sung Ghokong or Sung Gokhong in Javanese and Sun Gokong in Malay, among other languages.
claims.statement_id: Nama Sun Wukong dilafalkan Son Gokū dalam bahasa Jepang, Tôn Ngộ Không dalam bahasa Vietnam, Sung Ghokong atau Sung Gokhong dalam bahasa Jawa, dan Sun Gokong dalam bahasa Melayu, di antara bahasa lain.
claims.quote: Son Gokū in Japanese, Sonogong in Korean ... Tôn Ngộ Không in Vietnamese, Sung Ghokong or Sung Gokhong in Javanese, Sun Ngokong in Thai, Wu Khone in Burmese, and Sun Gokong in Malay.

claims.statement: The earliest known literary prototype of Sun Wukong appears in a Song dynasty (960–1279) storyteller's prompt-book, Poetic Tale of Tripitaka of the Great Tang Fetching Scriptures, a 17-chapter text that calls him the "Monkey Pilgrim" (猴行者, Hou Xingzhe).
claims.statement_id: Prototipe sastra tertua yang diketahui dari Sun Wukong muncul dalam buku pegangan juru cerita dinasti Song (960–1279), Poetic Tale of Tripitaka of the Great Tang Fetching Scriptures, teks 17 bab yang menyebutnya "Monkey Pilgrim" (猴行者, Hou Xingzhe).
claims.quote: The earliest known literary prototype of Sun Wukong appears in the Song dynasty (960–1279) storyteller's prompt-book Poetic Tale of Tripitaka of the Great Tang Fetching Scriptures (大唐三藏取經詩話). In this 17-chapter text, the character is known as the "Monkey Pilgrim" (猴行者, Hou Xingzhe).

claims.statement: Unlike the Ming dynasty classic, in which the monkey is freed from under a mountain, the Monkey Pilgrim approaches Xuanzang of his own accord.
claims.statement_id: Berbeda dari novel dinasti Ming yang menceritakan kera dibebaskan dari bawah gunung, Monkey Pilgrim mendekati Xuanzang atas kehendaknya sendiri.
claims.quote: Unlike the Ming dynasty classic where the monkey is freed from under a mountain, the Monkey Pilgrim voluntarily approaches Xuanzang

claims.statement: In that text the Monkey Pilgrim is Xuanzang's sole magical protector, since the characters of Zhu Bajie (Pigsy) and Sha Wujing (Sandy) had not yet been fully developed as fellow disciples.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks itu, Monkey Pilgrim menjadi satu-satunya pelindung gaib Xuanzang, karena tokoh Zhu Bajie (Pigsy) dan Sha Wujing (Sandy) belum dikembangkan sepenuhnya sebagai sesama murid.
claims.quote: Throughout the text, the Monkey Pilgrim serves as Xuanzang's sole magical protector, as the characters of Zhu Bajie (Pigsy) and Sha Wujing (Sandy) had not yet been fully developed as fellow disciples.

claims.statement: Hu Shih first suggested that Wu Cheng'en may have been influenced by the Hindu deity Hanuman of the Ramayana in his depictions of the Monkey King.
claims.statement_id: Hu Shih pertama kali mengusulkan bahwa Wu Cheng'en mungkin dipengaruhi dewa Hindu Hanuman dari Ramayana dalam penggambarannya tentang Raja Kera.
claims.quote: Hu Shih first suggested that Wu Cheng'en may have been influenced by the Hindu deity Hanuman from the Ramayana in his depictions of the Monkey King.

claims.statement: Instead, Lu Xun suggested the 9th-century Chinese deity Wuzhiqi, who appears as a sibling of Sun Wukong in older Yuan dynasty stories, as the inspiration.
claims.statement_id: Sebaliknya, Lu Xun mengusulkan dewa Tiongkok abad ke-9 Wuzhiqi, yang muncul sebagai saudara Sun Wukong dalam kisah dinasti Yuan yang lebih tua, sebagai sumber inspirasinya.
claims.quote: Instead, Lu Xun suggested the 9th-century Chinese deity Wuzhiqi, who appears as a sibling of Sun Wukong in older Yuan dynasty stories, as the inspiration.

claims.statement: According to Li Tianfei, the Monkey King of the final novel combines two separate folklore traditions that merged during the Yuan dynasty (1271–1368).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Li Tianfei, Raja Kera dalam novel akhir menggabungkan dua tradisi cerita rakyat terpisah yang bersatu pada masa dinasti Yuan (1271–1368).
claims.quote: According to Li, the Monkey King in the final novel combines two separate folklore traditions that merged during the Yuan dynasty (1271–1368).

claims.statement: In parts of southern China, including Sichuan, Fujian and Guangdong, local folklore featured powerful ape spirits that were worshipped and given titles such as "Great Sage Equal to Heaven" (齐天大圣).
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa bagian Tiongkok selatan, termasuk Sichuan, Fujian, dan Guangdong, cerita rakyat setempat memuat roh kera perkasa yang dipuja dan diberi gelar seperti "Great Sage Equal to Heaven" (齐天大圣).
claims.quote: In parts of southern China, including Sichuan, Fujian, and Guangdong, local folklore featured powerful ape spirits that were worshipped and given titles such as "Great Sage Equal to Heaven" (齐天大圣).

claims.statement: He forms a brotherhood called the Seven Sages (七聖) with the Bull Demon King (牛魔王) and other spirit kings, among them the Roc Demon King and the Lion Spirit King.
claims.statement_id: Ia membentuk persaudaraan bernama Tujuh Resi (Seven Sages, 七聖) dengan Bull Demon King (牛魔王) serta raja-raja siluman lain, antara lain Raja Roc dan Raja Singa.
claims.quote: He forms a brotherhood called the Seven Sages (七聖) with the Bull Demon King (牛魔王), the Saurian Demon King (蛟魔王), the Roc Demon King (鵬魔王), the Lion Spirit King (獅狔王), the Macaque Spirit King (獼猴王), and the snub-nosed monkey Spirit King (禺狨王).

claims.statement: Guanyin suggests the Jade Emperor's nephew Erlang Shen fight Wukong; Wukong and Erlang are evenly matched and eventually both turn into terrifying figures, which scares Wukong's monkey army away.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin menyarankan Erlang Shen, keponakan Kaisar Giok, melawan Wukong; Wukong dan Erlang sama kuat; keduanya akhirnya berubah menjadi sosok menakutkan yang membuat pasukan kera Wukong lari ketakutan.
claims.quote: Guanyin suggests the Jade Emperor's nephew Erlang Shen fight Wukong. Wukong and Erlang are evenly matched and eventually, both turn into terrifying figures, which scares Wukong's monkey army away.

claims.statement: Sun Wukong defeats the Army of Heaven's 100,000 celestial warriors, the 28 constellations and the Four Heavenly Kings, under the command of Devaraja Li and his third son Nezha.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong mengalahkan 100.000 prajurit langit Army of Heaven, 28 rasi bintang, dan Empat Raja Surgawi di bawah komando Devaraja Li dan putra ketiganya, Nezha.
claims.quote: Sun Wukong defeats the Army of Heaven's 100,000 celestial warriors, the 28 constellations and the Four Heavenly Kings, under the command of Devaraja Li and his third son, Princes Nezha, despite the Heavenly weapons used against him.

claims.statement: Wukong's fellow spiritual primates include the Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴), who is one of his antagonists in the main storyline.
claims.statement_id: Sesama primata rohani Wukong antara lain Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴), yang menjadi salah satu lawannya dalam alur utama.
claims.quote: His fellow spiritual primates are the Six-Eared Macaque (六耳獼猴), who is one of his antagonists in the main storyline

claims.statement: The brief satirical novel Xiyoubu (c. 1640) follows Sun Wukong trapped in a magical dream world created by the Qing Fish Demon, the embodiment of desire.
claims.statement_id: Novel satir pendek Xiyoubu (sekitar 1640) mengisahkan Sun Wukong terjebak di dunia mimpi gaib ciptaan Qing Fish Demon, perwujudan keinginan.
claims.quote: The brief satirical novel Xiyoubu (西遊補; "Supplement to the Journey to the West"), c. 1640, follows Sun Wukong as he is trapped in a magical dream world created by the Qing Fish Demon, the embodiment of desire

claims.statement: A Chinese Odyssey is a fantasy comedy film made in Hong Kong in 1995.
claims.statement_id: A Chinese Odyssey adalah film komedi fantasi yang dibuat di Hong Kong pada 1995.
claims.quote: A Chinese Odyssey is a fantasy comedy film made in Hong Kong 1995.

claims.statement: Donnie Yen plays Sun Wukong in the 2014 movie The Monkey King.
claims.statement_id: Donnie Yen memerankan Sun Wukong dalam film The Monkey King tahun 2014.
claims.quote: Martial Arts Superstar Donnie Yen plays Sun Wukong in the 2014 movie The Monkey King

claims.statement: The character Son Goku in Dragon Ball is based on Sun Wukong, as shown by his monkey tail, staff, flying cloud and name.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh Son Goku dalam Dragon Ball didasarkan pada Sun Wukong, terlihat dari ekor kera, tongkat, awan terbang, dan namanya.
claims.quote: The character of Son Goku in Dragon Ball is based on Sun Wukong, as attested by his monkey tail, staff, flying cloud, and name

claims.statement: The character Monkey in the 1978 Japanese television series Monkey is based on Sun Wukong.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh Monkey dalam serial televisi Jepang Monkey tahun 1978 didasarkan pada Sun Wukong.
claims.quote: The character of Monkey in the 1978 Japanese television series Monkey is based on Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: In the introduction to his 1913 translation, Timothy Richard writes that Sun Wu Kung is a monkey who personates the irrepressible human mind, the discoverer, the inventive genius, full of resource.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahannya tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menulis bahwa Sun Wu Kung adalah kera yang melambangkan pikiran manusia yang tak terkendali, sang penemu, jenius pencipta yang penuh akal.
claims.quote: Sun Wu Kung. A monkey who personates the irrepressible human mind, the discoverer, the inventive genius, full of resource

claims.statement: In Richard's 1913 translation, one day the living stone split open and produced a round stone egg; after exposure to the air it became a stone monkey with the five senses complete, able to creep and run.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913), suatu hari batu hidup itu terbelah dan menghasilkan telur batu bundar; setelah terkena udara, telur itu menjadi kera batu dengan kelima indra lengkap dan mampu merayap serta berlari.
claims.quote: On a certain day it split open and produced a stone egg, round like a big ball. After exposure to the air, this was transformed into a stone monkey with the five senses of the body complete, and able to creep and run.

claims.statement: Richard explains that the hat of spikes worn by the Monkey pricks his head and gives great pain when the Master orders some very difficult work and the Monkey hesitates.
claims.statement_id: Richard menjelaskan bahwa topi berduri yang dipakai Kera menusuk kepalanya dan menimbulkan sakit hebat bila Sang Guru memerintahkan pekerjaan sulit dan Kera ragu.
claims.quote: the Master orders some very difficult work to be done, and the Monkey hesitates, the spikes enter into his head and give great pain.

claims.statement: In the original text (chapter 1), a stone holding an immortal "womb" split open one day and produced a stone egg the size of a ball; touched by the wind it became a stone monkey with all five senses and four limbs complete.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks asli novel (bab 1), sebuah batu yang mengandung "kantong gaib" pecah pada suatu hari dan melahirkan telur batu sebesar bola; terkena angin, telur itu menjadi kera batu dengan panca indra dan keempat anggota badan lengkap.
claims.quote: 內育仙胞，一日迸裂，產一石卵，似圓毬樣大。因見風，化作一個石猴，五官俱備，四肢皆全。

claims.statement: The monkeys bow and hail him as "千歲大王"; the stone ape then ascends the throne, drops the word "stone" from his name, and is called the Handsome Monkey King (美猴王).
claims.statement_id: Para kera memberi hormat dan menyebutnya "千歲大王"; kera batu itu pun naik takhta, menanggalkan kata "batu" dari namanya, dan disebut Raja Kera Tampan (美猴王).
claims.quote: 眾猴聽說，即拱伏無違，一個個序齒排班，朝上禮拜，都稱「千歲大王」。自此，石猿高登王位，將「石」字兒隱了，遂稱「美猴王」。

claims.statement: The Handsome Monkey King led a troop of apes and monkeys; by day they roamed Flower Fruit Mountain (花果山) and by night they lodged in the Water Curtain Cave (水簾洞).
claims.statement_id: Raja Kera Tampan memimpin sekelompok kera dan monyet; mereka berkelana di Gunung Bunga dan Buah (花果山) pada siang hari dan bermalam di Gua Tirai Air (水簾洞) pada malam hari.
claims.quote: 美猴王領一群猿猴、獼猴、馬猴等，分派了君臣佐使。朝遊花果山，暮宿水簾洞

claims.statement: The Monkey King resolves to leave the mountain and wander far to find the three kinds of beings who escape death, so as to learn ageless long life and avoid the hardship of King Yama.
claims.statement_id: Raja Kera memutuskan turun gunung, mengembara jauh untuk mencari tiga golongan makhluk yang luput dari kematian, agar belajar hidup abadi dan menghindari bencana dari Raja Yama.
claims.quote: 我明日就辭汝等下山，雲遊海角，遠涉天涯，務必訪此三者，學一個不老長生，常躲過閻君之難。

claims.statement: The patriarch (祖師) says that in his school's sequence of twelve characters the monkey's turn falls on the character "悟", and gives him the dharma name "孫悟空", which the monkey gladly accepts.
claims.statement_id: Sang guru (祖師) berkata bahwa urutan dua belas aksara nama perguruannya jatuh pada aksara "悟" bagi si kera, lalu memberinya nama dharma "孫悟空"; si kera menerimanya dengan gembira.
claims.quote: 祖師道：「乃廣、大、智、慧、真、如、性、海、穎、悟、圓、覺十二字。排到你，正當『悟』字。與你起個法名叫做『孫悟空』，好麼？」猴王笑道：「好！好！好！自今就叫做孫悟空也。」

claims.statement: The patriarch says the monkey's body is unlovely yet like a pine-nut-eating macaque (猢猻), and after discussing the characters 猢 and 猻 gives him the surname "孫".
claims.statement_id: Sang guru menilai tubuh si kera buruk tetapi mirip kera pemakan buah pinus, lalu memberinya marga "孫" setelah membahas aksara 猢 dan 猻.
claims.quote: 你身軀雖是鄙陋，卻像個食松果的猢猻。我與你就身上取個姓氏，意思教你姓『猢』。猢字去了個獸傍，乃是個古月。古者，老也；月者，陰也。老陰不能化育，教你姓『猻』倒好。猻字去了獸傍，乃是個子系。子者，兒男也；系者。嬰細也，正合嬰兒之本論。教你姓『孫』罷。

claims.statement: In chapter 2 the Monkey King, once one opening is clear, finds a hundred open; he learns the oral formula, practises on his own, and masters the seventy-two transformations.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 2, si Raja Kera menguasai satu hal lalu seratus hal lain menyusul; ia mempelajari rumus lisan, berlatih sendiri, dan menguasai tujuh puluh dua perubahan wujud.
claims.quote: 這猴王也是他一竅通時百竅通，當時習了口訣，自修自煉，將七十二般變化都學成了。

claims.statement: The patriarch teaches the somersault cloud: with a hand sign, a spell, a clenched fist and a shake of the body, one somersault covers 108,000 li.
claims.statement_id: Sang guru mengajarkan awan salto: dengan rumus tangan, mantra, kepalan, dan guncangan tubuh, sekali salto menempuh seratus delapan ribu li.
claims.quote: 這朵雲，捻著訣，念動真言，攢緊了拳，將身一抖，跳將起來，一觔斗就有十萬八千里路哩。

claims.statement: In chapter 3 the weapon Wukong takes has two gold bands at its ends and a length of black iron between them, inscribed "如意金箍棒" (Ruyi Jingu Bang), weighing 13,500 jin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 3, senjata yang dipilih Wukong berujung dua gelang emas dengan batang besi hitam di tengah, bertuliskan "如意金箍棒" (tongkat gelang emas sesuka hati) seberat 13.500 kati.
claims.quote: 悟空十分歡喜，拿出海藏看時，原來兩頭是兩個金箍，中間乃一段烏鐵。緊挨箍有鐫成的一行字，喚做：「如意金箍棒，重一萬三千五百斤。

claims.statement: The Jade Emperor decrees that Wukong be made a "弼馬溫" (keeper of the horses) and sends him to the imperial stables to take up the post.
claims.statement_id: Kaisar Giok menetapkan Wukong sebagai "弼馬溫" (pengurus kuda) dan mengirimnya ke istal kerajaan untuk menjabat.
claims.quote: 玉帝傳旨道：「就除他做個弼馬溫罷。」眾臣叫謝恩，他也只朝上唱個大喏。玉帝又差木德星官送他去御馬監到任。

claims.statement: After the horse-keeper post, a banner reading "齊天大聖" (Great Sage Equal to Heaven) is set up and Wukong orders that he be called by that title and no longer "king".
claims.statement_id: Setelah menolak jabatan pengurus kuda, Wukong menyiapkan panji bertuliskan "齊天大聖" dan memerintahkan agar ia hanya disebut Sang Resi Setara Langit, bukan raja.
claims.quote: 就做個齊天大聖，有何不可？」猴王聞說，歡喜不勝，連道幾個「好！好！好！」教四健將：「就替我快置個旌旗，旗上寫『齊天大聖』四大字，立竿張掛。自此以後，只稱我為齊天大聖，不許再稱大王。

claims.statement: The Jade Emperor assigns Wukong to take charge of the Peach Garden (蟠桃園) for the time being.
claims.statement_id: Kaisar Giok menugaskan Wukong mengurus Kebun Persik Panjang Umur (蟠桃園) sementara waktu.
claims.quote: 朕見你身閑無事，與你件執事：你且權管那蟠桃園，早晚好生在意。

claims.statement: The Buddha proposes a wager: if Wukong can somersault out of his right palm in a single leap, Wukong wins.
claims.statement_id: Buddha menantang Wukong bertaruh: bila Wukong mampu sekali salto keluar dari telapak tangan kanannya, ia dianggap menang.
claims.quote: 佛祖道：「我與你打個賭賽：你若有本事，一觔斗打出我這右手掌中，算你贏

claims.statement: The Buddha turns his palm, pushes the Monkey King out of the West Heaven Gate, and turns his five fingers into five linked mountains called the Five Elements Mountain (五行山).
claims.statement_id: Buddha membalik telapak tangannya, mendorong Raja Kera keluar dari gerbang barat surga, dan mengubah lima jarinya menjadi lima gunung berantai bernama Gunung Lima Unsur (五行山).
claims.quote: 被佛祖翻掌一撲，把這猴王推出西天門外，將五指化作金、木、水、火、土五座聯山，喚名「五行山」

claims.statement: At the end of the novel the Buddha recalls that Sun Wukong made havoc in the heavenly palace and was pressed under the Five Elements Mountain, and for his merit in subduing demons along the way names him the Buddha Victorious in Fighting (鬥戰勝佛).
claims.statement_id: Di akhir novel, Buddha menyebut Sun Wukong pernah mengacau istana langit dan ditindih di bawah Gunung Lima Unsur; karena jasanya menaklukkan iblis di sepanjang jalan, ia dianugerahi gelar Buddha Pemenang Pertempuran (鬥戰勝佛).
claims.quote: 孫悟空，汝因大鬧天宮，吾以甚深法力，壓在五行山下，幸天災滿足，歸於釋教；且喜汝隱惡揚善，在途中煉魔降怪有功，全終全始，加陞大職正果，汝為鬥戰勝佛。

claims.statement: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) adalah novel Tiongkok yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en.
claims.quote: is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.

claims.statement: He was supposed to be reborn as a human but ended up in the womb of a sow because of an error on the Reincarnation Wheel, which turned him into a half-man, half-pig humanoid monster.
claims.statement_id: Ia seharusnya terlahir kembali sebagai manusia tetapi berakhir di rahim babi betina akibat kesalahan pada Roda Reinkarnasi, sehingga menjadi monster humanoid setengah manusia setengah babi.
claims.quote: He was supposed to be reborn as a human but ended up in the womb of a sow due to an error on the Reincarnation Wheel, which turned him into a half-man, half-pig humanoid monster.

claims.statement: He is also capable of 36 transformations and can travel on clouds, but not as fast as Sun Wukong.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga mampu melakukan 36 perubahan wujud dan dapat bepergian dengan awan, tetapi tidak secepat Sun Wukong.
claims.quote: He is also capable of 36 transformations and can travel on clouds, but not as fast as Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: His weapon of choice is the jiuchidingpa (九齒釘耙), the "nine-tooth iron rake".
claims.statement_id: Senjata pilihannya adalah jiuchidingpa (九齒釘耙), "garu besi bergigi sembilan".
claims.quote: His weapon of choice is the jiuchidingpa (九齿钉耙; 九齒釘耙; jiǔchǐdīngpá; "nine-tooth iron rake").

claims.statement: Wukong becomes Tang Sanzang's first disciple and provides three other disciples who agree to help in order to atone for their sins: Zhu Bajie, Sha Wujing and White Dragon Horse.
claims.statement_id: Wukong diberi tugas menjadi murid pertama Tang Sanzang dan menyediakan tiga murid lain yang bersedia membantu demi menebus dosa mereka: Zhu Bajie, Sha Wujing, dan White Dragon Horse.
claims.quote: three other disciples who agree to help him in order to atone for their sins: Zhu Bajie, Sha Wujing and White Dragon Horse.

claims.statement: His lust for women, extreme laziness and greediness made his spirituality the lowest in the group, with even the White Dragon Horse achieving more than him; he remained on Earth and was granted the title "Cleaner of the Altars".
claims.statement_id: Nafsu terhadap perempuan, kemalasan ekstrem, dan keserakahan membuat kerohaniannya terendah dalam rombongan, bahkan White Dragon Horse mencapai lebih darinya; ia tetap di bumi dan dianugerahi gelar "Cleaner of the Altars".
claims.quote: made his spirituality the lowest in the group, with even the White Dragon Horse achieving more than him, and he remained on Earth and was granted the title "Cleaner of the Altars,"

claims.statement: Once an immortal who was the Marshal of the Heavenly Canopy, commanding 100,000 naval soldiers of the Milky Way.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu seorang abadi yang menjadi Marshal of the Heavenly Canopy, memimpin 100.000 prajurit laut Bima Sakti.
claims.quote: Once an immortal who was the Marshal of the Heavenly Canopy commanding 100,000 naval soldiers of the Milky Way

claims.statement: Zhu Bajie, also named Zhu Wuneng, is one of the three disciples of Tang Sanzang, along with Sun Wukong and Sha Heshang, and a major character of the 16th-century novel Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Zhu Bajie, juga bernama Zhu Wuneng, adalah salah satu dari tiga murid Tang Sanzang bersama Sun Wukong dan Sha Heshang, serta tokoh utama novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West.
claims.quote: Zhu Bajie, also named Zhu Wuneng, is one of the three disciples of Tang Sanzang, along with Sun Wukong and Sha Heshang, and a major character of the 16th-century novel Journey to the West.

claims.statement: Zhu means "swine" and Bajie means "eight precepts". Before being recruited by the bodhisattva Guanyin, Zhu Bajie was known as Zhu Gāngliè (豬剛巤), literally "Strong-Maned Pig".
claims.statement_id: Zhu berarti "babi" dan Bajie berarti "delapan sila". Sebelum direkrut bodhisatwa Guanyin, Zhu Bajie dikenal sebagai Zhu Gāngliè (豬剛巤), secara harfiah "Babi Berbulu Kuduk Kuat".
claims.quote: Zhu means "swine", and Bajie means "eight precepts". Before being recruited by the bodhisattva Guanyin, Zhu Bajie was known as Zhu Gāngliè (豬剛巤), literally "Strong-Maned Pig".

claims.statement: He is portrayed as a fearsome humanoid monster, part human and part pig, who often causes trouble for himself and his companions through laziness, gluttony and lust.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai monster humanoid menakutkan, sebagian manusia dan sebagian babi, yang sering menimbulkan masalah bagi dirinya dan rekan-rekannya karena kemalasan, kerakusan, dan nafsu.
claims.quote: He is portrayed as a fearsome humanoid monster, part human and part pig, who often causes trouble for himself and his companions through laziness, gluttony, and lust.

claims.statement: His Buddhist name "Zhu Wuneng", given by Bodhisattva Guanyin, means "pig (reincarnated) who is aware of ability" or "pig who rises to power".
claims.statement_id: Nama Buddhisnya "Zhu Wuneng", diberikan oleh Bodhisatwa Guanyin, berarti "babi (reinkarnasi) yang sadar akan kemampuan" atau "babi yang naik ke kekuasaan".
claims.quote: His Buddhist name "Zhu Wuneng", given by Bodhisattva Guanyin, means "pig (reincarnated) who is aware of ability" or "pig who rises to power"

claims.statement: Tang Sanzang gave him the nickname Bājiè, meaning "eight restraints" or "eight commandments", to remind him of Buddhist discipline.
claims.statement_id: Tang Sanzang memberinya julukan Bājiè, berarti "delapan pantangan" atau "delapan perintah", untuk mengingatkannya pada disiplin Buddhis.
claims.quote: Tang Sanzang gave him the nickname Bājiè, meaning "eight restraints" or "eight commandments", to remind him of Buddhist discipline.

claims.statement: In the original Chinese novel he is often called dāizi (呆子), meaning "idiot".
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Tiongkok aslinya, ia sering disebut dāizi (呆子), yang berarti "si bodoh".
claims.quote: In the original Chinese novel, he is often called dāizi (呆子), meaning "idiot".

claims.statement: Bodhisattvas and other heavenly beings usually refer to him as Tiānpéng (天蓬), his former title when he was a heavenly marshal known as Marshal Tianpeng.
claims.statement_id: Bodhisatwa dan makhluk surgawi lain biasanya menyebutnya Tiānpéng (天蓬), gelarnya dahulu ketika menjadi marsekal langit bernama Marshal Tianpeng.
claims.quote: Bodhisattvas and other heavenly beings usually refer to him as Tiānpéng (天蓬), his former title when he was a heavenly marshal known as Marshal Tianpeng

claims.statement: Formerly a heavenly marshal and commander of 80,000 celestial sailors, Zhu Bajie is skilled at underwater combat, where he is portrayed as surpassing Sun Wukong.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu marsekal langit dan komandan 80.000 pelaut surgawi, Zhu Bajie mahir bertarung di bawah air, tempat ia digambarkan melampaui Sun Wukong.
claims.quote: Formerly a heavenly marshal and commander of 80,000 celestial sailors, Zhu Bajie is skilled at underwater combat, where he is portrayed as surpassing Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: After his drunken attempt to seduce Chang'e, she reported him to the Jade Emperor, leading to his banishment to Earth.
claims.statement_id: Setelah ia mabuk dan mencoba merayu Chang'e, sang dewi melaporkannya kepada Kaisar Giok, sehingga ia dibuang ke bumi.
claims.quote: After his drunken attempt to seduce her, she reported him to the Jade Emperor, leading to his banishment to Earth.

claims.statement: By mishap he fell into a pig well and was reborn as a man-eating pig-monster known as Zhū Gāngliè.
claims.statement_id: Karena kecelakaan, ia jatuh ke sumur babi dan terlahir kembali sebagai monster babi pemakan manusia bernama Zhū Gāngliè.
claims.quote: By mishap, he fell into a pig well and was reborn as a man-eating pig-monster known as Zhū Gāngliè

claims.statement: He is instead rewarded for his part in the pilgrimage's success with a job as "Cleanser of the Altars" (淨壇使者) and with all the leftovers he can eat.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai ganjaran atas perannya dalam keberhasilan ziarah, ia diberi tugas sebagai "Cleanser of the Altars" (淨壇使者) dan semua sisa makanan yang bisa ia makan.
claims.quote: He is instead rewarded for his part in the pilgrimage's success with a job as "Cleanser of the Altars" ... and with all the leftovers he can eat.

claims.statement: At the end of the novel most of Bajie's fellow pilgrims achieve enlightenment and become arhats, but he does not; although much improved, he remains too attached to his base desires.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir novel, sebagian besar rekan Bajie mencapai pencerahan dan menjadi arhat, tetapi ia tidak; walau sudah jauh membaik, ia masih terlalu terikat pada keinginan rendahnya.
claims.quote: At the end of the novel, most of Bajie's fellow pilgrims achieve enlightenment and become arhats, but he does not; although much improved, he remains too attached to his base desires.

claims.statement: After finishing his own slice he finds the watermelon so delicious that he makes excuses to eat each remaining piece until it is all gone; his large appetite is evident in many parts of the story.
claims.statement_id: Setelah menghabiskan bagiannya, ia menganggap semangka itu begitu lezat sehingga mencari alasan untuk memakan tiap potongan yang tersisa hingga habis; nafsu makannya besar dan tampak di banyak bagian cerita.
claims.quote: After finishing his own slice, he finds the watermelon so delicious that he makes excuses to eat each remaining piece until the whole watermelon is gone. He has a large appetite, which is evident in many parts of the story.

claims.statement: Zhu Bajie is given to laziness; he often neglects the group's troubles and responsibilities, looking for excuses to delay the pilgrimage.
claims.statement_id: Zhu Bajie cenderung malas; ia sering mengabaikan masalah dan tanggung jawab rombongan dan mencari alasan untuk menunda ziarah.
claims.quote: Zhu Bajie is given to laziness. He often neglects the group's troubles and responsibilities, looking for excuses to delay the pilgrimage.

claims.statement: After his reincarnation he is often portrayed as openly lustful when he meets women; his lust often gets the group into trouble and sometimes leads to disaster.
claims.statement_id: Setelah reinkarnasi, ia sering digambarkan terang-terangan berahi saat bertemu perempuan; nafsunya sering menjerumuskan rombongan ke dalam masalah dan kadang bencana.
claims.quote: After his reincarnation, he is often portrayed as openly lustful when he encounters women. His lust often gets the group into trouble and sometimes leads to disaster.

claims.statement: Although Sun Wukong can identify demons, Zhu Bajie often persuades him to release them rather than capture or kill them; his kindness often causes trouble and leads to disaster.
claims.statement_id: Meski Sun Wukong dapat mengenali iblis, Zhu Bajie sering membujuknya melepaskan mereka alih-alih menangkap atau membunuhnya; kebaikan hatinya sering menimbulkan masalah dan bencana.
claims.quote: Although Sun Wukong can identify demons, Zhu Bajie often persuades him to release them rather than capture or kill them; his kindness often causes trouble and leads to disaster.

claims.statement: Zhu Bajie respectfully calls Sun Wukong "brother", even though the two often clash and Sun frequently mocks him.
claims.statement_id: Zhu Bajie dengan hormat memanggil Sun Wukong "kakak", meski keduanya sering bentrok dan Sun sering mengejeknya.
claims.quote: Zhu Bajie respectfully calls Sun Wukong "brother", even though the two often clash and Sun frequently mocks him.

claims.statement: The character's name and pilgrimage origins may derive from Zhu Shixing, a real monk who lived during the late Han dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Nama dan asal-usul ziarah tokoh ini mungkin berasal dari Zhu Shixing, biksu nyata yang hidup pada akhir dinasti Han.
claims.quote: The character's name and pilgrimage origins may derive from Zhu Shixing, a real monk who lived during the late Han dynasty.

claims.statement: Zhu Bajie first appeared as a pig demon in theatrical plays of the Yuan and early Ming dynasties, including works by Yang Jingxian; in these early versions he introduces himself as the "Chariot General" and serves Marici, the Bodhisattva of Light.
claims.statement_id: Zhu Bajie pertama kali muncul sebagai iblis babi dalam drama panggung dinasti Yuan dan awal Ming, termasuk karya Yang Jingxian; dalam versi awal itu ia memperkenalkan diri sebagai "Chariot General" dan melayani Marici, Bodhisatwa Cahaya.
claims.quote: Zhu Bajie first appeared as a pig demon in theatrical plays of the Yuan and early Ming dynasties, including works by Yang Jingxian. In these early versions, the character introduces himself as the "Chariot General" and serves Marici, the Bodhisattva of Light.

claims.statement: Zhu Bajie's heavenly title, Marshal Tianpeng, comes from ancient Taoist star worship.
claims.statement_id: Gelar surgawi Zhu Bajie, Marshal Tianpeng, berasal dari pemujaan bintang Tao kuno.
claims.quote: Zhu Bajie's heavenly title, Marshal Tianpeng, comes from ancient Taoist star worship.

claims.statement: In modern times Zhu Bajie is seen as a patron deity of masseuses, hostesses and prostitutes in Taiwan and other parts of East Asia.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa modern, Zhu Bajie dipandang sebagai dewa pelindung pemijat, pramuria, dan pekerja seks di Taiwan dan bagian lain Asia Timur.
claims.quote: In modern times, Zhu Bajie is seen as a patron deity of masseuses, hostesses, and prostitutes in Taiwan and other parts of East Asia.

claims.statement: In the introduction to his 1913 translation Timothy Richard writes that the Pig personates irrepressible instincts, and that he has no sense and is too fond of ease, good feeding and pleasure.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahannya tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menulis bahwa si Babi melambangkan naluri yang tak terkendali, dan bahwa ia tak punya akal sehat serta terlalu gemar bersantai, makan enak, dan kesenangan.
claims.quote: The Pig, who personates irrepressible instincts ... But he has no sense, is too fond of ease, good feeding and pleasure

claims.statement: In Richard's 1913 translation the demon Chu says that, getting drunk, he made love to some of the fairies and was expelled to Fu Ling Shan through some mistake in transmigration.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913) si iblis Chu bercerita bahwa ia mabuk, merayu beberapa peri, lalu diusir ke Fu Ling Shan akibat kesalahan dalam perpindahan jiwa.
claims.quote: But getting drunk, I made love to some of the fairies, and was expelled to Fu Ling Shan, but by some mistake in transmigration

claims.statement: In Richard's 1913 translation the Master gives the demon a new name, Pa Kiel (eight commandments).
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913), Sang Guru memberi si iblis nama baru Pa Kiel (delapan perintah).
claims.quote: But I will also give you a new name Pa Kiel (eight commandments).

claims.statement: In chapter 8 the creature says he was once Marshal Tianpeng of the Heavenly River; for flirting with Chang'e while drunk the Jade Emperor had him struck two thousand blows with a hammer and cast down to the mortal world, where he took the wrong road and entered a sow's womb, taking this form.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 8, si monster mengaku dahulu Marsekal Tianpeng dari Sungai Langit; karena mabuk dan menggoda Chang'e ia dihukum Kaisar Giok dengan dua ribu pukulan palu, dibuang ke dunia, dan salah masuk ke rahim babi betina sehingga berwujud demikian.
claims.quote: 我本是天河裡天蓬元帥。只因帶酒戲弄嫦娥，玉帝把我打了二千鎚，貶下塵凡。一靈真性，徑來奪舍投胎，不期錯了道路，投在個母豬胎裡，變得這般模樣。

claims.statement: He says he bit the sow to death, killed the herd of pigs, took over the mountain ground and lived by eating people, and then begs the bodhisattva for rescue.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengaku menggigit mati babi betina, membunuh kawanan babi, merebut wilayah gunung itu, dan hidup dengan memakan manusia, lalu memohon pertolongan Guanyin.
claims.quote: 是我咬殺母豬，打死群彘，在此處占了山場，吃人度日。不期撞著菩薩，萬望拔救拔救。

claims.statement: He names the mountain Fuling (福陵山), with a cave called Yunzhan (雲棧洞) in it; in that cave there had been a Luan Erjie (卵二姐) who, seeing he had some martial skill, took him on as head of the household.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyebut gunung itu Fuling (福陵山), dengan sebuah gua bernama Yunzhan (雲棧洞) di dalamnya; di gua itu dahulu ada Luan Erjie (卵二姐) yang, melihat ia punya kepandaian bela diri, mengangkatnya sebagai kepala keluarga.
claims.quote: 叫做福陵山。山中有一洞，叫做雲棧洞。洞裡原有個卵二姐，他見我有些武藝，招我做了家長，又喚做倒蹅門。

claims.statement: The bodhisattva ordains him, gives him the surname "豬" (pig) from his body and the dharma name "豬悟能"; he then keeps a vegetarian fast, giving up the five pungent foods and three abstentions, to wait for the scripture seeker.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin menahbiskannya, memberinya marga "豬" (babi) dari tubuhnya dan nama dharma "豬悟能"; ia lalu berpuasa, menjauhi lima sayuran berbau dan tiga pantangan, menunggu orang yang akan mengambil sutra.
claims.quote: 菩薩才與他摩頂受戒，指身為姓，就姓了豬；替他起了法名，就叫做豬悟能。遂此領命歸真，持齋把素，斷絕了五葷三厭，專候那取經人。

claims.statement: In chapter 18 old Gao describes his son-in-law: at first a dark, stout man, then a dull fellow with a long snout and big ears, a mane behind his head and a pig-like head and face, who eats three to five dou of rice at one meal.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 18, Tuan Gao menggambarkan menantunya: mula-mula pria gemuk berkulit gelap, lalu berubah menjadi si dungu bermoncong panjang, bertelinga besar, berbulu kuduk di belakang kepala, dan berkepala seperti babi, yang sekali makan menghabiskan tiga hingga lima dou nasi.
claims.quote: 初來時是一條黑胖漢，後來就變做一個長嘴大耳朵的獃子，腦後又有一溜鬃毛，身體粗糙怕人，頭臉就像個豬的模樣。食腸卻又甚大：一頓要吃三五斗米飯，早間點心也得百十個燒餅才夠。

claims.statement: Old Gao says he can now stir up wind, bring clouds and mist, and make stones and sand fly, so that the family and neighbours cannot live in peace.
claims.statement_id: Tuan Gao menyebut kini ia dapat mengendalikan angin, mendatangkan awan dan kabut, serta menerbangkan batu dan pasir, sehingga keluarga dan tetangga tidak tenang.
claims.quote: 他如今又會弄風，雲來霧去，走石飛砂，諕得我一家並左鄰右舍，俱不得安生。

claims.statement: In chapter 19 the creature gathers red light, shows his true form, rushes into his cave and brings out a nine-toothed rake (九齒釘鈀) to fight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 19, si monster memusatkan cahaya merah, menampakkan wujud aslinya, menerobos masuk gua, dan membawa keluar sebuah garu bergigi sembilan (九齒釘鈀) untuk bertarung.
claims.quote: 正行處，忽見一座高山，那怪把紅光結聚，現了本相，撞入洞內，取出一柄九齒釘鈀來戰。

claims.statement: Tang Sanzang says that since he keeps away from the five pungent foods and three abstentions he will be given another name, "八戒" (Bajie); hence he is also called 豬八戒.
claims.statement_id: Tang Sanzang berkata bahwa karena ia menjauhi lima sayuran berbau dan tiga pantangan, ia diberi nama lain "八戒"; sejak itu ia juga disebut 豬八戒.
claims.quote: 三藏道：「不可，不可。你既是不吃五葷三厭，我再與你起個別名，喚為八戒。」那獃子歡歡喜喜道：「謹遵師命。」因此又叫做豬八戒。

claims.statement: Sun Wukong reports that the creature is really Marshal Tianpeng come down to the mortal world, who took the wrong birth and has a wild boar's face while his inner nature remains; he says he takes his surname from his looks and is named 豬剛鬣.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong melaporkan bahwa monster itu aslinya Marsekal Tianpeng yang turun ke dunia, salah menjelma sehingga wajahnya seperti babi hutan namun akal batinnya tetap ada; ia mengaku bermarga dari rupanya dan bernama 豬剛鬣.
claims.quote: 他本是天蓬元帥臨凡，只因錯投了胎，嘴臉像一個野豬模樣，其實性靈尚存。他說以相為姓，喚名豬剛鬣。

claims.statement: Sun Wukong reports to Guanyin that Wuneng (Zhu Bajie) fought the river monster three times on the water without winning, so the party was blocked from crossing.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong melapor kepada Guanyin bahwa Wuneng (Zhu Bajie) sudah bertarung tiga kali melawan monster sungai di permukaan air tanpa menang, sehingga rombongan terhalang menyeberang.
claims.quote: 甚虧了悟能與他水面上大戰三次，只是不能取勝，被他攔阻，不能渡河。

claims.statement: In chapter 23, hearing of such wealth and beauty, Bajie cannot restrain himself and squirms in his chair as if pricked by a needle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 23, mendengar kekayaan dan kecantikan itu, Bajie tak tahan; ia duduk gelisah seperti ditusuk jarum.
claims.quote: 那八戒聞得這般富貴，這般美色，他卻心癢難撓；坐在那椅子上，一似針戳屁股，左扭右扭的，忍耐不住。

claims.statement: At the end of the novel the Buddha says Zhu Wuneng was once the water god of the Heavenly River, Marshal Tianpeng, cast down for drunken misconduct with an immortal maiden; for his merit in carrying the baggage he is raised to the rank of Altar Cleanser (淨壇使者).
claims.statement_id: Di akhir novel, Buddha berkata bahwa Zhu Wuneng dahulu dewa air Sungai Langit, Marsekal Tianpeng, dibuang karena mabuk dan menggoda dewi; karena jasanya memikul beban, ia dinaikkan menjadi Pembersih Altar (淨壇使者).
claims.quote: 豬悟能，汝本天河水神天蓬元帥，為汝蟠桃會上酗酒戲了仙娥，貶汝下界投胎，身如畜類。幸汝記愛人身，在福陵山雲棧洞造孽，喜歸大教，入我沙門，保聖僧在路，卻又有頑心，色情未泯。因汝挑擔有功，加陞汝職正果，做淨壇使者。

claims.statement: Bajie protests that he is made only an Altar Cleanser while the others become buddhas; the Buddha answers that he has a big mouth, a lazy body and a wide appetite.
claims.statement_id: Bajie protes mengapa ia hanya menjadi Pembersih Altar sementara yang lain menjadi buddha; Buddha menjawab bahwa ia bermulut besar, bertubuh malas, dan berperut lebar.
claims.quote: 八戒口中嚷道：「他們都成佛，如何把我做個淨壇使者？」如來道：「因汝口壯身慵，食腸寬大。

claims.statement: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the West (Xiyouji) adalah novel Tiongkok yang terbit pada abad ke-16 pada masa dinasti Ming dan dikaitkan dengan Wu Cheng'en.
claims.quote: is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.

claims.statement: Sha Wujing was once a celestial Curtain Lifting General who stood in attendance by the imperial chariot in the Hall of Miraculous Mist.
claims.statement_id: Sha Wujing dahulu adalah Jenderal Pengangkat Tirai (Curtain Lifting General) di langit, yang berjaga di samping kereta kaisar di Aula Kabut Ajaib.
claims.quote: was once a celestial Curtain Lifting General, who stood in attendance by the imperial chariot in the Hall of Miraculous Mist.

claims.statement: The now-hideous immortal took up residence in the Flowing Sands River, terrorizing surrounding villages and travelers trying to cross it.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk abadi yang kini buruk rupa itu menetap di Sungai Pasir Mengalir (Flowing Sands River), meneror desa sekitar dan para pelancong yang mencoba menyeberang.
claims.quote: The now-hideous immortal took up residence in the Flowing Sands River, terrorizing surrounding villages and travelers trying to cross the river.

claims.statement: He is the most obedient, logical and polite of the three disciples, and always takes care of his master.
claims.statement_id: Ia murid paling patuh, logis, dan sopan di antara ketiga murid, dan selalu merawat gurunya.
claims.quote: He is the most obedient, logical, and polite of the three disciples, and always takes care of his master

claims.statement: At the end of the journey he becomes an arhat, a higher level of exaltation than Zhu Bajie, who is relegated to cleaning altars.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir perjalanan ia menjadi arhat, tingkat kemuliaan yang lebih tinggi daripada Zhu Bajie yang ditugaskan membersihkan altar.
claims.quote: He eventually becomes an arhat at the end of the journey, giving him a higher level of exaltation than Zhu Bajie, who is relegated to cleaning altars

claims.statement: He also knows 18 transformation methods and is highly effective in water combat.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga menguasai 18 cara perubahan wujud dan sangat efektif dalam pertempuran di air.
claims.quote: He also knows 18 transformation methods and is highly effective in water combat.

claims.statement: Sha Wujing is one of the three disciples of the Buddhist pilgrim Tang Sanzang in the 16th-century novel Journey to the West written by Wu Cheng'en in the Ming dynasty, although versions of his character predate the Ming novel.
claims.statement_id: Sha Wujing adalah salah satu dari tiga murid peziarah Buddha Tang Sanzang dalam novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West karya Wu Cheng'en pada masa dinasti Ming, meski versi tokohnya sudah ada sebelum novel Ming.
claims.quote: is one of the three disciples of the Buddhist pilgrim Tang Sanzang in the 16th-century novel Journey to the West written by Wu Cheng'en in the Ming dynasty, although versions of his character predate the Ming novel.

claims.statement: In the source novel his background is the least developed of the pilgrims and he contributes the least to their efforts; in the original Chinese story he is a man-eating monster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel sumbernya, latar belakangnya paling kurang dikembangkan di antara para peziarah dan sumbangannya paling sedikit; dalam kisah Tiongkok aslinya ia adalah monster pemakan manusia.
claims.quote: In the source novel, his background is the least developed of the pilgrims, and he contributes the least to their efforts. In the original Chinese story, he is a man-eating monster.

claims.statement: In many Japanese versions Sha Wujing is depicted as a Kappa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak versi Jepang, Sha Wujing digambarkan sebagai kappa.
claims.quote: In many Japanese versions, Sha Wujing is depicted as a Kappa.

claims.statement: His Buddhist Dharma name "Sha Wujing", given to him by the bodhisattva Guanyin, means "sand aware of purity".
claims.statement_id: Nama Dharma Buddhisnya, "Sha Wujing", yang diberikan bodhisatwa Guanyin, berarti "pasir yang sadar akan kemurnian".
claims.quote: His Buddhist Dharma name, "Sha Wujing", given to him by the bodhisattva Guanyin, means "sand aware of purity".

claims.statement: The names "Monk Sha" and Sha Heshang both basically translate as "Sand Monk" or "Sand Priest".
claims.statement_id: Sebutan "Monk Sha" dan Sha Heshang pada dasarnya berarti "Biksu Pasir" atau "Pendeta Pasir".
claims.quote: both basically translating as "Sand Monk" or "Sand Priest".

claims.statement: His fall from grace happens when he breaks a valuable jade or crystal vase or goblet during a Heavenly Peach Festival; some sources say he did it in a fit of rage, others that it was an unintentional accident.
claims.statement_id: Kejatuhannya terjadi saat ia memecahkan vas atau cawan giok atau kristal berharga pada Festival Persik Surgawi; sebagian sumber menyebut ia melakukannya dalam kemarahan, sumber lain menyebut tanpa sengaja.
claims.quote: His fall from grace happens when he broke a valuable Jade or Crystal vase or goblet, during a Heavenly Peach Festival; some sources say that he had done this in a fit of rage while other sources say that he had done this unintentionally, and it was an accident.

claims.statement: The Jade Emperor had him struck 800 times with a rod and exiled to earth, where he was to be reincarnated as a terrible man-eating monster.
claims.statement_id: Kaisar Giok menghukumnya dengan 800 pukulan tongkat dan membuangnya ke bumi untuk terlahir kembali sebagai monster pemakan manusia yang mengerikan.
claims.quote: he was punished by the Jade Emperor, who had him struck 800 times with a rod and exiled to earth, where he was to be reincarnated as a terrible man-eating monster.

claims.statement: Each day seven flying swords sent from Heaven would stab him in the chest and then return; he had to live in the river full-time to avoid the punishment.
claims.statement_id: Setiap hari tujuh pedang terbang dari langit menusuk dadanya lalu kembali; ia harus tinggal di sungai sepanjang waktu untuk menghindari hukuman itu.
claims.quote: Each day, seven flying swords sent from Heaven would stab him in the chest and then return. He had to live in the river full-time to avoid the punishment.

claims.statement: Wujing's appearance was grisly: he had a red beard, sometimes blue skin, and was partially bald.
claims.statement_id: Penampilan Wujing mengerikan: berjanggut merah, kadang berkulit biru, dan sebagian botak.
claims.quote: Wujing's appearance was grisly. He had a red beard and sometimes had blue skin, and he was partially bald.

claims.statement: Like Sun Wukong's Ruyi Jingu Bang, Wujing's Xiangyaobaozhang can grow, shrink, lengthen and shorten at will.
claims.statement_id: Seperti Ruyi Jingu Bang milik Sun Wukong, Xiangyaobaozhang milik Wujing dapat membesar, mengecil, memanjang, dan memendek sesuka hati.
claims.quote: Like Sun Wukong's Ruyi Jingu Bang, Wujing's Xiangyaobaozhang is capable of growing, shrinking, lengthening and shortening at will.

claims.statement: During the Journey to the West his swimming ability was useful.
claims.statement_id: Selama Journey to the West, kemampuannya berenang berguna.
claims.quote: During the Journey to the West, his swimming ability was useful.

claims.statement: Wujing was a kind-hearted, obedient person loyal to his master and, compared with his fellow disciples, serves as a "Straight man" character.
claims.statement_id: Wujing orang yang baik hati, patuh, dan setia kepada gurunya; dibandingkan sesama murid, ia berperan sebagai tokoh "Straight man".
claims.quote: Wujing was a kind-hearted and obedient person and loyal to his master, and, compared to his fellow disciples, Wujing serves as a 'Straight man' character.

claims.statement: At the journey's end the Buddha transformed him into an arhat known as the Golden-bodied Arhat.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir perjalanan, Buddha mengubahnya menjadi arhat yang dikenal sebagai Arhat Bertubuh Emas (Golden-bodied Arhat).
claims.quote: At the journey's end, Buddha transformed him into an arhat known as the Golden-bodied Arhat

claims.statement: He knows only 18 forms of transformation (one quarter of the full 72 that Wukong knows and one half of Bajie's 36).
claims.statement_id: Ia hanya menguasai 18 bentuk perubahan wujud (seperempat dari 72 milik Wukong dan setengah dari 36 milik Bajie).
claims.quote: He knows only 18 forms of transformation (one-quarter of the full 72 that Wukong knows, and one-half of Bajie's 36)

claims.statement: The complete version of Journey to the West anonymously published in 1592 borrowed liberally from tales concerning Shensha shen.
claims.statement_id: Versi lengkap Journey to the West yang terbit anonim pada 1592 banyak meminjam dari kisah tentang Shensha shen.
claims.quote: As can be seen, the complete version of Journey to the West anonymously published in 1592 borrowed liberally from tales concerning Shensha shen.

claims.statement: His home, the "Flowing Sands River" (流沙河), is derived from the "Flowing Sands" desert inhabited by Shensha shen.
claims.statement_id: Tempat tinggalnya, "Sungai Pasir Mengalir" (流沙河), berasal dari gurun "Pasir Mengalir" yang dihuni Shensha shen.
claims.quote: is derived from the "Flowing Sands" desert inhabited by Shensha shen.

claims.statement: In the introduction to his 1913 translation Timothy Richard calls Sa Wu Ching the Seeker after Purity, a sort of dandy Dolphin or strict Pharisee who gains Heaven by Taoist methods.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pengantar terjemahannya tahun 1913, Timothy Richard menyebut Sa Wu Ching sebagai Pencari Kemurnian, semacam "dandy Dolphin" atau orang Farisi yang ketat, yang meraih surga lewat metode Tao.
claims.quote: Sa Wu Ching. The Seeker after Purity, a sort of dandy Dolphin or strict Pharisee, who gains Heaven by Taoist methods

claims.statement: In Richard's 1913 translation he is called Sa Wu Tsing, or Seeker after Purity, and also Sa Seng (the monk Sand).
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913), ia dipanggil Sa Wu Tsing, atau Pencari Kemurnian, dan juga Sa Seng (biksu Pasir).
claims.quote: and he was called Sa Wu Tsing, or Seeker after Purity. He was also called Sa Seng, (the monk Sand).

claims.statement: In Richard's 1913 translation the demon tells how, when the Queen of Heaven held her peach banquet, some crystals broke by mischance and he was sentenced to death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Richard (1913) sang iblis mengisahkan bahwa ketika Ratu Surga mengadakan jamuan persik, beberapa kristal pecah secara tak sengaja dan ia dijatuhi hukuman mati.
claims.quote: But when the Queen of Heaven Ordered her peach banquet. By mischance some crystals broke, And I was sentenced to death,

claims.statement: In chapter 8 the monster from the river is described with a gloomy face neither blue nor black, bare feet, eyes flashing like two stove lamps, tusks jutting like sword blades and tangled red hair, roaring like thunder.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 8, monster dari sungai digambarkan berwajah suram tidak biru dan tidak hitam, berkaki telanjang, bermata berkilau seperti dua pelita tungku, bertaring mencuat seperti bilah pedang, berambut merah kusut, dan menggelegar seperti guntur.
claims.quote: 青不青，黑不黑，晦氣色臉；長不長，短不短，赤腳筋軀。眼光閃爍，好似灶底雙燈；口角丫叉，就如屠家火缽。獠牙撐劍刃，紅髮亂蓬鬆。一聲叱咤如雷吼，兩腳奔波似滾風。

claims.statement: The monster says he is no evil demon but the Curtain-Lifting General who attended the imperial carriage at the Lingxiao Hall; for accidentally breaking a glass cup at the peach banquet he was struck eight hundred times and cast to earth, and every seven days flying swords pierce his flanks over a hundred times.
claims.statement_id: Si monster mengaku bukan siluman jahat melainkan Jenderal Pengangkat Tirai yang melayani kereta kaisar di Aula Lingxiao; karena tak sengaja memecahkan cawan kaca pada jamuan persik ia dipukul delapan ratus kali dan dibuang ke bumi, serta tiap tujuh hari pedang terbang menusuk dadanya seratus kali lebih.
claims.quote: 我不是妖邪，我是靈霄殿下侍鑾輿的捲簾大將。只因在蟠桃會上失手打碎了玻璃盞，玉帝把我打了八百，貶下界來，變得這般模樣。又叫七日一次，將飛劍來穿我胸脅百餘下方回。

claims.statement: He admits to having eaten many people, including earlier scripture seekers; their heads sank in the flowing sands except nine skulls that floated, which he strung together on a cord to play with.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengaku telah memakan banyak orang, termasuk para pengambil sutra sebelumnya; kepala mereka tenggelam di pasir mengalir, kecuali sembilan tengkorak yang mengapung, yang ia rangkai dengan tali untuk bermain.
claims.quote: 凡吃的人頭，拋落流沙，竟沉水底。這個水，鵝毛也不能浮。惟有九個取經人的骷髏浮在水面，再不能沉。我以為異物，將索兒穿在一處，閑時拿來頑耍。

claims.statement: The bodhisattva ordains him, gives him the surname "沙" (sand) and the dharma name "沙悟淨"; he then cleanses his mind, no longer takes life, and waits for the scripture seeker.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin menahbiskannya, memberinya marga "沙" (pasir) dan nama dharma "沙悟淨"; ia lalu membersihkan batinnya, tidak lagi membunuh, dan menunggu pengambil sutra.
claims.quote: 菩薩方與他摩頂受戒，指沙為姓，就姓了沙；起個法名，叫做個沙悟淨。當時入了沙門，送菩薩過了河，他洗心滌慮，再不傷生，專等取經人。

claims.statement: The bodhisattva and her attendant reach the region of the Flowing Sands River (流沙河), three thousand li of weak water, and judge that a scripture seeker of mortal flesh would find it hard to cross.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin dan muridnya tiba di wilayah Sungai Pasir Mengalir (流沙河), air lemah tiga ribu li, dan menilai bahwa pengambil sutra yang bertubuh fana sulit menyeberanginya.
claims.quote: 忽然見弱水三千，乃是流沙河界。菩薩道：「徒弟呀，此處卻是難行。取經人濁骨凡胎，如何得渡？」

claims.statement: In chapter 22 the bodhisattva says the Flowing Sands River monster is the Curtain-Lifting General come down to the mortal world, a believer she has persuaded to protect scripture seekers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bab 22, Guanyin berkata bahwa monster Sungai Pasir Mengalir adalah Jenderal Pengangkat Tirai yang turun ke dunia, penganut yang telah ia bujuk untuk melindungi para pengambil sutra.
claims.quote: 那流沙河的妖怪，乃是捲簾大將臨凡，也是我勸化的善信，教他保護取經之輩。

claims.statement: The bodhisattva tells Muzha to take the red gourd with Sun Wukong to the river surface and simply call "悟淨" so that he comes out.
claims.statement_id: Guanyin menyuruh Muzha membawa labu merah bersama Sun Wukong ke permukaan sungai dan cukup memanggil "悟淨" agar ia keluar.
claims.quote: 你可將此葫蘆，同孫悟空到流沙河水面上，只叫『悟淨』，他就出來了。

claims.statement: Wujing says the bodhisattva took sand as his surname and gave him the dharma name Sha Wujing; Tang Sanzang, seeing his bearing as a true monk, also calls him 沙和尚 (Sha Heshang).
claims.statement_id: Wujing berkata bahwa Guanyin telah menunjuk pasir sebagai marganya dan memberinya nama dharma Sha Wujing; Tang Sanzang melihat sikapnya seperti biksu sejati dan memanggilnya 沙和尚.
claims.quote: 悟淨道：「弟子向蒙菩薩教化，指沙為姓，與我起個法名，喚做沙悟淨，豈有不從師父之理？」三藏道：「既如此，」叫：「悟空，取戒刀來，與他落了髮。」大聖依言，即將戒刀與他剃了頭。又來拜了三藏，拜了行者與八戒，分了大小。三藏見他行禮真像個和尚家風，故又叫他做沙和尚。

claims.statement: Wujing takes the skulls from his neck, strings them into the nine palaces with the bodhisattva's gourd set in the middle as a dharma boat; the elder boards it and it proves steady as a light skiff.
claims.statement_id: Wujing melepas tengkorak dari lehernya, merangkainya dengan tali menjadi sembilan palas, dan menaruh labu Guanyin di tengah sebagai perahu pusaka; Tang Sanzang naik dan perahu itu setenang sampan ringan.
claims.quote: 那悟淨不敢怠慢，即將頸項下掛的骷髏取下，用索子結作九宮，把菩薩葫蘆安在當中，請師父下岸。那長老遂登法船，坐於上面，果然穩似輕舟。

claims.statement: Sun Wukong reports that Wuneng (Zhu Bajie) fought the river monster three times on the water without winning, so the party could not cross.
claims.statement_id: Sun Wukong melapor bahwa Wuneng (Zhu Bajie) bertarung tiga kali melawan monster sungai itu di permukaan air tanpa menang, sehingga rombongan tidak dapat menyeberang.
claims.quote: 甚虧了悟能與他水面上大戰三次，只是不能取勝，被他攔阻，不能渡河。

claims.statement: At the end of the novel the Buddha says Sha Wujing was once the Curtain-Lifting General who smashed a glass cup at the peach banquet, fell into the Flowing Sands River and ate people; for protecting the holy monk and leading the horse he is raised to the golden-bodied arhat (金身羅漢).
claims.statement_id: Di akhir novel Buddha berkata bahwa Sha Wujing dahulu Jenderal Pengangkat Tirai yang memecahkan cawan kaca pada jamuan persik, jatuh ke Sungai Pasir Mengalir dan memakan manusia; karena jasanya menjaga biksu dan menuntun kuda ia dinaikkan menjadi arhat bertubuh emas (金身羅漢).
claims.quote: 沙悟淨，汝本是捲簾大將。先因蟠桃會上打碎玻璃盞，貶汝下界，汝落於流沙河，傷生吃人造孽。幸皈吾教，誠敬迦持，保護聖僧，登山牽馬有功，加陞大職正果，為金身羅漢。

claims.quote: is a Chinese novel published in the 16th century during the Ming dynasty and attributed to Wu Cheng'en.

claims.statement: The White Dragon Horse is a major character in the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West; he serves as Tang Sanzang's steed during the pilgrimage. He is also known as Ao Lie.
claims.statement_id: White Dragon Horse adalah tokoh utama novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West; ia menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang selama ziarah. Ia juga dikenal sebagai Ao Lie.
claims.quote: is a major character in the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West. He serves as Tang Sanzang's steed during the pilgrimage ... He is also known as Ao Lie.

claims.statement: In Chinese the White Dragon Horse is known as Bai Longma (白龍馬).
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Tionghoa, White Dragon Horse dikenal sebagai Bai Longma (白龍馬).
claims.quote: The White Dragon Horse, known in Chinese as Bai Longma (Chinese: 白龍馬

claims.statement: In Journey to the West Bai Longma is a dragon prince, the third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea; he once accidentally set fire to a pearl given as a gift by the Jade Emperor.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Journey to the West, Bai Longma adalah pangeran naga, putra ketiga Raja Naga Laut Barat; ia pernah tak sengaja membakar mutiara yang dihadiahkan Kaisar Giok.
claims.quote: In Journey to the West, Bai Longma is a dragon prince and the third son of the Dragon King of the West Sea. He once accidentally set fire to a pearl that had been given as a gift by the Jade Emperor.

claims.statement: The dragon prince was spared and banished to Yingchou Stream (鷹愁澗) in Shepan Mountain (蛇盤山), where he was told to wait for the monk whom Guanyin would send on a pilgrimage to the Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Sang pangeran naga diampuni dan dibuang ke Sungai Yingchou (鷹愁澗) di Gunung Shepan (蛇盤山), tempat ia diperintahkan menunggu biksu yang akan dikirim Guanyin berziarah menemui Buddha.
claims.quote: The dragon prince was spared and banished to Yingchou Stream (鷹愁澗) in Shepan Mountain (蛇盤山), where he was instructed to wait for the monk whom Guanyin would send on a pilgrimage to the Buddha.

claims.statement: When Tang Sanzang crosses the stream the prince appears as a gigantic white dragon and swallows Tang's white horse; he fights Sun Wukong but is defeated and retreats underwater.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Tang Sanzang menyeberangi sungai itu, sang pangeran muncul sebagai naga putih raksasa dan menelan kuda putih Tang; ia melawan Sun Wukong, kalah, dan mundur ke bawah air.
claims.quote: When Tang Sanzang crosses the stream, the prince appears as a gigantic white dragon and swallows Tang's white horse. He fights Sun Wukong but is defeated and retreats underwater.

claims.statement: He is then transformed into the White Dragon Horse and serves as Tang Sanzang's steed for the rest of the journey; compared with some of the other pilgrims he is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and occasionally returns to dragon form to fight when the group is in danger.
claims.statement_id: Ia kemudian diubah menjadi White Dragon Horse dan menjadi tunggangan Tang Sanzang sepanjang sisa perjalanan; dibandingkan beberapa peziarah lain ia sering digambarkan pendiam dan cerdas, dan sesekali kembali ke wujud naga untuk bertarung saat rombongan terancam.
claims.quote: He is then transformed into the White Dragon Horse and serves as Tang Sanzang's steed for the rest of the journey. Compared with some of the other pilgrims, he is often depicted as quiet and intelligent, and he occasionally returns to dragon form to fight when the group is in danger.

claims.statement: When Tang Sanzang is captured by the Yellow Robe Demon, the White Dragon Horse transforms into a young man and tries to rescue him, but fails.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Tang Sanzang ditawan Iblis Jubah Kuning, White Dragon Horse berubah menjadi pemuda dan mencoba menyelamatkannya, tetapi gagal.
claims.quote: the White Dragon Horse transforms into a young man and attempts to rescue him, but fails.

claims.statement: At the end of the novel he resumes his white dragon form and coils around one of the pillars in the Great Leiyin Temple.
claims.statement_id: Di akhir novel ia kembali ke wujud naga putih dan melingkari salah satu tiang di Kuil Leiyin Agung.

claims.quote: 他曾在火燄山修行了三百年，煉成三昧真火，卻也神通廣大，牛魔王使他來鎮守號山。

claims.statement: In the novel, as the travelers cross the mountain, a red cloud rises from the hollow into the sky and gathers into a mass of fire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, saat para peziarah melewati gunung itu, awan merah naik dari lembah hingga ke langit dan menggumpal menjadi hawa api.
claims.quote: 師徒們正當悚懼，又只見那山凹裡有一朵紅雲，直冒到九霄空內，結聚了一團火氣。

claims.statement: In the novel, the being in the red light is a yaojing (妖精, demon). He has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐僧), traveling west to fetch scriptures, is the reincarnation of Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live long.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, makhluk di dalam cahaya merah itu adalah seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman). Ia mendengar bahwa Tang Sanzang (唐僧), yang bepergian ke Barat untuk mengambil kitab, adalah reinkarnasi Jinchan Zhanglao (金蟬長老), dan bahwa orang yang memakan sepotong dagingnya akan hidup panjang.
claims.quote: 卻說紅光裡，真是個妖精。他數年前聞得人講：東土唐僧往西天取經，乃是金蟬長老轉生，十世修行的好人，有人吃他一塊肉，延生長壽，與天地同休。

claims.statement: In the novel, Red Boy transforms (搖身一變) into a seven-year-old child, naked, hands and feet bound with hemp rope and hung from the top of a pine tree, shouting for help.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Red Boy berubah wujud (搖身一變) menjadi anak berusia tujuh tahun yang telanjang, tangan dan kakinya diikat tali rami dan digantung di pucuk pohon pinus sambil berteriak minta tolong.
claims.quote: 好妖怪，即散紅光，按雲頭落下。去那山坡裡，搖身一變，變作七歲頑童，赤條條的身上無衣，將麻繩綑了手足，高吊在那松樹梢頭，口口聲聲只叫：「救人，救人！」

claims.statement: In the novel, Red Boy comes out to fight with a fire-tipped spear (火尖槍) eighteen chi long, wearing no armor, only an embroidered war skirt, and barefoot.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Red Boy keluar bertarung membawa tombak ujung api (火尖槍) sepanjang satu zhang delapan chi, tanpa baju zirah, hanya mengenakan rok perang bersulam dan bertelanjang kaki.
claims.quote: 有那一夥管兵器的小妖，著兩個擡出一桿丈八長的火尖槍，遞與妖王。妖王掄槍拽步，也無甚麼盔甲，只是腰間束一條錦繡戰裙，赤著腳，走出門前。

claims.statement: In the novel, Red Boy's cave lies on Mount Hao (號山), at the Withered Pine Ravine (枯松澗), and is named Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, gua tempat tinggal Red Boy berada di Gunung Hao (號山), di Lembah Pinus Kering (枯松澗), dan bernama Huoyun Dong (火雲洞).
claims.quote: 將近行到門前，見有一座石碣，上鐫八個大字，乃是「號山枯松澗火雲洞」。

claims.statement: In the novel, the rain sent by the Dragon King (龍王) can only put out ordinary fire, not the demon's sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火); it only makes the fire burn the fiercer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, hujan yang dikirim Dragon King (龍王) hanya bisa memadamkan api biasa, bukan sanmei zhenhuo (三昧真火) milik siluman itu; hujan justru membuat api makin membara.
claims.quote: 原來龍王私雨，只好潑得凡火，妖精的三昧真火如何潑得？好一似火上澆油，越潑越灼。

claims.statement: In the novel, Red Boy himself says that he disguised himself as Guanyin (觀音) to lure Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), who now hangs in a bag.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Red Boy sendiri mengatakan bahwa ia menyamar sebagai Guanyin (觀音) untuk memancing Zhu Bajie (豬八戒), yang kini tergantung di dalam kantong.
claims.quote: 是我假變觀音，把豬八戒賺來，見吊在如意袋中，也要蒸他與眾小的們吃哩。

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong gladly invites Guanyin (觀音) out of the Chaoyin cave (潮音仙洞); the gods line up on the Putuo rock (普陀巖), and the Bodhisattva (菩薩) says to him, "Wukong, cross the sea."
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong dengan gembira mengundang Guanyin (觀音) keluar dari gua Chaoyin (潮音仙洞); para dewa berjajar di batu karang Putuo (普陀巖), dan sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) berkata kepadanya, "Wukong, seberangi laut."
claims.quote: 孫大聖十分歡喜，請觀音出了潮音仙洞。諸天大神都列在普陀巖上。菩薩道：「悟空，過海。」

claims.statement: In the novel, after Red Boy begs for mercy, the Bodhisattva (菩薩) shaves his head with a golden razor into a "Mount Tai pressing down" (太山壓頂) style, leaving three tufts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, setelah Red Boy memohon ampun, sang Bodhisattva (菩薩) mencukur kepalanya dengan pisau emas hingga berbentuk "太山壓頂" dan menyisakan tiga jambul.
claims.quote: 菩薩道：「既如此，我與你摩頂受戒。」就袖中取出一把金剃頭刀兒，近前去，把那怪分頂剃了幾刀，剃作一個太山壓頂，與他留下三個頂搭，挽起三個窩角揪兒。

claims.statement: In the novel, the Bodhisattva names him Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) after he accepts the precepts; Red Boy nods and accepts, hoping to be spared.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva menyebutnya Shancai Tongzi (善財童子) setelah ia menerima ajaran; Red Boy mengangguk menerimanya dengan harapan diampuni.
claims.quote: 菩薩道：「你今既受我戒，我卻也不慢你，稱你做善財童子，如何？」那妖點頭受持，只望饒命。

claims.statement: In the novel, the Bodhisattva takes out a golden band (金箍兒), one of three bands given by the Buddha, and, finding Red Boy disrespectful, decides to give it to him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva mengeluarkan sebuah gelang emas (金箍兒), satu dari tiga gelang pemberian Buddha, karena Red Boy bersikap kurang ajar, lalu memutuskan memberikannya kepadanya.
claims.quote: 卻又袖中取出一個金箍兒來道：「這寶貝原是我佛如來賜我往東土尋取經人的金、緊、禁三個箍兒。緊箍兒先與你戴了；禁箍兒收了守山大神；這個金箍兒未曾捨得與人，今觀此怪無禮，與他罷。

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong says he knows the demon's father, the son of Bull Demon King (牛魔王), so by relation he is his uncle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong berkata bahwa ia mengenal ayah siluman itu, putra Bull Demon King (牛魔王), sehingga secara kekerabatan ia adalah pamannya.
claims.quote: 這妖精是牛魔王的兒子，我與他父親相識，若論將起來，還是他老叔哩，他怎敢害我師父？

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in certain regional folk religions Red Boy is venerated as a deity; a cavern in Meishan, Sichuan Province, houses a statue of him that serves as an object of local worship.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam agama rakyat di beberapa daerah Red Boy dihormati sebagai dewa; sebuah gua di Meishan, Provinsi Sichuan, menyimpan patungnya yang menjadi objek pemujaan setempat.
claims.quote: In certain regional folk religions, Red Boy is venerated as a deity. A cavern in Meishan, Sichuan Province, houses a statue of Red Boy that serves as an object of local worship.

claims.statement: The 2021 film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child features Red Boy as the main character.
claims.statement_id: Film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child tahun 2021 menampilkan Red Boy sebagai tokoh utama.
claims.quote: The 2021 film The Journey to the West: Demon's Child features Red Boy as the main character.
