claims.statement: Princess Iron Fan is a character from the 16th-century Chinese novel Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Princess Iron Fan adalah tokoh dari novel Tiongkok abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat).
claims.quote: is a character from the 16th century Chinese novel Journey to the West.

claims.statement: She is also addressed as Rākṣasī (羅剎女, Luóchànǚ), a female rakshasa.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut Rākṣasī (羅剎女, Luóchànǚ), yaitu raksasi.
claims.quote: She is also addressed as Rākṣasī (羅剎女; Luóchànǚ).

claims.statement: Princess Iron Fan is a beautiful demoness, married to Bull Demon King and mother to Red Boy.
claims.statement_id: Princess Iron Fan adalah iblis perempuan (demoness) yang cantik, istri Bull Demon King dan ibu Red Boy.
claims.quote: Princess Iron Fan is a beautiful demoness, married to the Bull Demon King and mother to the Red Boy.

claims.statement: In the novel, a woodcutter says that the one who lives there is Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), also called Luocha Nü (羅剎女), owner of a banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) able to extinguish the Flaming Mountains (火焰山) and wife of the mighty Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, seorang penebang kayu menyebut bahwa yang ada adalah Tieshan Gongzhu (鐵扇公主), juga bernama Luocha Nü (羅剎女), pemilik kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) yang bisa memadamkan Flaming Mountains (火焰山) dan istri Bull Demon King (大力牛魔王).
claims.quote: 這芭蕉洞雖有，卻無個鐵扇仙，只有個鐵扇公主，又名羅剎女。」行者道：「人言他有一柄芭蕉扇，能熄得火焰山，敢是他麼？」樵子道：「正是，正是。這聖賢有這件寶貝，善能熄火，保護那方人家，故此稱為鐵扇仙。我這裡人家用不著他，只知他叫做羅剎女，乃大力牛魔王妻也。

claims.statement: In the novel, a man explains that the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) of Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙), if obtained, puts out fire with one fanning, raises wind with two, and brings rain with three.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, seseorang menjelaskan bahwa kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) milik Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙) bila dimohon dapat memadamkan api dengan satu kibasan, membangkitkan angin dengan dua kibasan, dan menurunkan hujan dengan tiga kibasan.
claims.quote: 行者道：「鐵扇仙怎的？」那人道：「鐵扇仙有柄芭蕉扇，求得來，一扇息火，二扇生風，三扇下雨。

claims.statement: In the novel, after fighting Sun Wukong (行者) until evening, Luocha Nü (羅剎女) takes out the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇) and one fanning of its cold wind sweeps Sun Wukong out of sight.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, setelah bertarung sampai petang dengan Sun Wukong (行者), Luocha Nü (羅剎女) mengeluarkan kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) dan satu kibasan angin dinginnya menyapu Sun Wukong hingga tak terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: 那羅剎女與行者相持到晚，見行者棒重，卻又解數周密，料鬥他不過，即便取出芭蕉扇，幌一幌，一扇陰風，把行者搧得無影無形，莫想收留得住。

claims.statement: In the novel, Luocha Nü says that a person fanned by her treasure is carried eighty-four thousand li before stopping.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Luocha Nü berkata bahwa orang yang terkena kibasan kipasnya terbawa sejauh delapan puluh empat ribu li sebelum berhenti.
claims.quote: 我的寶貝搧著人，要去八萬四千里，方能停止；他怎麼才吹去，就回來也？

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong (老孫) tells Luocha Nü that he is already inside her belly and has seen her lungs and liver.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong (老孫) berkata kepada Luocha Nü bahwa ia sudah berada di dalam perutnya dan telah melihat paru-paru serta hatinya.
claims.quote: 老孫一生不會弄術，都是些真手段，實本事，已在尊嫂尊腹之內耍子，已見其肺肝矣。

claims.statement: In the novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) rebukes Sun Wukong for harming her son and names her son as Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王) Red Boy (紅孩兒) of Huoyun Dong (火雲洞) on Mount Hao.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) menegur Sun Wukong karena mencelakai putranya dan menyebut putranya adalah Shengying Dawang (聖嬰大王) Red Boy (紅孩兒) dari Huoyun Dong (火雲洞) di Gunung Hao.
claims.quote: 你這潑猴！既有兄弟之親，如何坑陷我子？」行者佯問道：「令郎是誰？」羅剎道：「我兒是號山枯松澗火雲洞聖嬰大王紅孩兒。

claims.statement: In the novel, the local earth deity says that Dàliwáng (大力王) is the husband of Luocha Nü (羅剎女) but has abandoned her and now lives at Moyun Cave (摩雲洞) on Jilei Mountain (積雷山), where Yumian Gongzhu (玉面公主), the daughter of a fox king, lives.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, dewa bumi berkata bahwa Dàliwáng (大力王) adalah suami Luocha Nü (羅剎女), tetapi telah meninggalkannya dan kini tinggal di Gua Moyun (摩雲洞) di Gunung Jilei (積雷山), tempat Yumian Gongzhu (玉面公主), putri seorang raja rubah, berada.
claims.quote: 大力王乃羅剎女丈夫。他這向撇了羅剎，現在積雷山摩雲洞。有個萬年狐王，那狐王死了，遺下一個女兒，叫做玉面公主。

claims.statement: In the novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) comes out carrying the banana-leaf fan (芭蕉扇), twelve chi long; seeing the gods, she kneels and begs for the couple's lives, offering the fan to Sun Wukong (孫叔叔).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) keluar membawa kipas pisang (芭蕉扇) sepanjang satu zhang dua chi; melihat para dewa, ia berlutut dan memohon agar nyawa suami-istri itu diampuni sambil menyerahkan kipas itu kepada Sun Wukong (孫叔叔).
claims.quote: 羅剎聽叫，急卸了釵環，脫了色服，挽青絲如道姑，穿縞素似比丘，雙手捧那柄丈二長短的芭蕉扇子，走出門。又見有金剛眾聖與天王父子，慌忙跪在地下，磕頭禮拜道：「望菩薩饒我夫妻之命，願將此扇奉承孫叔叔成功去也。

claims.statement: In the novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) tells how to cut the root of the fire: fan it 49 times in a row and it will never flare again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Luocha Nü (羅剎) memberi tahu bahwa untuk memutus akar api, kipas itu cukup dikibaskan berturut-turut 49 kali dan api tidak akan menyala lagi selamanya.
claims.quote: 如何治得除根？」羅剎道：「要是斷絕火根，只消連搧四十九扇，永遠再不發了。

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, before appearing as the wife of Bull Demon King in the Ming dynasty novel Journey to the West, Princess Iron Fan appeared in Yang Jingxian's Yuan dynasty zaju play Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, sebelum tampil sebagai istri Bull Demon King dalam novel dinasti Ming Journey to the West, Princess Iron Fan muncul dalam drama zaju dinasti Yuan Journey to the West karya Yang Jingxian.
claims.quote: Before her appearance as the wife of the Bull Demon King in the Ming dynasty novel Journey to the West, Princess Iron Fan appeared in Yang Jingxian's Yuan dynasty zaju play Journey to the West.

claims.statement: In the zaju play, she identifies herself as an immortal who had served as an ancestor of the Wind Department (风部祖师).
claims.statement_id: Dalam drama zaju itu, ia memperkenalkan diri sebagai makhluk abadi (immortal) yang pernah menjadi leluhur Departemen Angin (风部祖师).
claims.quote: In the play, she identifies herself as an immortal who had served as an ancestor of the Wind Department (风部祖师).

claims.statement: According to Journey to the South, Princess Iron Fan is depicted as a goddess.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Journey to the South, Princess Iron Fan digambarkan sebagai dewi (goddess).
claims.quote: According to Journey to the South, Princess Iron Fan is depicted as a goddess.

claims.statement: Because of the story of their marriage, Princess Iron Fan is worshipped alongside Huaguang Dadi in the Huaguang Great Emperor Temple.
claims.statement_id: Karena kisah pernikahan mereka, Princess Iron Fan dipuja bersama Huaguang Dadi di Kuil Huaguang Great Emperor.
claims.quote: Due to the story of their marriage, Princess Iron Fan is worshipped alongside Huaguang Dadi in the Huaguang Great Emperor Temple

claims.statement: The first Chinese animated feature film, entitled Princess Iron Fan (1941), is a liberal adaptation of the encounter between Sun Wukong and Princess Iron Fan.
claims.statement_id: Film animasi panjang Tiongkok pertama, berjudul Princess Iron Fan (1941), mengadaptasi secara bebas pertemuan Sun Wukong dan Princess Iron Fan.
claims.quote: The subject of the first Chinese animated feature film is a liberally adapted version of the encounter between Sun Wukong and Princess Iron Fan entitled Princess Iron Fan (1941).

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong asks about Cuiyun Mountain (翠雲山) and the Banana Cave (芭蕉洞) of Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙); the woodcutter confirms that it is Cuiyun Mountain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong menanyakan Gunung Cuiyun (翠雲山) dan keberadaan Gua Pisang (芭蕉洞) milik Tieshan Xian (鐵扇仙); penebang kayu membenarkan bahwa itu Gunung Cuiyun.
claims.quote: 行者近前作禮道：「樵哥，問訊了。」那樵子撇了柯斧，答禮道：「長老何往？」行者道：「敢問樵哥，這可是翠雲山？」樵子道：「正是。」行者道：「有個鐵扇仙的芭蕉洞，在何處？」

claims.statement: In the novel, Nezha (哪吒) hangs a fire wheel on the horns of Bull Demon King (牛王), and Heavenly King Li (托塔天王) fixes his true form with the 照妖鏡 mirror until he cannot flee and says he is willing to submit to the Buddhist faith.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Nezha (哪吒) menggantungkan roda api di tanduk Bull Demon King (牛王), dan Heavenly King Li (托塔天王) menahan wujud aslinya dengan cermin 照妖鏡 hingga ia tak bisa lari dan menyatakan bersedia tunduk pada ajaran Buddha.
claims.quote: 哪吒取出火輪兒掛在那老牛的角上，便吹真火，焰焰烘烘，把牛王燒得張狂哮吼，搖頭擺尾。才要變化脫身，又被托塔天王將照妖鏡照住本像，騰那不動，無計逃生，只叫：「莫傷我命，情願歸順佛家也。」

claims.statement: Baigujing (白骨精, pinyin Báigǔjīng) is a demon from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West.
claims.statement_id: Baigujing (白骨精, pinyin Báigǔjīng) adalah iblis (demon) dari novel abad ke-16 Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat).
claims.quote: Baigujing (Chinese: 白骨精; pinyin: Báigǔjīng) is a demon from the 16th-century novel Journey to the West.

claims.statement: In the William John Francis Jenner translation, the name is rendered in English as White Bone Spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan William John Francis Jenner, namanya diterjemahkan ke dalam bahasa Inggris sebagai White Bone Spirit.
claims.quote: The name is translated into English as White Bone Spirit in the William John Francis Jenner translation.

claims.statement: Baigujing is a shapeshifting demoness, and in her true form she is depicted as a skeleton.
claims.statement_id: Baigujing adalah iblis perempuan (demoness) pengubah wujud, dan dalam wujud aslinya digambarkan sebagai kerangka.
claims.quote: Baigujing is a shapeshifting demoness, and in her true form she is depicted as a skeleton.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, Baigujing desired the flesh of Tang Sanzang, disguised herself as a village girl, and offered Tang Sanzang and his disciples poisonous fruits.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Baigujing menginginkan daging Tang Sanzang, menyamar sebagai gadis desa, dan menawarkan buah beracun kepada Tang Sanzang dan murid-muridnya.
claims.quote: Baigujing was a demon who desired to eat the flesh of Tang Sanzang. It disguised itself as a village girl and offered Tang Sanzang and his disciples poisonous fruits.

claims.statement: In the novel, the demon is delighted because for years she has heard that Tang Sanzang (唐和尚) is the incarnation of Jinchanzi (金蟬子) and that anyone who eats a piece of his flesh will live a long life.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, siluman itu bergembira karena sudah bertahun-tahun mendengar bahwa Tang Sanzang (唐和尚) adalah penjelmaan Jinchanzi (金蟬子) dan bahwa orang yang memakan sepotong dagingnya akan panjang umur.
claims.quote: 造化，造化。幾年家人都講東土的唐和尚取大乘，他本是金蟬子化身，十世修行的原體，有人吃他一塊肉，長壽長生。

claims.statement: In the novel, the demon transforms (搖身一變) into a beautiful girl carrying a green clay jar and a green porcelain bottle, and walks straight toward Tang Sanzang (唐僧).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, siluman itu berubah (搖身一變) menjadi gadis cantik yang membawa kendi hijau dan botol porselen hijau, lalu berjalan langsung menuju Tang Sanzang (唐僧).
claims.quote: 好妖精，停下陰風，在那山凹裡搖身一變，變做個月貌花容的女兒，說不盡那眉清目秀，齒白唇紅。左手提著一個青砂罐兒，右手提著一個綠磁瓶兒，從西向東，徑奔唐僧

claims.statement: In the novel, when the jar and bottle are checked, the fragrant rice turns out to be a jar of long tailed maggots and the fried gluten turns out to be frogs and toads hopping everywhere.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, ketika isi kendi dan botol itu diperiksa, nasi harum ternyata berupa belatung berekor dan "gluten goreng" berupa katak dan kodok yang melompat ke mana-mana.
claims.quote: 沙僧攙著長老，近前看時，那裡是甚香米飯，卻是一罐子拖尾巴的長蛆；也不是麵觔，卻是幾個青蛙、癩蝦蟆，滿地亂跳。

claims.statement: In the novel, the demon uses the "jieshi fa" (解屍法) technique when Sun Wukong's staff comes: she slips away beforehand and leaves a false corpse struck dead on the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, siluman itu memakai "jieshi fa" (解屍法) saat tongkat Sun Wukong datang: ia meloloskan diri lebih dulu dan meninggalkan mayat palsu yang terpukul mati.
claims.quote: 那怪物有些手段，使個「解屍法」，見行者棍子來時，他卻抖擻精神，預先走了，把一個假屍首打死在地下。

claims.statement: In the novel, the demon later transforms into an old woman of eighty who walks along weeping, and then into an old man.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, siluman itu kemudian berubah menjadi perempuan tua berusia delapan puluh tahun yang berjalan sambil menangis, lalu menjadi seorang kakek.
claims.quote: 好妖精，按落陰雲，在那前山坡下搖身一變，變作個老婦人，年滿八旬，手拄著一根彎頭竹杖，一步一聲的哭著走來。 ... 好妖精，按聳陰風，在山坡下搖身一變，變做一個老公公

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong returns from picking peaches, looks with his fiery golden eyes (火眼金睛), recognizes the girl as a demon, and strikes at her at once with his iron staff.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong kembali dari memetik buah persik, menatap dengan mata api bermata emas (火眼金睛), mengenali gadis itu sebagai siluman, dan langsung memukulnya dengan tongkat besi.
claims.quote: 只見那行者自南山頂上摘了幾個桃子，托著缽盂，一觔斗，點將回來，睜火眼金睛觀看，認得那女子是個妖精，放下缽盂，掣鐵棒，當頭就打。

claims.statement: In the novel, Sun Wukong says the creature is a jiangshi (僵尸, corpse) that has become a troublemaker; once killed it shows its true form, and on its back is written "Baigu Furen" (白骨夫人).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Sun Wukong berkata bahwa makhluk itu adalah jiangshi (僵尸, mayat) yang menjelma menjadi pengacau; setelah dibunuh ia menampakkan wujud aslinya, dan di punggungnya tertulis "Baigu Furen" (白骨夫人).
claims.quote: 他是個潛靈作怪的僵尸，在此迷人敗本，被我打殺，他就現了本相。他那脊梁上有一行字，叫做『白骨夫人』。

claims.statement: In the novel, the body that has just died turns out to be a pile of white skeleton (粉骷髏), and Tang Sanzang is shocked.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, tubuh yang baru mati itu ternyata berupa setumpuk tengkorak putih (粉骷髏), dan Tang Sanzang terkejut karenanya.
claims.quote: 卻是一堆粉骷髏在那裡。唐僧大驚道：「悟空，這個人才死了，怎麼就化作一堆骷髏？」

claims.statement: In the novel, Zhu Bajie (八戒) goads Tang Sanzang by saying Sun Wukong deliberately changed the corpse into a skeleton to fool his master; Tang Sanzang believes him and chants the spell again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Zhu Bajie (八戒) menghasut Tang Sanzang dengan mengatakan bahwa Sun Wukong sengaja mengubah mayat itu menjadi kerangka untuk mengelabui mata gurunya; Tang Sanzang percaya dan kembali merapal mantra.
claims.quote: 怎禁那八戒傍邊唆嘴道：「師父，他的手重棍兇，把人打死，只怕你念那話兒，故意變化這個模樣，掩你的眼目哩。」唐僧果然耳軟，又信了他，隨復念起。

claims.statement: In the novel, the disguised girl says the mountain is called Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), where snakes turn back and beasts take fright.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sosok gadis yang menyamar itu menyebut bahwa gunung itu bernama Baihu Ling (白虎嶺), tempat ular mundur dan hewan buas takut.
claims.quote: 師父，此山叫做蛇回獸怕的白虎嶺，正西下面是我家。我父母在堂，看經好善，廣齋方上遠近僧人。

claims.statement: In the novel, after being dismissed, Sun Wukong takes leave of his master holding back his anger and flies on a somersault cloud back to the Water Curtain Cave (水簾洞) on Flower-Fruit Mountain (花果山).
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, setelah diusir, Sun Wukong berpamitan dengan menahan amarah dan terbang dengan awan salto kembali ke Gua Tirai Air (水簾洞) di Gunung Buah Bunga (花果山).
claims.quote: 你看他忍氣別了師父，縱觔斗雲，徑回花果山水簾洞去了。獨自個悽悽慘慘，忽聞得水聲聒耳。

claims.statement: In the novel, a saying is cited, "where mountains are high there must be monsters, where ridges are steep spirits are born," and indeed there is a yaojing (妖精, demon) on that mountain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, dikatakan bahwa ada pepatah "gunung tinggi pasti ada siluman, bukit curam melahirkan roh", dan memang ada seorang yaojing (妖精, siluman) di gunung itu.
claims.quote: 卻說常言有云：「山高必有怪，嶺峻卻生精。」果然這山上有一個妖精，孫大聖去時，驚動那怪。

claims.statement: In The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing is the main antagonist.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing adalah antagonis utama.
claims.quote: In The Monkey King Conquers the Demon, Baigujing is the main antagonist.

claims.statement: In the TV series Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (referred to as Lady Bone Demon) is the main antagonist in the second and third seasons.
claims.statement_id: Dalam serial TV Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (disebut Lady Bone Demon) adalah antagonis utama di musim kedua dan ketiga.
claims.quote: In the TV series Lego Monkie Kid, Baigujing (referred to as Lady Bone Demon) is the main antagonist in the second and third season.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, Sun Wukong finally beats Baigujing with his staff and kills her, revealing that she was just a skeleton spirit.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Sun Wukong akhirnya memukul Baigujing dengan tongkatnya dan membunuhnya, sehingga tampak bahwa makhluk itu hanyalah roh kerangka (skeleton spirit).
claims.quote: Provoked, Sun finally beats Baigujing with his staff and kills the demon, revealing that it was just a skeleton spirit.

claims.statement: Six-Eared Macaque is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).
claims.statement_id: Six-Eared Macaque adalah antagonis utama dan salah satu tokoh paling kuat dalam novel fantasi Journey to the West (Perjalanan ke Barat) karya Wu Cheng'en, yang paling diingat karena menirukan Sun Wukong (Monkey King) dengan sangat mirip.
claims.quote: is a major antagonist and one of the most powerful characters in Wu Cheng'en's fantasy novel Journey to the West, best remembered for closely impersonating Sun Wukong (Monkey King).

claims.statement: The Chinese name of the Six-Eared Macaque is 六耳獼猴, in pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.
claims.statement_id: Nama Tionghoa Six-Eared Macaque adalah 六耳獼猴, dalam pinyin Liù'ěr míhóu.
claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque (Chinese: 六耳獼猴; pinyin: Liù'ěr míhóu)

claims.statement: According to the Buddha in the novel, the Six-Eared Macaque is one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories into which all beings in the universe are classified.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Buddha dalam novel, Six-Eared Macaque adalah satu dari empat primata spiritual yang tidak termasuk dalam sepuluh golongan yang menjadi pengelompokan semua makhluk di alam semesta.
claims.quote: according to the Buddha, one of the four spiritual primates that do not belong to any of the ten categories that all beings in the universe are classified under.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Buddha also says the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" because his six ears eavesdrop on information around him, "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Buddha juga berkata bahwa Six-Eared Macaque "hampir mahatahu" (near-omniscient) karena enam telinganya menyadap banyak informasi di sekelilingnya, "mengetahui masa lalu dan masa depan", dan "memahami segala hal".
claims.quote: Buddha also says that the Six-Eared Macaque is "near-omniscient" (thanks to his six ears eavesdropping upon many tidbits of information around him far and wide), "knowledgeable of past and future" and "comprehensive of all things".

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) disguised as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious, steals his baggage and paperwork, and takes them to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, dengan harapan menggantikan Sun Wukong dan menerima ganjarannya dari Buddha, Six-Eared Macaque pertama kali muncul di Xiliang (西粱) menyamar sebagai Sun Wukong. Ia membuat Tang Sanzang pingsan, mencuri barang dan dokumennya, lalu membawanya ke Flower-Fruit Mountain untuk membentuk rombongan peziarahnya sendiri.
claims.quote: Hoping to replace Sun Wukong and gain his rewards from the Buddha in Sun Wukong's place, the Six-Eared Macaque first appears in Xiliang (西粱) in disguise as Sun Wukong. He knocks Tang Sanzang unconscious and steals the baggage and paperwork which he takes to Flower-Fruit Mountain to set up his own pilgrim band.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, the Six-Eared Macaque tries to flee when he hears the Buddha speak of his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl; the macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, Six-Eared Macaque mencoba kabur saat mendengar Buddha membicarakan jati dirinya, tetapi Buddha mengurungnya di bawah mangkuk sedekah emas raksasa; setelah itu ia dibunuh Sun Wukong.
claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque attempts to flee when he hears the Buddha speak about his true identity, but the Buddha traps him under a giant golden alms bowl. The macaque is then killed by Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: In the novel, the figure who appears as Sun Wukong (行者) in chapter 57 scolds Tang Sanzang, strikes him on the back with an iron staff until he faints, and then flies off on a somersault cloud with two bundles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sosok yang tampil sebagai Sun Wukong (行者) di Bab 57 memarahi Tang Sanzang, memukulnya dengan tongkat besi hingga pingsan, lalu membawa kabur dua bungkusan kain dengan awan salto.
claims.quote: 那行者變了臉，發怒生嗔，喝罵長老道：「你這個狠心的潑禿！十分賤我。」掄鐵棒，丟了磁杯，望長老脊背上砑了一下。那長老昏暈在地，不能言語，被他把兩個青氈包袱提在手中，駕觔斗雲，不知去向。

claims.statement: In the novel, the "Sun Wukong" at the Water Curtain Cave says that he beat Tang Sanzang and took his baggage, and that he himself will go west to worship the Buddha and fetch the scriptures, so that the world will honor him as a founder and his name will be passed down for generations.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, "Sun Wukong" di Gua Tirai Air berkata bahwa ia memukul Tang Sanzang dan merampas barangnya, dan bahwa ia sendiri akan pergi ke Barat untuk menghadap Buddha dan mengambil kitab, agar dunia mengangkatnya sebagai perintis dan namanya dikenang turun-temurun.
claims.quote: 我打唐僧，搶行李，不因我不上西方，亦不因我愛居此地。我今熟讀了牒文，我自己上西方拜佛求經，送上東土，我獨成功，教那南贍部洲人立我為祖，萬代傳名也。

claims.statement: In the novel, Diting (諦聽) says in the underworld that the demon's powers are the same as Sun Wukong's, so the gods of the underworld cannot capture him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Diting (諦聽) berkata di alam baka bahwa kesaktian siluman itu sama dengan Sun Wukong, sehingga para dewa alam baka tidak mampu menangkapnya.
claims.quote: 妖精神通，與孫大聖無二。幽冥之神，能有多少法力？故此不能擒拿。

claims.statement: In the novel, Rulai (如來, the Buddha) names four monkeys outside the ten categories of beings: the Lingming stone monkey (靈明石猴), the red-buttocked horse monkey (赤尻馬猴), the long-armed ape (通臂猿猴), and the fourth, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), skilled at listening, able to discern reason, knowing before and after, and understanding all things.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來, Buddha) menyebut empat kera yang tidak termasuk sepuluh golongan makhluk: kera batu Lingming (靈明石猴), kera pantat merah (赤尻馬猴), kera lengan panjang (通臂猿猴), dan yang keempat Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang pandai mendengar, mampu menelaah, tahu sebelum dan sesudah, dan memahami segala hal.
claims.quote: 又有四猴混世，不入十類之種。」菩薩道：「敢問是那四猴？」如來道：「第一是靈明石猴，通變化，識天時，知地利，移星換斗；第二是赤尻馬猴，曉陰陽，會人事，善出入，避死延生；第三是通臂猿猴，拿日月，縮千山，辨休咎，乾坤摩弄；第四是六耳獼猴，善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。

claims.statement: In the novel, Rulai (如來) says that when this monkey stands in one place he can know events a thousand li away and also what people say, and that Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) is the one who matches the real Sun Wukong (真悟空) in form and voice.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, Rulai (如來) berkata bahwa bila kera ini berdiri di satu tempat ia dapat mengetahui kejadian sejauh seribu li dan juga ucapan manusia, dan bahwa Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴) adalah yang serupa rupa dan suara dengan Sun Wukong (真悟空) yang asli.
claims.quote: 此猴若立一處，能知千里外之事；凡人說話，亦能知之。故此善聆音，能察理，知前後，萬物皆明。與真悟空同像同音者，六耳獼猴也。

claims.statement: In the novel, the monkey transforms into a bee (蜜蜂兒) and flies upward, but Rulai (如來) throws his golden bowl (金缽盂), which falls and covers the bee.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, kera itu berubah menjadi seekor lebah (蜜蜂兒) dan terbang ke atas, tetapi Rulai (如來) melemparkan mangkuk emas (金缽盂) yang jatuh menutupi lebah itu.
claims.quote: 那獼猴毛骨悚然，料著難脫，即忙搖身一變，變作個蜜蜂兒，往上便飛。如來將金缽盂撇起去，正蓋著那蜂兒，落下來。

claims.statement: In the novel, when the bowl is lifted his true form appears, a Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) cannot hold back and strikes his head dead with the iron staff, so that this kind is extinct.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, ketika mangkuk diangkat, tampaklah wujud aslinya, Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴); Sun Wukong (孫大聖) tak tahan dan memukul kepalanya dengan tongkat besi sampai mati, sehingga jenis ini punah.
claims.quote: 大眾一發上前，把缽盂揭起，果然見了本像，是一個六耳獼猴。孫大聖忍不住，掄起鐵棒，劈頭一下打死，至今絕此一種。

claims.statement: In the novel, the Bodhisattva tells Tang Sanzang that the one who struck him the other day was the false Sun Wukong (假行者), Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), who has been killed by Sun Wukong thanks to Rulai's recognition.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, sang Bodhisattva memberi tahu Tang Sanzang bahwa yang memukulnya tempo hari adalah Sun Wukong palsu (假行者), yaitu Liu'er Mihou (六耳獼猴), yang telah dibunuh Sun Wukong berkat pengenalan Rulai.
claims.quote: 菩薩道：「唐僧，前日打你的，乃假行者六耳獼猴也。幸如來知識，已被悟空打死。

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the name of the Six-eared Macaque is a likely nod to the old saying that "a secret is not safe between six ears".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, nama Six-eared Macaque kemungkinan merujuk pada pepatah lama bahwa "rahasia tidak aman di antara enam telinga".
claims.quote: The Six-eared Macaque's name is a likely nod to the old saying that "a secret is not safe between six ears"

claims.statement: According to an interpretation recorded by Wikipedia, the monkey symbolizes the mind in Chinese Buddhism, and the two monkeys are likely metaphors for zhenxin (真心, "true mind") and wangxin (妄心, "false mind").
claims.statement_id: Menurut tafsir yang dicatat Wikipedia, kera melambangkan pikiran dalam Buddhisme Tiongkok, dan kedua kera itu kemungkinan metafora zhenxin (真心, "pikiran sejati") dan wangxin (妄心, "pikiran palsu").
claims.quote: Monkey symbolizes the mind in Chinese Buddhism, and the two monkeys are likely metaphors for zhenxin (真心; "true mind") and wangxin (妄心; "false mind")

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, the Ming dynasty Xu Xiyouji.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Six-Eared Macaque dilahirkan kembali dalam salah satu sekuel tidak resmi paling awal dari Xiyouji, yaitu Xu Xiyouji dari dinasti Ming.
claims.quote: The Six-Eared Macaque is reincarnated in one of the earliest unofficial sequels to Xiyouji, the Ming dynasty Xu Xiyouji

claims.statement: According to Hongmei Sun as cited by Wikipedia, Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Hongmei Sun yang dikutip Wikipedia, pembunuhan Sun Wukong atas rekan, saingan, dan kembaran dirinya adalah "pertentangan diri yang ekstrem" (self-contradiction to an extreme).
claims.quote: Hongmei Sun argues that Sun Wukong's killing of his peer, rival and doppelgänger is "self-contradiction to an extreme"

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia's summary, no one can tell the real Sun Wukong from the fake; the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan Wikipedia, tak seorang pun dapat membedakan Sun Wukong asli dan palsu; mantra penyamaran Six-Eared Macaque begitu baik sehingga ia juga bereaksi terhadap "Headache Sutra", sampai keduanya menghadap Buddha, yang menjelaskan tentang empat primata spiritual.
claims.quote: No one is able to differentiate between the real and the fake Sun Wukong—the Six-Eared Macaque's spell of impersonation is so good that he also responds to the "Headache Sutra", preventing the pilgrims from differentiating between him and Sun Wukong—until the two appear before the Buddha, who tells them about the four spiritual primates.

claims.statement: Erlang Shen, or simply Erlang, is a god in Chinese folk religion and Daoism, associated with water (flood control), justice, warriorhood, hunting, and demon subdual.
claims.statement_id: Erlang Shen, atau Erlang saja, adalah dewa dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok dan Daoisme yang dikaitkan dengan air (pengendalian banjir), keadilan, keprajuritan, perburuan, dan penaklukan iblis.
claims.quote: Erlang Shen, or simply Erlang, is a god in Chinese folk religion and Daoism, associated with water (flood control), justice, warriorhood, hunting, and demon subdual.

claims.statement: He is most commonly believed to be the deification of Li Erlang, the second son of Li Bing, a hydraulic engineer of the Qin dynasty (221–206 BC).
claims.statement_id: Ia paling lazim dipercaya sebagai pendewaan Li Erlang, putra kedua Li Bing, seorang insinyur hidrolik zaman Dinasti Qin (221–206 SM).
claims.quote: He is most commonly believed to be the deification of Li Erlang, the second son of Li Bing, a hydraulic engineer of the Qin dynasty (221–206 BC).

claims.statement: Erlang (二郎) literally means 'second son/boy/lad/male' and is an ancient given name for boys.
claims.statement_id: Erlang (二郎) secara harfiah berarti 'putra kedua/anak laki-laki' dan merupakan nama pemberian kuno untuk anak laki-laki.
claims.quote: Erlang (Chinese: 二郎; pinyin: Èrláng; lit. 'Second Son/Boy/Lad/Male') is an ancient given name for boys.

claims.statement: Shen (神) means 'God'.
claims.statement_id: Shen (神) berarti 'dewa'.
claims.quote: Shen (Chinese: 神; pinyin: Shén) means "God".

claims.statement: Since Li Erlang was from Guankou, Sichuan, the god Erlang is also known by the epithets Chuanzhu (川主, 'Lord of Sichuan') and Guankou Erlang (灌口二郎, 'Erlang of Guankou').
claims.statement_id: Karena Li Erlang berasal dari Guankou, Sichuan, dewa Erlang juga dikenal dengan julukan Chuanzhu (川主, 'Penguasa Sichuan') dan Guankou Erlang (灌口二郎, 'Erlang dari Guankou').
claims.quote: Since Li Erlang was from Guankou, Sichuan, the god Erlang is also known by the epithets Chuanzhu (Chinese: 川主; pinyin: Chuānzhǔ; lit. 'Lord of Sichuan') and Guankou Erlang (Chinese: 灌口二郎; pinyin: Guànkǒu Èrláng; lit. 'Erlang of Guankou').

claims.statement: He is commonly depicted as a young man with a third, truth-seeing eye in the middle of his forehead, wielding a three-pronged spear, and accompanied by his loyal hunting dog, Xiaotian Quan.
claims.statement_id: Ia biasa digambarkan sebagai pemuda dengan mata ketiga yang melihat kebenaran di tengah dahinya, bersenjata tombak bermata tiga, dan ditemani anjing pemburu setianya, Xiaotian Quan.
claims.quote: He is commonly depicted as a young man with a third, truth-seeing eye in the middle of his forehead, wielding a three-pronged spear, and being accompanied by his loyal hunting dog, Xiaotian Quan.

claims.statement: He originated as a local god of Guankou, Sichuan, where Li Erlang was from. During the Northern Song dynasty (960–1127 CE), the cult of Erlang spread to the rest of China.
claims.statement_id: Ia bermula sebagai dewa lokal Guankou, Sichuan, tempat asal Li Erlang. Pada masa Dinasti Song Utara (960–1127 M), pemujaan Erlang menyebar ke seluruh Tiongkok.
claims.quote: He originated as a local god of Guankou, Sichuan, where Li Erlang was from. During the Northern Song dynasty (960–1127 CE), the cult of Erlang spread to the rest of China.

claims.statement: According to Jim R. McClanahan (citing Wu 1987), Lord Erlang was originally worshiped during the Han as a hunting god and queller of mountain ghosts by the Qiang ethnic group of western Sichuan.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Jim R. McClanahan (merujuk Wu 1987), Tuan Erlang semula dipuja pada zaman Han sebagai dewa pemburu dan penakluk hantu gunung oleh kelompok etnis Qiang di wilayah Sichuan barat.
claims.quote: Lord Erlang was originally worshiped during the Han as a hunting god and queller of mountain ghosts by the Qiang (羌) ethnic group of the western Sichuan region.

claims.statement: According to Wu (1987), quoted by McClanahan, the Erlang cult became even more popular in Sichuan under the patronage of the Later Shu emperor Meng Chang (r. 934-65); in 965, when the Song dynasty conquered the kingdom, it adopted the cult and erected temples for the god in the capital and throughout the country.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kajian Wu (1987) yang dikutip McClanahan, kultus Erlang semakin populer di Sichuan di bawah dukungan kaisar Shu Kemudian, Meng Chang (berkuasa 934-65); pada 965, ketika Dinasti Song menaklukkan kerajaan itu, Song mengadopsi kultus tersebut dan mendirikan kuil bagi sang dewa di ibu kota dan di seluruh negeri.
claims.quote: The Er-lang cult became even more popular in Sichuan under the patronage of the Later Shu emperor, Meng Chang 孟昶 (r. 934-65), and in 965, when the Song dynasty conquered the kingdom, it adopted the cult, erecting temples for the god in the capital and throughout the country.

claims.statement: According to the Cleveland Museum of Art, the painting theme 'Searching the Mountains' is associated with the legend of the god Erlang, who ended devastating floods by defeating a vicious dragon and other malevolent creatures on Mount Guankou in Sichuan Province in southwest China.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cleveland Museum of Art, tema lukisan 'Searching the Mountains' (mencari iblis di pegunungan) dikaitkan dengan legenda dewa Erlang, yang berhasil mengakhiri banjir dahsyat dengan mengalahkan naga ganas dan makhluk jahat lain di Gunung Guankou, Provinsi Sichuan, Tiongkok barat daya.
claims.quote: Searching the Mountains is associated with the legend of the god Erlang, who succeeded in ending devastating floods by defeating a vicious dragon and other malevolent creatures on Mount Guankou in Sichuan Province in southwest China.

claims.statement: According to the Cleveland Museum of Art, a pivotal scene in paintings of this theme shows a giant dragon being chained by demon-soldiers under the command of Erlang, who appears in the civil robes of a court official.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cleveland Museum of Art, adegan penting dalam lukisan bertema ini memperlihatkan naga raksasa dirantai oleh prajurit-iblis di bawah komando Erlang, yang tampil dengan jubah sipil seorang pejabat istana.
claims.quote: A pivotal scene shows a giant dragon being chained by demon-soldiers under the command of Erlang, who appears in the civil robes of a court official.

claims.statement: According to the Cleveland Museum of Art, paintings of the 'Searching the Mountains' theme are rarely seen and only about a dozen are known to survive.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cleveland Museum of Art, lukisan bertema 'Searching the Mountains' jarang terlihat dan hanya sekitar selusin yang diketahui masih ada.
claims.quote: Paintings of this theme are rarely seen and only about a dozen of them are known to be extant.

claims.statement: According to the Cleveland Museum of Art, the third section of an album, called 'Clearing the Mountains,' features divine soldiers, presumably led by the deity Erlang Shen (二郎神), fighting undesirable creatures.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Cleveland Museum of Art, bagian ketiga sebuah album lukisan bertajuk 'Clearing the Mountains' menampilkan prajurit ilahi yang diperkirakan dipimpin dewa Erlang Shen (二郎神) melawan makhluk-makhluk yang tidak diinginkan.
claims.quote: The third section, called “Clearing the Mountains,” features divine soldiers, led presumably by the deity Erlang Shen 二郎神, fighting undesirable creatures.

claims.statement: According to McClanahan, one anonymous 13th-century album leaf ink painting portrays Erlang seated in a kingly fashion and watching as his spirit soldiers round up and execute ape demons.
claims.statement_id: Menurut McClanahan, sebuah lukisan tinta lembar album anonim dari abad ke-13 menampilkan Erlang duduk bak raja sambil menyaksikan prajurit rohnya menangkap dan mengeksekusi iblis kera.
claims.quote: One anonymous 13th-century album leaf ink painting portrays Erlang seated in a kingly fashion and watching as his spirit soldiers round up and execute ape demons

claims.statement: According to McClanahan, the image of the deity as a queller of ape monsters culminated in an anonymous Yuan-Ming Dynasty play called The God Er-lang Locks up the Great Sage-Equal to Heaven (二郎神鎖齊天大聖).
claims.statement_id: Menurut McClanahan, citra sang dewa sebagai penakluk monster kera memuncak dalam sebuah drama anonim zaman Yuan-Ming berjudul The God Er-lang Locks up the Great Sage-Equal to Heaven (二郎神鎖齊天大聖).
claims.quote: The image of the deity as a queller of ape monsters culminated in an anonymous Yuan-Ming Dynasty play called The God Er-lang Locks up the Great Sage-Equal to Heaven (二郎神鎖齊天大聖, Er-lang Shen suo Qitian Dasheng).

claims.statement: In the novel Journey to the West (Xiyouji), Guanyin recommends to the Jade Emperor a deity, the Illustrious Sage Erlang Zhenjun, the emperor's nephew, who lives at Guanjiangkou in Guanzhou and receives incense offerings from below; he once slew six monsters and has the Meishan brothers and twelve hundred 'grass-head gods'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Perjalanan ke Barat (Xiyouji), Guanyin menyarankan kepada Kaisar Giok seorang dewa: Xiansheng Erlang Zhenjun, keponakan sang kaisar, yang tinggal di Guanjiangkou di Guanzhou dan menerima dupa persembahan dari bawah; ia pernah membinasakan enam siluman dan memiliki saudara-saudara Meishan serta seribu dua ratus 'dewa kepala rumput'.
claims.quote: 乃陛下令甥顯聖二郎真君，見居灌洲灌江口，享受下方香火。他昔日曾力誅六怪，又有梅山兄弟與帳前一千二百草頭神，神通廣大。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, Erlang introduces himself to Sun Wukong as the Jade Emperor's nephew, enfeoffed as Prince Zhaohui Lingxian (昭惠靈顯王), and says he has come on higher orders to capture him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, Erlang memperkenalkan diri kepada Sun Wukong sebagai keponakan Kaisar Giok yang bergelar Raja Zhaohui Lingxian (昭惠靈顯王), dan menyatakan datang atas perintah atas untuk menangkapnya.
claims.quote: 吾乃玉帝外甥、敕封昭惠靈顯王二郎是也。今蒙上命，到此擒你這造反天宮的弼馬溫猢猻，你還不知死活。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, Sun Wukong recalls that the Jade Emperor's sister longed for the mortal world, descended, married a man surnamed Yang, and bore a son who once split Peach Mountain with an axe, and asks whether that is Erlang.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, Sun Wukong menyebut bahwa adik perempuan Kaisar Giok turun ke dunia karena merindukan kehidupan manusia, menikah dengan seorang bermarga Yang, dan melahirkan seorang putra yang pernah membelah Gunung Tao dengan kapak; ia menanyakan apakah itu Erlang.
claims.quote: 我記得當年玉帝妹子思凡下界，配合楊君，生一男子，曾使斧劈桃山的，是你麼？

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, in the duel with Sun Wukong, Erlang summons his divine might, transforms into a figure ten thousand zhang tall, and raises his three-pointed, double-edged divine spear with both hands.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, dalam duel melawan Sun Wukong, Erlang mengerahkan wibawa ilahinya, berubah wujud menjadi setinggi sepuluh ribu zhang, dan mengangkat tombak sakti bermata tiga berbilah dua dengan kedua tangannya.
claims.quote: 真君抖擻神威，搖身一變，變得身高萬丈，兩隻手舉著三尖兩刃神鋒，好便似華山頂上之峰

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, while Sun Wukong is fighting the seven sages, a weapon falls from heaven and strikes his head so that he stumbles; Erlang's hound (細犬) catches up, bites his calf, and pulls him down again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, ketika Sun Wukong sedang bertarung melawan tujuh dewa, sebuah senjata jatuh dari langit mengenai kepalanya sehingga ia terjatuh; anjing pemburu (細犬) milik Erlang mengejarnya, menggigit betisnya, dan menjatuhkannya lagi.
claims.quote: 猴王只顧苦戰七聖，卻不知天上墜下這兵器，打中了天靈，立不穩腳，跌了一跤，爬將起來就跑。被二郎爺爺的細犬趕上，照腿肚子上一口，又扯了一跌。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, a verse describes Erlang with a pellet bow at his waist and a three-pointed, double-edged spear in hand; it also says he split Peach Mountain with an axe to save his mother and swore brotherhood with the seven sages of Meishan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, sebuah syair menggambarkan Erlang membawa busur peluru di pinggang dan memegang tombak bermata tiga berbilah dua; syair itu juga menyebut ia membelah Gunung Tao dengan kapak untuk menyelamatkan ibunya, serta mengikat persaudaraan dengan tujuh orang suci Meishan.
claims.quote: 腰挎彈弓新月樣，手執三尖兩刃槍。斧劈桃山曾救母，彈打鋋羅雙鳳凰。力誅八怪聲名遠，義結梅山七聖行。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian calls himself a disciple of Yuding Zhenren of Jinxia Cave on Mount Yuquan, as he tells his opponent that he is already inside the opponent's belly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian menyebut dirinya murid Yuding Zhenren dari Gua Jinxia di Gunung Yuquan, ketika ia berbicara kepada lawannya dengan menyatakan dirinya sudah berada di dalam perut lawan itu.
claims.quote: 楊戩在腹內答曰：「吾乃玉泉山金霞洞玉鼎真人門徒楊戩是也。今已在你腹內。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nüwa tells Yang Jian that, although he is a disciple of Yuding Zhenren skilled in 'eight-nine transformations,' he cannot subdue the monster, and gives him a treasure.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nuwa berkata kepada Yang Jian bahwa ia murid Yuding Zhenren yang pandai 'delapan-sembilan perubahan' tetapi tidak mampu menaklukkan siluman itu, lalu memberinya sebuah pusaka.
claims.quote: 你雖是玉泉山金霞洞玉鼎真人門徒，善會八九變化，不能降伏此怪。吾將此寶授你

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian sends up his dog Xiaotian Quan (哮天犬); described as an immortal hound, it dodges Dai Li's bead (珠) and seizes Dai Li in its jaws so that he cannot struggle free.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian melepaskan anjing Xiaotian Quan (哮天犬) ke udara; anjing yang disebut anjing dewata itu menghindari manik (珠) milik Dai Li lalu menggigit Dai Li hingga tak bisa meronta.
claims.quote: 楊戩祭起哮天犬，飛在空中。此犬乃是仙犬，看見此珠，十分兇惡，竟讓過他的珠來奔戴禮。戴禮見仙犬奔來，正欲抽身逃走，早被哮天犬一口咬住，不能掙挫。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian tells Jiang Ziya that Yuan Hong (袁洪) is a white ape of Mount Meishan who has attained the Way and is very cunning, and that he will remove him gradually.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Yang Jian berkata kepada Jiang Ziya bahwa Yuan Hong (袁洪) adalah kera putih Gunung Meishan yang telah memperoleh Dao dan sangat cerdik, dan ia akan menyingkirkannya perlahan-lahan.
claims.quote: 子牙大喜；又謂楊戩曰：「只是袁洪此怪未除，如之奈何？」楊戩曰：「此怪乃梅山得道白猿，最是精靈，俟徐徐除之。」

claims.statement: According to an ancient text, Erlang Baojuan, Yang Jian's mother was Princess Yunhua, the Jade Emperor's sister, who was imprisoned under Mount Tao for violating the Heavenly Rules by marrying a human named Yang Tianyou.
claims.statement_id: Menurut teks kuno Erlang Baojuan, ibu Yang Jian adalah Putri Yunhua, adik perempuan Kaisar Giok, yang dipenjara di bawah Gunung Tao karena melanggar Aturan Langit dengan menikahi manusia bernama Yang Tianyou.
claims.quote: According to an ancient text, Erlang Baojuan, Yang Jian's mother was Princess Yunhua, the Jade Emperor's sister, who was imprisoned under Mount Tao because she violated the Heavenly Rules by marrying a human named Yang Tianyou.

claims.statement: Erlang Shen is also identified with Zhao Yu, a hermit who lived on Mount Qingcheng and was appointed by Emperor Yang of Sui as Governor of Jiazhou.
claims.statement_id: Erlang Shen juga diidentifikasi dengan Zhao Yu, seorang pertapa di Gunung Qingcheng yang diangkat Kaisar Yang dari Sui sebagai Gubernur Jiazhou.
claims.quote: Erlang Shen is also identified with Zhao Yu, a hermit who lived on Mount Qingcheng and was appointed by Emperor Yang of Sui as Governor of Jiazhou.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Li Erlang assisted his father in building the complex irrigation system that prevented the Min River from flooding and irrigated the Chengdu Plain.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Li Erlang membantu ayahnya membangun sistem irigasi rumit yang mencegah Sungai Min meluap dan mengairi Dataran Chengdu.
claims.quote: Li Erlang assisted his father in the construction of the complex irrigation system that prevented the Min River from flooding and irrigated the Chengdu Plain.

claims.statement: In later stories, Erlang is the deification of Yang Jian, son of the goddess Yunhua and nephew of the legendary Jade Emperor. This portrayal as Yang Jian is most common in popular media.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah-kisah yang lebih belakangan, Erlang adalah pendewaan Yang Jian, putra dewi Yunhua dan keponakan Kaisar Giok yang legendaris. Penggambaran sebagai Yang Jian ini paling umum dalam media populer.
claims.quote: In later stories, Erlang is the deification of Yang Jian, son of the goddess Yunhua, and nephew of the legendary Jade Emperor. This portrayal as Yang Jian is most common in popular media.

claims.statement: Erlang is featured as a boss in the Game Science 2024 video game Black Myth: Wukong, voiced by Zhang Jie in Mandarin and Andrew Koji in English.
claims.statement_id: Erlang tampil sebagai bos dalam gim video Black Myth: Wukong (Game Science, 2024), diisi suara oleh Zhang Jie dalam bahasa Mandarin dan Andrew Koji dalam bahasa Inggris.
claims.quote: Erlang is featured as a boss in the Game Science 2024 video game Black Myth: Wukong, voiced by Zhang Jie in Mandarin and Andrew Koji in English.

claims.statement: As a god, Erlang is a noble and powerful warrior who vanquishes demons and monsters, and embodies justice and righteousness.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa, Erlang adalah prajurit mulia dan perkasa yang menaklukkan iblis dan monster, serta mewujudkan keadilan dan kebenaran.
claims.quote: As a god, Erlang is a noble and powerful warrior who vanquishes demons and monsters, and embodies justice and righteousness.

claims.statement: In the Ming-era semi-mythical novels Investiture of the Gods (Fengshen Yanyi) and Journey to the West, Erlang Shen is the nephew of the Jade Emperor. In the former he assists the Zhou army in defeating the Shang; in the latter he is the second son of a mortal and the Jade Emperor's sister Yunhua, and an enemy-turned-ally of Sun Wukong.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel semimitos zaman Ming, Fengshen Yanyi (Investiture of the Gods) dan Perjalanan ke Barat, Erlang Shen adalah keponakan Kaisar Giok. Dalam novel pertama ia membantu pasukan Zhou mengalahkan Shang; dalam novel kedua ia putra kedua seorang manusia fana dan Yunhua, adik Kaisar Giok, serta musuh yang kemudian menjadi sekutu Sun Wukong.
claims.quote: In the Ming-era semi-mythical novels Investiture of the Gods and Journey to the West, Erlang Shen is the nephew of the Jade Emperor. In the former novel, he assists the Zhou army in defeating the Shang. In the latter, he is the second son of a mortal and the Jade Emperor's sister Yunhua, as well as an enemy-turned-ally of Sun Wukong.

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Fengshen Yanyi (封神演義), commonly called Fengshen Bang, is a Chinese novel of gods and demons whose author is given as Chen Zhonglin (or Xu Zhonglin) of the Ming dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Fengshen Yanyi (封神演義), yang biasa disebut Fengshen Bang, adalah novel dewa-iblis Tiongkok; pengarangnya disebut Chen Zhonglin (atau Xu Zhonglin) dari Dinasti Ming.
claims.quote: 《封神演義》，一般俗稱《封神榜》，又名《商周列國全傳》、《武王伐紂外史》、《封神傳》。是一部中國神魔小說，作者是明朝的陳仲琳（或許仲琳）

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Xiyouji (Journey to the West) is a long Chinese mythological novel of the Ming dynasty, written in classical vernacular, in 100 chapters.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Xiyouji (Perjalanan ke Barat) adalah novel mitologi panjang dari zaman Dinasti Ming, ditulis dalam bahasa lisan klasik dengan 100 bab.
claims.quote: 《西遊記》是中國明代長篇神話小說，古代白話寫成。全書20卷100回。

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Fengshen Yanyi was roughly completed in the Longqing and Wanli periods; it has one hundred chapters and is set against Jiang Ziya helping the house of Zhou (King Wen and King Wu) attack the Shang tyrant.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Fengshen Yanyi kira-kira rampung ditulis pada masa Longqing dan Wanli; novel ini terdiri dari seratus bab dengan latar Jiang Ziya membantu wangsa Zhou (Raja Wen dan Raja Wu) menyerang Zhou raja Shang.
claims.quote: 約成書於隆慶、萬曆年間。全書共一百回，以姜子牙輔佐周室（周文王、周武王）討伐商紂的歷史為背景

claims.statement: Nezha (哪吒), sometimes called Nezha the Crown Prince (哪吒太子) or Natha, is a protection deity in Taoism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and Chinese folk religion.
claims.statement_id: Nezha (哪吒), kadang disebut Nezha Sang Putra Mahkota (哪吒太子) atau Natha, adalah dewa pelindung dalam Taoisme, Buddhisme, Konfusianisme, dan agama rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Nezha (哪吒, Nézhā) or sometimes Nezha the Crown Prince (哪吒太子, Nézhā Tàizǐ), or Natha, is a protection deity in Taoism, Buddhism, Confucianism, and Chinese folk religion.

claims.statement: His official Taoist name is 'Marshal of the Central Altar' (中壇元帥). After he became a deity he was given the title 'Third Lotus Prince' (蓮花三太子).
claims.statement_id: Nama resmi Taoisnya adalah 'Marsekal Altar Tengah' (中壇元帥). Setelah menjadi dewa, ia diberi gelar 'Pangeran Ketiga Teratai' (蓮花三太子).
claims.quote: His official Taoist name is "Marshal of the Central Altar" (中壇元帥). He was then given the title "Third Lotus Prince" (蓮花三太子) after he became a deity.

claims.statement: Nezha is worshipped in Chinese folk religion and is called 'Marshal of the Central Altar' (三坛大会元帅) or the 'Third Prince' (三太子).
claims.statement_id: Nezha dipuja dalam agama rakyat Tiongkok dan disebut 'Marsekal Altar Tengah' (三坛大会元帅) atau 'Pangeran Ketiga' (三太子).
claims.quote: Nezha is worshipped in Chinese folk religion and is called "Marshal of the Central Altar" (三坛大会元帅), or the "Third Prince" (三太子).

claims.statement: As in traditional folklore, Nezha flies around swiftly on his wind fire wheels, so he is also regarded as the tutelary god of many professional drivers, such as truck, taxi, or sightseeing-bus drivers.
claims.statement_id: Seperti dalam cerita rakyat tradisional, Nezha terbang cepat dengan roda angin-api (風火輪), sehingga ia juga dianggap dewa pelindung banyak pengemudi profesional, seperti sopir truk, taksi, atau bus wisata.
claims.quote: As in traditional folklore, Nezha flies around swiftly on his wind fire wheels, so he is also regarded as the tutelary god of many professional drivers, like trucks, taxis, or sightseeing bus drivers.

claims.statement: Nezha is also often regarded as the patron god of children and filial piety. Parents would make an offering to Nezha hoping their children would grow up strong, healthy, dutiful, and respectful.
claims.statement_id: Nezha juga sering dianggap dewa pelindung anak-anak dan bakti anak. Orang tua mempersembahkan sesaji kepada Nezha dengan harapan anak mereka tumbuh kuat, sehat, berbakti, dan hormat.
claims.quote: Nezha is also often regarded as the patron god of children and filial piety. Parents would make an offering to Nezha with the hope that their children would grow up strong, healthy, and be dutiful and respectful.

claims.statement: According to the description of Meir Shahar's book, the legend and cult of Nezha reach back over two thousand years to their origins in India, where Nezha began as a mythological being named Nalakūbara, whose sexual misadventures were celebrated in the Sanskrit epics as early as the first centuries BCE.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi buku Meir Shahar, legenda dan kultus Nezha dapat ditelusuri lebih dari dua ribu tahun ke asalnya di India, tempat Nezha bermula sebagai makhluk mitologis bernama Nalakūbara, yang petualangan seksualnya dirayakan dalam epos Sanskerta sejak abad-abad pertama SM.
claims.quote: Finally, the book offers a detailed history of the legend and the cult reaching back over two thousand years to its origins in India, where Nezha began as a mythological being named Nalakūbara, whose sexual misadventures were celebrated in the Sanskrit epics as early as the first centuries BCE.

claims.statement: According to the description of Shahar's book, the rebellious infant Nezha has been venerated in many ways by Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, and possessed spirit mediums.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi buku Shahar, Nezha sang bayi pemberontak dipuja dengan berbagai cara oleh biksu Buddha, pendeta Dao, dan perantara roh yang kerasukan.
claims.quote: Crossing the boundaries between China’s diverse religious traditions, it tracks the rebellious infant in the many ways he has been venerated by Buddhist monks, Daoist priests, and possessed spirit mediums

claims.statement: According to the description of Shahar's book, Nezha has been celebrated for over a millennium and is among the most formidable and enigmatic of all Chinese gods.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi buku Shahar, Nezha telah dimuliakan selama lebih dari seribu tahun dan termasuk dewa Tiongkok yang paling tangguh dan penuh teka-teki.
claims.quote: Celebrated for over a millennium, Nezha is among the most formidable and enigmatic of all Chinese gods.

claims.statement: Shahar argues that, despite a disastrous father-son relationship, Confucian ethics require the oedipal drive to masquerade as filial piety in Nezha's story, dictating that the child-god kill himself before trying to avenge himself on his father.
claims.statement_id: Shahar berpendapat bahwa, meski hubungan ayah-anak itu buruk, etika Konfusian menuntut dorongan oedipal menyamar sebagai bakti anak dalam kisah Nezha, sehingga sang dewa kecil bunuh diri sebelum mencoba membalas dendam kepada ayahnya.
claims.quote: Shahar argues that, despite a disastrous father-son relationship, Confucian ethics require that the oedipal drive masquerade as filial piety in Nezha’s story, dictating that the child-god kill himself before trying to avenge himself upon his father.

claims.statement: According to Meir Shahar, the name Nezha comes from Nalakuvara, depicted as a heroic yaksha general in the Mahamayuri.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Meir Shahar, nama Nezha berasal dari Nalakuvara, yang digambarkan sebagai jenderal yaksa heroik dalam Mahamayuri.
claims.quote: According to Meir Shahar, the name Nezha comes from Nalakuvara, depicted as a heroic yaksha general in the Mahamayuri.

claims.statement: The original variant 那羅鳩婆羅 changed to 捺羅俱跋羅, 那吒矩韈囉, and finally 那吒 (Nazha). Adding the 'mouth radical' (口) to Na (那) gives the current form Nezha (哪吒).
claims.statement_id: Bentuk asli 那羅鳩婆羅 berubah menjadi 捺羅俱跋羅, 那吒矩韈囉, dan akhirnya 那吒 (Nazha). Penambahan 'radikal mulut' (口) pada Na (那) mengubah nama menjadi bentuk sekarang, Nezha (哪吒).
claims.quote: The original variant 那羅鳩婆羅 changed to 捺羅俱跋羅, 那吒矩韈囉 and finally 那吒 (Nazha). The simple addition of the "mouth radical" (口) to Na (那) changes the name to the current form Nezha (哪吒).

claims.statement: In the novel Journey to the West, when the Heavenly King had this son, the character 'Ne' (哪) was on his left palm and 'zha' (吒) on his right palm, hence the name Nezha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Perjalanan ke Barat, ketika sang Raja Langit melahirkan putra ini, di telapak tangan kirinya ada aksara 'Ne' (哪) dan di telapak tangan kanannya aksara 'zha' (吒), sehingga ia dinamai Nezha.
claims.quote: 原來天王生此子時，他左手掌上有個「哪」字，右手掌上有個「吒」字，故名哪吒。

claims.statement: In the novel Fengshen Yanyi, Lady Yin was pregnant for three years and six months without giving birth, and Li Jing, worried, said that a pregnancy so long must mean a demon or a monster.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Fengshen Yanyi, Nyonya Yin mengandung selama tiga tahun enam bulan tanpa melahirkan, dan Li Jing cemas serta berkata bahwa kehamilan sepanjang itu pasti pertanda siluman atau makhluk aneh.
claims.quote: 殷夫人後又懷孕在身，已及三年零六個月，倘不生產。李靖時常心下憂疑，一日，指夫人之腹，言曰：「孕懷三載有餘，尚不降生，非妖即怪。」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing slashes a ball of flesh that turns like a wheel; it splits open and a small boy jumps out amid red light, with a face white as powder, a golden bracelet on his right hand, and a red silk cloth around his belly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing menebas sebuah bola daging yang berputar seperti roda; bola itu terbelah dan keluarlah seorang anak laki-laki dengan cahaya merah, bermuka putih, bergelang emas di tangan kanan, dan berselempang kain merah di perutnya.
claims.quote: 有一肉毬，滴溜溜圓轉如輪。李靖大驚，望肉毬上一劍砍去，劃然有聲。分開肉毬，跳出一個小孩兒來，滿地紅光，面如傅粉，右手套一金鐲，肚腹上圍著一塊紅綾，金光射目。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the narrator states that this divine being was born at Chentang Pass as an incarnation of Lingzhu Zi and as Jiang Ziya's vanguard; the golden bracelet is the Qiankun Quan (乾坤圈) and the red silk the Huntian Ling (混天綾), treasures of Jinguang Cave on Mount Qianyuan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, narator menyatakan bahwa dewa ini lahir di Chentang Pass sebagai penjelmaan Lingzhu Zi dan pembuka jalan bagi Jiang Ziya; gelang emasnya bernama Qiankun Quan (乾坤圈) dan kain merahnya Huntian Ling (混天綾), pusaka Gua Jinguang di Gunung Qianyuan.
claims.quote: 這位神聖下世，出在陳塘關，乃姜子牙先行官是也；靈珠子化身。金鐲是「乾坤圈」，紅綾名曰「混天綾。」此物乃是乾元山鎮金光洞之寶。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing names his three sons: Jinzha (a disciple of Wenshu Guangfa Tianzun) and Muzha (a disciple of Puxian Zhenren); the Daoist then names the third son 'Nezha'.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing menyebut ketiga putranya: Jinzha (murid Wenshu Guangfa Tianzun) dan Muzha (murid Puxian Zhenren); sang Daois lalu menamai putra ketiga 'Nezha'.
claims.quote: 李靖答曰：「不才有三子；長曰金吒，拜五龍山雲霄洞文殊廣法天尊為師；次曰木吒，拜九宮山白鶴洞普賢真人為師。老師既要此子為門下，但憑起一名諱，便拜道長為師。」道人曰：「此子第三，取名叫做『哪吒』。」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the Daoist introduces himself as Taiyi Zhenren of Jinguang Cave on Mount Qianyuan, who has come to congratulate Li Jing on the birth of his son.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, sang Daois memperkenalkan diri sebagai Taiyi Zhenren dari Gua Jinguang di Gunung Qianyuan, yang datang memberi selamat atas kelahiran putra Li Jing.
claims.quote: 貧道乃乾元山金光洞太乙真人是也。聞得將軍生了公子，特來賀喜。借令公子一看，不知尊意如何？

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha bathes in the Jiuwan River at the mouth of the East Sea and dips his treasure in the water; the water turns red, the river shakes, and the crystal palace rattles.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha mandi di Sungai Jiuwan di muara Laut Timur dengan mencelupkan pusakanya; air menjadi merah, sungai bergoyang, dan istana kristal ikut berguncang.
claims.quote: 不知這河是九灣河，是東海口上。哪吒將此寶放在水中，把水俱映紅了。擺一擺，江河晃動，搖一搖，乾坤動撼。那哪吒洗澡，不覺那水晶宮已愰的亂響。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha raises the Qiankun Quan into the air and it strikes the head of the patrolling yaksha Li Gen, who dies on the bank.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha mengangkat Qiankun Quan ke udara dan benda itu menimpa kepala yaksa pengintai Li Gen hingga ia tewas di tepi sungai.
claims.quote: 把右手套的乾坤圈望空中一舉。此寶原係崑崙山玉虛宮所賜太乙真人鎮金光洞之物，夜叉那裏經得起，那寶打將下來，正落在夜叉頭上，只打的腦漿迸流，即死於岸上。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha strikes the Dragon King's third son with the Qiankun Quan until his true form, a dragon, appears; he then pulls out its sinew to make a belt for his father.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha memukul putra ketiga Raja Naga dengan Qiankun Quan hingga wujud aslinya, seekor naga, tampak; ia lalu mencabut urat sang naga untuk dijadikan ikat pinggang bagi ayahnya.
claims.quote: 提起乾坤圈，照頂門一下，把三太子的元身打出，是一條龍，在地上挺直。哪吒曰：「打出這小龍的本像來了。也罷，把他的筋抽去，做一條龍筋絛與俺父親束甲。」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Ao Guang, furious, transforms into a scholar, goes to Chentang Pass, and announces himself as an old acquaintance come to visit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Ao Guang murka dan, setelah menjelma menjadi seorang terpelajar, pergi ke Chentang Pass dan mengumumkan dirinya sebagai kenalan lama yang berkunjung.
claims.quote: 敖光大怒，恨不能即與其子報仇，隨化一秀士，逕往陳塘關來。至於帥府，對門官曰：「你與我傳報，有故人敖光拜訪。」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha declares that he killed Ao Bing and Li Gen and must pay for it himself, says he is Lingzhu Zi, and says he will return his flesh and bones to his parents so that they are not burdened.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha menyatakan bahwa ia yang membunuh Ao Bing dan Li Gen sehingga ia sendiri yang harus menanggung akibatnya, mengaku sebagai Lingzhu Zi, dan berkata akan mengembalikan daging dan tulangnya kepada orang tuanya agar mereka tidak terbebani.
claims.quote: 『一人行事一人當』，我打死敖丙、李艮，我當償命，豈有子連累父母之理！」乃對敖光曰：「我一身非輕，乃靈珠子是也。奉玉虛符命，應運下世。我今日剖腹、剜腸、剔骨肉，還於父母，不累雙親。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha, sword in his right hand, cuts off an arm and then slits open his own belly; he dies, and the Dragon Kings report according to his words.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha dengan pedang di tangan kanan memotong sebelah lengannya lalu membelah perutnya sendiri; ia mati dan para Raja Naga melaporkan sesuai ucapannya.
claims.quote: 哪吒便右手提劍，先去一臂膊，後自剖其腹，剜腸剔骨，散了七魂三魄，一命歸泉。四龍王據哪吒之言回旨。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha's spirit has nothing to rest on; he was the manifestation of a treasure that borrowed essence and blood and so has a spirit, and he drifts on the wind to Mount Qianyuan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, roh Nezha tak punya tempat bersandar; ia berasal dari penjelmaan pusaka yang meminjam darah dan sari tubuh sehingga memiliki roh, dan ia melayang tertiup angin sampai ke Gunung Qianyuan.
claims.quote: 哪吒魂無所依，魄無所倚──他原是寶貝化現，借了精血，故有魂魄。哪吒飄飄蕩蕩，隨風而至，逕到乾元山來。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Taiyi Zhenren tells Nezha to appear in his mother's dream and ask for a shrine-palace (行宮) on Mount Cuiping, forty li from the pass; after receiving incense for three years he can return to the human world to assist the true ruler.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Taiyi Zhenren menyuruh Nezha menemui ibunya dalam mimpi dan meminta dibangunkan sebuah istana persinggahan (行宮) di Gunung Cuiping, empat puluh li dari pass itu; setelah menerima dupa selama tiga tahun ia dapat kembali ke dunia manusia untuk membantu sang penguasa sejati.
claims.quote: 真人吩咐哪吒：「此處非汝安身之所。你回到陳塘關，托一夢與你母親，離關四十里，有一翠屏山，山上有一空地，令你母親造一座哪吒行宮，你受香煙三載，又可立於人間，輔佐真主。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha manifests his power at Mount Cuiping; residents from near and far come with incense in growing numbers day by day, and prayers for blessings or the warding off of disaster are always answered.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha menampakkan kesaktian di Gunung Cuiping; penduduk dari dekat dan jauh berdatangan membawa dupa, makin ramai dari hari ke hari, dan doa memohon berkah atau penangkal bencana selalu terkabul.
claims.quote: 哪吒在翠屏山顯聖，四方遠近居民，俱來進香，紛紛如蟻，日盛一日，往往不斷。祈福禳災，無不感應。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing smashes Nezha's golden statue with a whip, kicks over the ghost-judge statues, and orders the temple burned.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Li Jing menghancurkan arca emas Nezha dengan cambuk, menendang roboh arca hakim hantu, dan memerintahkan agar kuil dibakar.
claims.quote: 罵罷，提六陳鞭，一鞭把哪吒金身打的粉碎。李靖怒發，復一腳蹬倒鬼判。傳令：「放火，燒了廟宇。」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, Taiyi Zhenren arranges lotus petals and lotus-leaf stalks into a body with three hundred joints of bone, then places a grain of golden elixir at its center.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Taiyi Zhenren menata kelopak teratai dan tangkai daun teratai menjadi tubuh dengan tiga ratus ruas tulang, lalu menaruh sebutir pil emas di tengahnya.
claims.quote: 真人將花勒下瓣兒，鋪成三才，又將荷葉梗兒折成三百骨節，三個荷葉，按上、中、下，按天、地、人。真人將一粒金丹放於居中

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the guards report that the third son stands on two wind-fire wheels and holds a fire-tipped spear.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, para pengawal melaporkan bahwa putra ketiga berdiri di atas dua roda angin-api dan memegang tombak berujung api.
claims.quote: 外面有三公子，腳踏風火二輪，手提火尖鎗，口稱老爺姓諱，不知何故，請老爺定奪。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, a Daoist drops a pagoda that traps Nezha and claps it so that fire breaks out inside and Nezha cries for mercy.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, seorang Daois menurunkan sebuah pagoda yang mengurung Nezha, lalu menepuknya hingga api berkobar di dalam dan Nezha berteriak minta ampun.
claims.quote: 只見祥雲繚繞，紫霧盤旋，一物往下落來，把哪吒罩在玲瓏塔裏。道人雙手在塔上一拍，塔裏火發，把哪吒燒的大叫：「饒命！」

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the Daoist turns out to have been invited by Taiyi Zhenren to temper Nezha's nature so that he acknowledges the father-son bond; later the father and three sons become sages in the flesh, and Li Jing is the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Daois itu ternyata diundang Taiyi Zhenren untuk menjinakkan watak Nezha agar mengakui ikatan ayah-anak; kemudian keempat ayah dan putra itu menjadi suci dengan tubuh jasmani, dan Li Jing menjadi Raja Langit Pembawa Pagoda.
claims.quote: 道人原是太乙真人請到此間磨哪吒之性，以認父子之情。後來父子四人，肉身成聖，托塔天王乃李靖也。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the closing verse of the chapter says that without Randeng's spiritual power the father and son could hardly have been reunited by the golden pagoda.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, syair penutup bab menyebut bahwa tanpa kekuatan gaib Randeng, ayah dan anak itu sulit rukun kembali berkat pagoda emas.
claims.quote: 黃金造就玲瓏塔，萬道毫光透九重。不是燃燈施法力，難教父子復相從。

claims.statement: In the novel Journey to the West, Nezha returns his flesh to his mother and his bones to his father, his spirit goes to plead with the Buddha in the Western Paradise, and the Buddha revives him with lotus root for bones and lotus leaf for clothing.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Perjalanan ke Barat, Nezha mengembalikan daging kepada ibu dan tulang kepada ayah, rohnya pergi memohon kepada Buddha di Surga Barat, dan Buddha menghidupkannya kembali dengan akar teratai sebagai tulang dan daun teratai sebagai pakaian.
claims.quote: 割肉還母，剔骨還父，還了父精母血。一點靈魂，徑到西方極樂世界告佛。佛正與眾菩薩講經，只聞得幢幡寶蓋有人叫道：「救命！」佛慧眼一看，知是哪吒之魂，即將碧藕為骨，荷葉為衣，念動起死回生真言，哪吒遂得了性命。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, the Tathagata gives the father a golden pagoda with Buddhas on every level and tells Nezha to take the Buddha as his father, ending the grudge; this is why Li Tianwang is called the Pagoda-Bearer.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, Rulai (Buddha) memberi sang ayah sebuah pagoda emas yang berlapis-lapis Buddha dan menyuruh Nezha menganggap Buddha sebagai ayah sehingga dendam selesai; inilah asal gelar Li Tianwang Pembawa Pagoda.
claims.quote: 如來以和為尚，賜他一座玲瓏剔透舍利子如意黃金寶塔。那塔上層層有佛，豔豔光明。喚哪吒以佛為父，解釋了冤仇。所以稱為托塔李天王者，此也。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, after being revived Nezha uses his divine power to subdue ninety-six caves of demons, and later wants to kill the Heavenly King to avenge having stripped his own bones.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, setelah hidup kembali Nezha memakai kekuatan gaibnya untuk menaklukkan sembilan puluh enam gua siluman, dan kemudian hendak membunuh sang Raja Langit untuk membalas dendam atas tulangnya yang dikupas.
claims.quote: 運用神力，法降九十六洞妖魔，神通廣大。後來要殺天王，報那剔骨之仇。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, the Pagoda-Bearing Heavenly King Li Jing and Third Prince Nezha volunteer to subdue the 'monster' Sun Wukong; the Jade Emperor appoints Li Jing Great Marshal Subduer of Demons and Nezha Great Deity of the Three Altars' Sea Assembly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, Raja Langit Li Jing dan Pangeran Ketiga Nezha mengajukan diri menaklukkan 'siluman' Sun Wukong; Kaisar Giok mengangkat Li Jing sebagai Marsekal Penakluk Iblis dan Nezha sebagai Dewa Agung Haihui Tiga Altar.
claims.quote: 班部中閃上托塔李天王與哪吒三太子，越班奏上道：「萬歲，微臣不才，請旨降此妖怪。」玉帝大喜，即封托塔天王李靖為降魔大元帥，哪吒三太子為三壇海會大神，即刻興師下界。

claims.statement: In Journey to the West, Nezha shouts 'Change!' and becomes three-headed and six-armed, holding six weapons: a demon-slaying sword, a demon-cutting blade, a demon-binding rope, a demon-subduing pestle, an embroidered ball, and a fire wheel.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Perjalanan ke Barat, Nezha berteriak 'Berubah!' dan menjadi bertiga kepala berenam lengan, memegang enam senjata: pedang pembasmi siluman, golok pemotong siluman, tali pengikat siluman, pentungan penakluk siluman, bola bersulam, dan roda api.
claims.quote: 那哪吒奮怒，大喝一聲，叫：「變！」即變做三頭六臂，惡狠狠，手持著六般兵器，乃是斬妖劍、砍妖刀、縛妖索、降妖杵、繡毬兒、火輪兒，丫丫叉叉，撲面來打。

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in the Yuan-dynasty Sanjiao Soushen Daquan (Complete Collection of Deities of the Three Religions), before his reincarnation into the mortal realm Nezha was a great immortal under the Jade Emperor who wears a golden wheel around his head, has three heads, nine eyes, and eight arms, and can blow azure clouds out of his mouth.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Sanjiao Soushen Daquan (Kumpulan Lengkap Dewa Tiga Ajaran) zaman Yuan, sebelum menjelma ke dunia fana Nezha adalah dewa agung di bawah Kaisar Giok yang mengenakan roda emas di kepala, bertiga kepala, bermata sembilan, bertangan delapan, dan dapat mengembuskan awan biru dari mulutnya.
claims.quote: In the Yuan dynasty Sanjiao Soushen Daquan (Complete Collection of Deities of the Three Religions), prior to his reincarnation into the mortal realm, Nezha was a great immortal under the Jade Emperor, who wears a golden wheel around his head, has three heads, nine eyes, and eight arms, and can blow azure clouds out of his mouth.

claims.statement: In popular culture, Nezha's killing of Li Gen and Ao Bing is often seen as a result of Ao Guang demanding young boys and girls from Chentang Pass as sacrifices.
claims.statement_id: Dalam budaya populer, pembunuhan Li Gen dan Ao Bing oleh Nezha sering dipandang sebagai akibat Ao Guang menuntut anak laki-laki dan perempuan dari Chentang Pass sebagai korban persembahan.
claims.quote: In popular culture, Nezha's killing of Li Gen and Ao Bing is often seen as a result of Ao Guang demanding young boys and girls from Chentang Pass as sacrifices.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, the plot described just before (the demand for sacrifices and the flood threat) is found only in the 1979 Shanghai Animation Film Studio movie Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, and not in the Fengshen Yanyi novel or Qing-dynasty opera adaptations.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, alur yang dijelaskan sebelumnya (tuntutan korban dan ancaman banjir) hanya ditemukan dalam film Shanghai Animation Film Studio tahun 1979, Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, dan tidak ada dalam novel Fengshen Yanyi maupun adaptasi opera zaman Qing.
claims.quote: The above plot is only found in the 1979 Shanghai Animation Film Studio movie, Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, and not in the Fengshen Yanyi novel or Qing dynasty opera adaptations.

claims.statement: The character increased in popularity in 1979 with the animated feature film Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, which was screened at the 1980 Cannes Film Festival and is considered one of the great classic works of Chinese animation.
claims.statement_id: Popularitas tokoh ini meningkat pada 1979 dengan film animasi panjang Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, yang diputar di Festival Film Cannes 1980 dan dianggap salah satu karya klasik besar animasi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The character increased in popularity in 1979 with the animated feature film Nezha Conquers the Dragon King, which was screened at the 1980 Cannes Film Festival and is considered one of the great classic works of Chinese animation.

claims.statement: On 26 July 2019, another animated feature film, Ne Zha, was more successful, setting numerous all-time box-office records, including third-highest-grossing of all films in China and highest-grossing animated film from outside the United States.
claims.statement_id: Pada 26 Juli 2019, film animasi panjang lain, Ne Zha, lebih sukses dan memecahkan banyak rekor pendapatan sepanjang masa, termasuk film berpendapatan tertinggi ketiga di Tiongkok dan film animasi berpendapatan tertinggi dari luar Amerika Serikat.
claims.quote: On 26 July 2019, another animated feature film, Ne Zha, was more successful, setting numerous all-time records for box-office grosses, including third-highest-grossing of all films in China and highest-grossing animated film from outside the United States.

claims.statement: A sequel, Ne Zha 2 (2025), set further box-office records, becoming the highest-grossing film in China, the highest-grossing non-English-language film of all time, and the highest-grossing animated movie of all time.
claims.statement_id: Sekuelnya, Ne Zha 2 (2025), mencetak rekor pendapatan lebih jauh, menjadi film berpendapatan tertinggi di Tiongkok, film berbahasa non-Inggris berpendapatan tertinggi sepanjang masa, dan film animasi berpendapatan tertinggi sepanjang masa.
claims.quote: A sequel, Ne Zha 2 (2025), set further box office records, becoming the highest-grossing film in China, and the highest grossing non-English language film of all time, and the highest grossing animated movie of all time.

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, in Journey to the West Nezha fought the Monkey King Sun Wukong when the latter rebelled against the Jade Emperor; they later became friends.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, dalam Perjalanan ke Barat Nezha bertarung melawan Raja Kera Sun Wukong ketika yang terakhir memberontak melawan Kaisar Giok; keduanya kemudian menjadi teman.
claims.quote: He fought the Monkey King, Sun Wukong, when the latter rebelled against the Jade Emperor. They later became friends.

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Fengshen Yanyi (封神演義), commonly called Fengshen Bang, is a Chinese novel of gods and demons whose author is given as Chen Zhonglin (or Xu Zhonglin) of the Ming dynasty.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Fengshen Yanyi (封神演義), yang biasa disebut Fengshen Bang, adalah novel dewa-iblis Tiongkok; pengarangnya disebut Chen Zhonglin (atau Xu Zhonglin) dari Dinasti Ming.
claims.quote: 《封神演義》，一般俗稱《封神榜》，又名《商周列國全傳》、《武王伐紂外史》、《封神傳》。是一部中國神魔小說，作者是明朝的陳仲琳（或許仲琳）

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Fengshen Yanyi was roughly completed in the Longqing and Wanli periods; it has one hundred chapters and is set against Jiang Ziya helping the house of Zhou (King Wen and King Wu) attack the Shang tyrant.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Fengshen Yanyi kira-kira rampung ditulis pada masa Longqing dan Wanli; novel ini terdiri dari seratus bab dengan latar Jiang Ziya membantu wangsa Zhou (Raja Wen dan Raja Wu) menyerang Zhou raja Shang.
claims.quote: 約成書於隆慶、萬曆年間。全書共一百回，以姜子牙輔佐周室（周文王、周武王）討伐商紂的歷史為背景

claims.statement: According to the Wikisource introduction, Xiyouji (Journey to the West) is a long Chinese mythological novel of the Ming dynasty, written in classical vernacular, in 100 chapters.
claims.statement_id: Menurut pengantar Wikisource, Xiyouji (Perjalanan ke Barat) adalah novel mitologi panjang dari zaman Dinasti Ming, ditulis dalam bahasa lisan klasik dengan 100 bab.
claims.quote: 《西遊記》是中國明代長篇神話小說，古代白話寫成。全書20卷100回。

claims.statement: In Fengshen Yanyi, the revived Nezha rebukes Li Jing for whipping his golden statue and burning his shrine-palace on Mount Cuiping, then thrusts his spear at Li Jing's head to avenge that one lash.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fengshen Yanyi, Nezha yang sudah hidup kembali menegur Li Jing karena mencambuk arca emasnya dan membakar istana persinggahannya di Gunung Cuiping, lalu menusukkan tombaknya ke arah kepala Li Jing untuk membalas dendam atas satu cambukan itu.
claims.quote: 哪吒曰：「李靖！我骨肉已交還與你，我與你無干礙，你為何往翠屏山鞭打我的金身，火燒我的行宮？今日拿你，報一鞭之恨！」把鎗愰一愰，劈腦刺來。

claims.statement: According to the book description, Meir Shahar recounts Nezha's riveting tale, which culminates in suicide and attempted patricide, and uncovers hidden tensions in the Chinese family system.
claims.statement_id: Menurut deskripsi buku, Meir Shahar menceritakan kisah Nezha yang memikat, yang berpuncak pada bunuh diri dan percobaan membunuh ayah, serta mengungkap ketegangan tersembunyi dalam sistem keluarga Tiongkok.
claims.quote: In this theoretically informed study Meir Shahar recounts Nezha’s riveting tale—which culminates in suicide and attempted patricide—and uncovers hidden tensions in the Chinese family system.
