claims.statement: In the novel, when Jonathan Harker addresses him as Count Dracula, the Count replies that he is Dracula and welcomes Harker to his house.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel, ketika Jonathan Harker menyapanya sebagai Count Dracula, sang Count menjawab bahwa ia adalah Dracula dan menyambut Harker di rumahnya.
claims.quote: “Count Dracula?” He bowed in a courtly way as he replied:— “I am Dracula; and I bid you welcome, Mr. Harker, to my house.

claims.statement: Harker sees a tall old man, clean shaven except for a long white moustache, clad in black from head to foot.
claims.statement_id: Harker melihat seorang lelaki tua yang tinggi, tercukur bersih kecuali kumis putih panjang, dan berpakaian hitam dari kepala sampai kaki.
claims.quote: Within, stood a tall old man, clean shaven save for a long white moustache, and clad in black from head to foot, without a single speck of colour about him anywhere.

claims.statement: Harker notes the Count's strongly aquiline face, peculiarly sharp white teeth protruding over the lips, pale ears extremely pointed at the tops, and a general effect of extraordinary pallor.
claims.statement_id: Harker mencatat wajah sang Count yang sangat berhidung bengkok, gigi putih yang sangat runcing dan menonjol di atas bibir, telinga pucat yang sangat runcing di bagian atas, dan kesan umum berupa kepucatan luar biasa.
claims.quote: His face was a strong—a very strong—aquiline, with high bridge of the thin nose and peculiarly arched nostrils ... with peculiarly sharp white teeth; these protruded over the lips ... his ears were pale, and at the tops extremely pointed ... The general effect was one of extraordinary pallor.

claims.statement: Harker notes hairs in the centre of the Count's palm, and nails that are long and fine and cut to a sharp point.
claims.statement_id: Harker mencatat ada rambut di tengah telapak tangan sang Count, dan kukunya panjang, halus, dan dipotong runcing.
claims.quote: Strange to say, there were hairs in the centre of the palm. The nails were long and fine, and cut to a sharp point.

claims.statement: As wolves howl, the Count's eyes gleam and he tells Harker to listen to "the children of the night".
claims.statement_id: Saat serigala melolong, mata sang Count berkilat dan ia berkata agar Harker mendengarkan "anak-anak malam" itu.
claims.quote: the howling of many wolves. The Count’s eyes gleamed, and he said:— “Listen to them—the children of the night. What music they make!”

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, Jonathan never saw the Count eat, and the Count throws no shadow and makes no reflection in the mirror.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, Jonathan tidak pernah melihat sang Count makan, sang Count tidak berbayang, dan tidak tampak pantulannya di cermin.
claims.quote: Even friend Jonathan, who lived with him for weeks, did never see him to eat, never! He throws no shadow; he make in the mirror no reflect, as again Jonathan observe.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, the Count can transform himself into a wolf, a bat, and a mist that he creates, as he gathers from the ship's arrival in Whitby.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, sang Count dapat berubah menjadi serigala, kelelawar, dan kabut yang ia ciptakan; ia menarik kesimpulan itu dari kedatangan kapal di Whitby.
claims.quote: He can transform himself to wolf, as we gather from the ship arrival in Whitby, when he tear open the dog; he can be as bat, as Madam Mina saw him on the window at Whitby ... He can come in mist which he create

claims.statement: Van Helsing reminds the others that the Count has the strength of twenty men and that his neck is not amenable to mere strength.
claims.statement_id: Van Helsing mengingatkan bahwa sang Count memiliki kekuatan dua puluh orang dan lehernya tidak dapat dilumpuhkan dengan kekuatan biasa.
claims.quote: Remember that he has the strength of twenty men, and that, though our necks or our windpipes are of the common kind—and therefore breakable or crushable—his are not amenable to mere strength.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, within his range the Count can direct the storm, the fog and the thunder, command the rat, the owl, the bat, the moth, the fox and the wolf, grow and become small, and at times vanish and come unknown.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, dalam jangkauannya sang Count dapat mengarahkan badai, kabut, dan guntur, memerintah tikus, burung hantu, kelelawar, ngengat, rubah, dan serigala, menjadi kecil, dan kadang-kadang lenyap serta datang tanpa diketahui.
claims.quote: he can, within his range, direct the elements; the storm, the fog, the thunder; he can command all the meaner things: the rat, and the owl, and the bat—the moth, and the fox, and the wolf; he can grow and become small; and he can at times vanish and come unknown.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, the Count may not enter anywhere at first unless someone of the household bids him to come, and his power ceases at the coming of the day.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, pada mulanya sang Count tidak boleh masuk ke mana pun kecuali ada penghuni rumah yang mengundangnya, dan kekuatannya berhenti ketika siang tiba.
claims.quote: He may not enter anywhere at the first, unless there be some one of the household who bid him to come; though afterwards he can come as he please. His power ceases, as does that of all evil things, at the coming of the day.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, if the Count is not at the place he is bound for, he can only change himself at noon or at exact sunrise or sunset.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, jika sang Count tidak berada di tempat tujuannya, ia hanya dapat mengubah dirinya pada tengah hari atau tepat saat matahari terbit atau terbenam.
claims.quote: If he be not at the place whither he is bound, he can only change himself at noon or at exact sunrise or sunset.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, the vampire lives on and cannot die by the mere passing of time, flourishes when he can fatten on the blood of the living, and can even grow younger.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, vampir terus hidup dan tidak dapat mati hanya karena berlalunya waktu, ia berkembang bila memangsa darah makhluk hidup, dan bahkan dapat menjadi lebih muda.
claims.quote: The vampire live on, and cannot die by mere passing of the time; he can flourish when that he can fatten on the blood of the living. Even more, we have seen amongst us that he can even grow younger

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, those who become Un-Dead receive the curse of immortality, and all who die from the preying of the Un-Dead become Un-Dead themselves and prey on their kind.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, mereka yang menjadi Un-Dead menerima kutukan keabadian, dan semua yang mati karena dimangsa Un-Dead menjadi Un-Dead juga dan memangsa sesamanya.
claims.quote: When they become such, there comes with the change the curse of immortality; they cannot die, but must go on age after age adding new victims and multiplying the evils of the world; for all that die from the preying of the Un-Dead becomes themselves Un-Dead, and prey on their kind.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, to sacred things such as the crucifix the Count is nothing, and in their presence he takes his place far off and silent with respect.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, terhadap benda suci seperti salib sang Count tidak berarti apa-apa, dan di hadapannya ia menyingkir jauh dengan diam dan hormat.
claims.quote: as for things sacred, as this symbol, my crucifix, that was amongst us even now when we resolve, to them he is nothing, but in their presence he take his place far off and silent with respect.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, a branch of wild rose on his coffin keeps him from moving from it, a sacred bullet fired into the coffin kills him so that he is truly dead, and the stake through him or the cut-off head gives rest.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, cabang mawar liar pada peti menahannya agar tidak beranjak dari sana, peluru suci yang ditembakkan ke peti membunuhnya sungguh-sungguh, dan pancang atau kepala yang dipenggal memberinya ketenangan.
claims.quote: The branch of wild rose on his coffin keep him that he move not from it; a sacred bullet fired into the coffin kill him so that he be true dead; and as for the stake through him, we know already of its peace; or the cut-off head that giveth rest.

claims.statement: Harker finds the Count lying in one of fifty great boxes on a pile of newly dug earth, and cannot say whether he is dead or asleep.
claims.statement_id: Harker menemukan sang Count terbaring di salah satu dari lima puluh peti besar, di atas tumpukan tanah yang baru digali, dan ia tidak dapat memastikan apakah sang Count mati atau tidur.
claims.quote: There, in one of the great boxes, of which there were fifty in all, on a pile of newly dug earth, lay the Count! He was either dead or asleep, I could not say which

claims.statement: The Russian schooner from Varna called the Demeter carries only a small cargo of a number of great wooden boxes filled with mould.
claims.statement_id: Kapal layar Rusia dari Varna bernama Demeter membawa muatan sedikit berupa sejumlah peti kayu besar berisi tanah gembur.
claims.quote: It turns out that the schooner is a Russian from Varna, and is called the Demeter. She is almost entirely in ballast of silver sand, with only a small amount of cargo—a number of great wooden boxes filled with mould.

claims.statement: The instant the ship touched the shore, an immense dog sprang up on deck and jumped onto the sand, making straight for the steep cliff where the churchyard hangs over the laneway.
claims.statement_id: Begitu kapal menyentuh pantai, seekor anjing besar melompat naik ke geladak lalu ke pasir, dan berlari lurus menuju tebing curam tempat pemakaman gereja menggantung di atas jalan setapak.
claims.quote: the very instant the shore was touched, an immense dog sprang up on deck from below ... jumped from the bow on the sand. Making straight for the steep cliff, where the churchyard hangs over the laneway to the East Pier

claims.statement: Harker again sees the Count go out in lizard fashion, moving downwards in a sidelong way some hundred feet down and a good deal to the left.
claims.statement_id: Harker kembali melihat sang Count keluar dengan cara seperti cicak, bergerak ke bawah menyamping sekitar seratus kaki dan agak jauh ke kiri.
claims.quote: Once more have I seen the Count go out in his lizard fashion. He moved downwards in a sidelong way, some hundred feet down, and a good deal to the left.

claims.statement: According to Van Helsing, citing Arminius, the Draculas were a great and noble race, some of whose scions were held to have had dealings with the Evil One and learned his secrets in the Scholomance amongst the mountains over Lake Hermanstadt.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Van Helsing, mengutip Arminius, keluarga Dracula adalah bangsa yang agung dan mulia, dan sebagian keturunannya dianggap berurusan dengan si Jahat serta mempelajari rahasianya di Scholomance di pegunungan di atas Danau Hermanstadt.
claims.quote: The Draculas were, says Arminius, a great and noble race, though now and again were scions who were held by their coevals to have had dealings with the Evil One. They learned his secrets in the Scholomance, amongst the mountains over Lake Hermanstadt

claims.statement: Van Helsing concludes that the Count must have been that Voivode Dracula who won his name against the Turk, over the great river on the very frontier of Turkey-land.
claims.statement_id: Van Helsing menyimpulkan bahwa sang Count pastilah Voivode Dracula yang memenangkan namanya melawan bangsa Turki di seberang sungai besar di perbatasan negeri Turki.
claims.quote: He must, indeed, have been that Voivode Dracula who won his name against the Turk, over the great river on the very frontier of Turkey-land.

claims.statement: Harker finds that the district the Count named lies in the extreme east of the country, on the borders of Transylvania, Moldavia and Bukovina, in the midst of the Carpathian mountains, one of the wildest and least known portions of Europe.
claims.statement_id: Harker mendapati bahwa wilayah yang disebut sang Count berada di ujung timur negeri itu, di perbatasan Transylvania, Moldavia, dan Bukovina, di tengah Pegunungan Karpatia, salah satu bagian Eropa yang paling liar dan paling kurang dikenal.
claims.quote: I find that the district he named is in the extreme east of the country, just on the borders of three states, Transylvania, Moldavia and Bukovina, in the midst of the Carpathian mountains; one of the wildest and least known portions of Europe.

claims.statement: Jonathan's great knife shears through the Count's throat and Mr. Morris's bowie knife plunges into his heart, and the whole body crumbles into dust and passes from sight.
claims.statement_id: Pisau besar Jonathan menebas leher sang Count dan pisau bowie Mr. Morris menembus jantungnya, lalu seluruh tubuhnya hancur menjadi debu dan lenyap dari pandangan.
claims.quote: But, on the instant, came the sweep and flash of Jonathan’s great knife. I shrieked as I saw it shear through the throat; whilst at the same moment Mr. Morris’s bowie knife plunged into the heart. It was like a miracle; but before our very eyes, and almost in the drawing of a breath, the whole body crumbled into dust and passed from our sight.

claims.statement: The Count tells Harker that the Székelys have a right to be proud because in their veins flows the blood of many brave races.
claims.statement_id: Sang Count berkata kepada Harker bahwa kaum Székely berhak bangga karena dalam urat mereka mengalir darah banyak bangsa pemberani.
claims.quote: “We Szekelys have a right to be proud, for in our veins flows the blood of many brave races who fought as the lion fights, for lordship.

claims.statement: Van Helsing says the nosferatu do not die like the bee that stings once but only grow stronger, with yet more power to work evil.
claims.statement_id: Van Helsing mengatakan bahwa nosferatu tidak mati seperti lebah yang menyengat sekali, melainkan menjadi lebih kuat dan lebih berkuasa untuk berbuat jahat.
claims.quote: The nosferatu do not die like the bee when he sting once. He is only stronger; and being stronger, have yet more power to work evil.

claims.statement: Dracula, by Abraham Stoker, who generally published under the abbreviated first name Bram, was first published in Great Britain in 1897.
claims.statement_id: Dracula karya Abraham Stoker, yang biasanya menerbitkan karya dengan nama depan singkat Bram, pertama kali terbit di Britania Raya pada 1897.
claims.quote: Dracula, by Abraham Stoker—who generally published under the abbreviated first name Bram—was first published in Great Britain in 1897.

claims.statement: Although myths and legends about vampires had existed since ancient times, Stoker's novel synthesized much of this lore and gave it a palpable feeling in the character of Count Dracula.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun mitos dan legenda tentang vampir sudah ada sejak zaman kuno, novel Stoker merangkum banyak kisah itu dan memberinya wujud nyata dalam tokoh Count Dracula.
claims.quote: Although myths and legends about vampires had existed since ancient times, Stoker's novel synthesized much of this lore and gave it a palpable feeling in the character of Count Dracula.

claims.statement: According to this character summary, Dracula has limited motion during the day, consumes only human blood, must pass over water in certain ways, has no reflection, must sleep on soil from his own land, has power over certain animals and weather, and can turn others into vampires.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ringkasan tokoh ini, sang Count bergerak terbatas pada siang hari, hanya meminum darah manusia, harus melintasi air dengan cara tertentu, tidak berpantulan, harus tidur di atas tanah dari negerinya sendiri, berkuasa atas hewan dan cuaca tertentu, serta dapat mengubah orang lain menjadi vampir.
claims.quote: Dracula has limited motion during the day, consumes only human blood, must pass over water in certain ways, has no reflection, must sleep on soil from his own land, has power over certain animals and weather, and has the power to turn others into vampires.

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia.com, most critics agree that Dracula was based in part on a historical figure, Vlad the Impaler, a fifteenth-century Romanian ruler known for his indiscriminate brutality.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia.com, sebagian besar kritikus sepakat bahwa Dracula sebagian didasarkan pada tokoh sejarah Vlad si Penusuk, penguasa Rumania abad kelima belas yang dikenal karena kekejamannya.
claims.quote: However, most critics agree that Dracula was based in part on a historical figure, Vlad the Impaler, a fifteenth-century Romanian ruler known for his indiscriminate brutality

claims.statement: Films, most notably the 1931 film Dracula starring Bela Lugosi, have overshadowed the book, but have also helped to keep the story alive.
claims.statement_id: Film, terutama film Dracula 1931 yang dibintangi Bela Lugosi, telah membayangi novelnya, tetapi juga membantu menjaga kisahnya tetap hidup.
claims.quote: While films, most notably the 1931 film Dracula, starring Bela Lugosi, have overshadowed the book, they have also helped to keep the story alive.

claims.statement: Count Dracula is a fictional character and the title antagonist of Bram Stoker's gothic horror novel Dracula (1897), considered the prototypical and archetypal vampire in subsequent works of fiction.
claims.statement_id: Count Dracula adalah tokoh fiksi dan antagonis utama novel horor gotik Dracula (1897) karya Bram Stoker, dan dianggap vampir purwarupa dan arketipal dalam karya fiksi sesudahnya.
claims.quote: is a fictional character and title antagonist of Bram Stoker's gothic horror novel Dracula (1897). He is considered the prototypical and archetypal vampire in subsequent works of fiction.

claims.statement: Count Dracula is an undead, centuries-old vampire and a Transylvanian nobleman who claims to be a Székely descended from Attila the Hun, and he inhabits a decaying castle in the Carpathian Mountains near the Borgo Pass.

claims.quote: They all lay in stone houses in Their great city of R’lyeh, preserved by the spells of mighty Cthulhu for a glorious resurrection when the stars and the earth might once more be ready for Them.

claims.statement: The cult remains hidden until the time when the great priest Cthulhu, from his dark house in the mighty city of R'lyeh under the waters, should rise and bring the earth again beneath his sway.

claims.quote: until the time when the great priest Cthulhu, from his dark house in the mighty city of R’lyeh under the waters, should rise and bring the earth again beneath his sway.

claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita, para Great Old Ones berbicara kepada orang-orang peka dengan membentuk mimpi mereka, karena hanya begitu bahasa mereka dapat mencapai pikiran berdaging mamalia.
claims.quote: the Great Old Ones spoke to the sensitive among them by molding their dreams; for only thus could Their language reach the fleshly minds of mammals.

claims.statement: The Thing of the idols, the green, sticky spawn of the stars, had awaked to claim his own; the stars were right again and after vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again and ravening for delight.
claims.statement_id: Benda dari arca-arca itu, keturunan bintang yang hijau dan lengket, terbangun untuk menuntut miliknya; bintang-bintang kembali tepat dan setelah vigintillions tahun Cthulhu yang agung lepas lagi dan rakus akan kesenangan.
claims.quote: The Thing of the idols, the green, sticky spawn of the stars, had awaked to claim his own. The stars were right again ... After vigintillions of years great Cthulhu was loose again, and ravening for delight.

claims.quote: The Thing can not be described—there is no language for such abysms of shrieking and immemorial lunacy, such eldritch contradictions of all matter, force, and cosmic order. A mountain walked or stumbled.

claims.statement: Great Cthulhu slid greasily into the water and began to pursue with vast wave-raising strokes of cosmic potency.
claims.statement_id: Cthulhu yang agung meluncur licin ke dalam air dan mulai mengejar dengan ayunan besar yang menimbulkan gelombang dengan daya kosmik.
claims.quote: great Cthulhu slid greasily into the water and began to pursue with vast wave-raising strokes of cosmic potency.

claims.quote: That cult would never die till the stars came right again, and the secret priests would take great Cthulhu from His tomb to revive His subjects and resume His rule of earth.

claims.statement: Corbacho Carrobles states that Lovecraft's style is no longer considered Gothic but cosmic horror, because the terror in his tales relates to alien entities from beyond human understanding rather than to ghosts.
claims.statement_id: Corbacho Carrobles menyatakan bahwa gaya Lovecraft tidak lagi dianggap Gotik melainkan kengerian kosmik, karena teror dalam kisahnya berkaitan dengan entitas asing dari luar pemahaman manusia, bukan hantu.
claims.quote: The style in which Lovecraft writes is no longer considered Gothic, but cosmic horror. The main reasons are mainly that the terror depicted in Lovecraft's tales is not focused on ghosts or that sort of creatures, but rather it is related to alien entities from beyond human understanding.

claims.statement: Corbacho Carrobles writes that the Mythos monsters originate outside time and space and always stand for humanity's frailty and insignificance.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Corbacho Carrobles, monster dalam Cthulhu Mythos datang dari luar waktu dan ruang dan selalu dipakai untuk melambangkan kerapuhan dan ketidakberartian umat manusia.
claims.quote: The monsters in the Cthulhu Mythos come from beyond time and space and are always used to represent the feebleness and meaninglessness of mankind.

claims.statement: Corbacho Carrobles calls these creatures hybrid beings, like Cthulhu, a grotesque amalgam of different concepts, never easy to define or categorize, designed to create ambiguity.
claims.statement_id: Corbacho Carrobles menyebut makhluk-makhluk itu sebagai makhluk campuran, seperti Cthulhu, perpaduan ganjil dari berbagai konsep yang tidak mudah ditakrifkan atau digolongkan dan dirancang untuk menciptakan ambiguitas.
claims.quote: They are hybrid beings, as Cthulhu, a grotesque amalgam of different concepts, never easy to define or categorize, designed to create ambiguity

claims.statement_id: Menurut Corbacho Carrobles, Cthulhu adalah makhluk paling dikenal dari panteon rekaan Lovecraft, dan siluet makhluk raksasa mirip naga berkepala gembung yang bangkit dari kedalaman adalah citra utama dalam segala karya yang terinspirasi Lovecraft.
claims.quote: Cthulhu, being the best known creature from Lovecraft's imaginary pantheon, is almost a coat of arms for anything branded after him. The sinister silhouette of a gargantuan dragon-like creature with a pulpy head rising from the depths is the main image to be found in anything inspired by Lovecraft's works

claims.quote: The climax of the tale unveils during its last part, with the words of the late Sailor Gustaf Johansen as we learn that the dreams of the artist begin at the very same time as earthquakes and storms made the ancient tomb city of Cthulhu, R'lyeh, arise from the depths.

claims.statement: The weird tales of the Cthulhu Mythos have become the axis not only for a never-ending number of tales by renowned authors but also for video-games, films, role-playing games, and graphic novels.

claims.quote: The weird tales of the Cthulhu Mythos have become the axis for, not only a never ending amount of tales from renowned authors, but also for video-games, films, role-playing games, or graphic novels.

claims.statement: The research concerns H.P. Lovecraft's most renowned tale, The Call of Cthulhu, and its adaptations into contemporary comics and graphic novels, in particular the one by the Swiss writer and artist Michael Zigerlig.
claims.statement_id: Penelitian ini membahas kisah paling terkenal karya H.P. Lovecraft, The Call of Cthulhu, dan adaptasinya ke dalam komik dan novel grafis kontemporer, khususnya karya penulis dan seniman Swiss Michael Zigerlig.
claims.quote: My research involves the most renowned tale by the master of modern horror H.P. Lovecraft, The call of Cthulhu, and its adaptations into contemporary comics and graphic novels, in particular the one by Swiss writer/artist Michael Zigerlig.

claims.statement: Corbacho Carrobles notes that it is through nightmares that the creature gets in touch with the people of the world, as we understand when reading the tale.

claims.quote: And it is through nightmares that the creature gets in touch with the people of the world as we understand when reading the tale.

claims.statement: Cthulhu is a fictional cosmic entity created by writer H. P. Lovecraft, introduced in his short story "The Call of Cthulhu", published by the American pulp magazine Weird Tales in 1928.

claims.statement: Considered a Great Old One within the pantheon of Lovecraftian cosmic entities, Cthulhu is depicted as a gigantic entity worshipped by cultists, in a green humanoid form incorporating visual elements similar to an octopus and dragon.

claims.quote: Considered a Great Old One within the pantheon of Lovecraftian cosmic entities, he is depicted as a gigantic entity worshipped by cultists, in a green humanoid form incorporating visual elements similar to an octopus and dragon.

claims.statement: The name Cthulhu was invented by Lovecraft in 1926 and was probably chosen to echo the word chthonic (Ancient Greek "of the earth").
claims.statement_id: Nama Cthulhu diciptakan Lovecraft pada 1926 dan kemungkinan dipilih untuk menggemakan kata chthonic (Yunani Kuno "dari bumi").
claims.quote: Invented by Lovecraft in 1926, the name Cthulhu was probably chosen to echo the word chthonic (Ancient Greek "of the earth")

claims.quote: Cthulhu is said to be hundreds of meters tall, with webbed, human-looking arms and legs. Its head is depicted as similar to the entirety of a gigantic octopus, with an unknown number of tentacles surrounding its supposed mouth.

claims.statement: His age is described as at least "vigintillions of years", and he is also said to have cast spells which preserved the Great Old Ones until their reawakening.
claims.statement_id: Usianya digambarkan paling sedikit "vigintillions of years", dan ia juga disebut telah melontarkan mantra yang mengawetkan Great Old Ones sampai kebangkitan mereka.
claims.quote: His age is described to be at least "vigintillions of years". He is also said to have cast spells which preserved the Great Old Ones until their reawakening.

claims.quote: is also the object of worship, both by many human cults (including some within New Zealand, Greenland, Louisiana, and the Chinese mountains) and by other Lovecraftian monsters (called Deep Ones and Mi-Go).

claims.quote: August Derleth, a correspondent of Lovecraft's, used the creature's name to identify the system of lore employed by Lovecraft and his literary successors, the Cthulhu Mythos.

claims.quote: According to Derleth's scheme, "Great Cthulhu is one of the Water Elementals" and was engaged in an age-old arch-rivalry with a designated air elemental, Hastur the Unspeakable, described as Cthulhu's "half-brother."

claims.statement_id: Buku Houellebecq H. P. Lovecraft: Against the World, Against Life (2005) mengecam Derleth karena berupaya membentuk ulang kelanjutan Lovecraft yang sepenuhnya amoral menjadi pertentangan stereotipikal antara kekuatan baik dan jahat yang objektif.
claims.quote: Houellebecq's H. P. Lovecraft: Against the World, Against Life (2005) decries Derleth for attempting to reshape Lovecraft's strictly amoral continuity into a stereotypical conflict between forces of objective good and evil.

claims.quote: Lovecraft conceived a detailed genealogy for Cthulhu (published as "Letter 617" in Selected Letters) and made the character a central reference in his works.

claims.statement: The Wikipedia infobox lists Cthulhu's relatives: Azathoth (great-great-grandfather), Yog-Sothoth (grandfather), Shub-Niggurath (grandmother), and Nug (parent).
claims.statement_id: Kotak info Wikipedia mencantumkan kerabat Cthulhu: Azathoth (kakek buyut), Yog-Sothoth (kakek), Shub-Niggurath (nenek), dan Nug (orang tua).
claims.quote: Relatives Azathoth (great-great-grandfather) Yog-Sothoth (grandfather) Shub-Niggurath (grandmother) Nug (parent)

claims.statement: The short story "The Dunwich Horror" (1928) refers to Cthulhu, while The Whisperer in Darkness (1930) hints that one of its characters knows the creature's origins.
claims.statement_id: Cerpen "The Dunwich Horror" (1928) merujuk Cthulhu, sedangkan The Whisperer in Darkness (1930) mengisyaratkan bahwa salah satu tokohnya mengetahui asal makhluk itu.
claims.quote: The short story "The Dunwich Horror" (1928) refers to Cthulhu, while The Whisperer in Darkness (1930) hints that one of his characters knows the creature's origins

claims.statement: The 1931 novella At the Mountains of Madness refers to the "star-spawn of Cthulhu", who warred with another race called the Elder Things before the dawn of man.
claims.statement_id: Novela At the Mountains of Madness (1931) merujuk "star-spawn of Cthulhu" yang berperang dengan ras lain bernama Elder Things sebelum fajar manusia.
claims.quote: The 1931 novella At the Mountains of Madness refers to the "star-spawn of Cthulhu", who warred with another race called the Elder Things before the dawn of man.

claims.statement: Derleth wrote a series of short stories published in Weird Tales (1944–1952) and collected as The Trail of Cthulhu, depicting the struggle of Dr. Laban Shrewsbury and his associates against Cthulhu and his minions.
claims.statement_id: Derleth menulis serangkaian cerita pendek yang terbit di Weird Tales (1944–1952) dan dikumpulkan sebagai The Trail of Cthulhu, yang menggambarkan perjuangan Dr. Laban Shrewsbury dan rekan-rekannya melawan Cthulhu dan para pengikutnya.
claims.quote: Derleth wrote a series of short stories published in Weird Tales (1944–1952) and collected as The Trail of Cthulhu, depicting the struggle of a Dr. Laban Shrewsbury and his associates against Cthulhu and his minions.

claims.statement: The games company TSR included an entire chapter on the Cthulhu mythos (including character statistics) in the first printing of the Dungeons & Dragons sourcebook Deities & Demigods (1980).
claims.statement_id: Perusahaan gim TSR menyertakan satu bab penuh tentang mitos Cthulhu (termasuk statistik karakter) dalam cetakan pertama buku sumber Dungeons & Dragons, Deities & Demigods (1980).
claims.quote: games company TSR included an entire chapter on the Cthulhu mythos (including character statistics) in the first printing of Dungeons & Dragons sourcebook Deities & Demigods (1980).

claims.statement: Cthulhu has appeared as a parody candidate in several elections, including the 2010 Polish presidential election and the 2012 and 2016 US presidential elections.
claims.statement_id: Cthulhu muncul sebagai kandidat parodi dalam beberapa pemilu, termasuk pemilihan presiden Polandia 2010 serta pemilihan presiden AS 2012 dan 2016.
claims.quote: Cthulhu has appeared as a parody candidate in several elections, including the 2010 Polish presidential election and the 2012 and 2016 US presidential elections.

claims.statement: Several organisms have been named after Cthulhu, including the California spider Pimoa cthulhu, the New Guinea moth Speiredonia cthulhui, and Sollasina cthulhu, a fossil echinoderm.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa organisme dinamai menurut Cthulhu, termasuk laba-laba California Pimoa cthulhu, ngengat Papua Nugini Speiredonia cthulhui, dan Sollasina cthulhu, echinodermata fosil.
claims.quote: Several organisms have been named after Cthulhu, including the California spider Pimoa cthulhu, the New Guinea moth Speiredonia cthulhui, and Sollasina cthulhu, a fossil echinoderm.

claims.statement: The Wikipedia infobox lists Cthulhu's aliases: The Sleeper of R'lyeh and High Priest of the Great Old Ones.
claims.statement_id: Kotak info Wikipedia mencantumkan julukan Cthulhu: The Sleeper of R'lyeh dan High Priest of the Great Old Ones.
claims.quote: Aliases The Sleeper of R'lyeh High Priest of the Great Old Ones

claims.statement: Cthulhu has also been spelled in many other ways, including Tulu, Katulu, and Kutulu.
claims.statement_id: Cthulhu juga dieja dengan banyak cara lain, termasuk Tulu, Katulu, dan Kutulu.
claims.quote: Cthulhu has also been spelled in many other ways, including Tulu, Katulu, and Kutulu.

issues.message: Keterkaitan otomatis: nama berkas, deskripsi berkas, kategori "Frankenstein's monster", dipakai di ast.wikipedia.org: Bisarma de Frankenstein. Cek visual tetap diperlukan.

claims.statement: Victor recounts that on a dreary night of November he completed his toils and collected the instruments of life so that he might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing at his feet.
claims.statement_id: Victor menceritakan bahwa pada suatu malam November ia menyelesaikan karyanya dan mengumpulkan alat-alat kehidupan agar dapat menanamkan percikan keberadaan pada benda tak bernyawa di kakinya.
claims.quote: It was on a dreary night of November that I beheld the accomplishment of my toils. With an anxiety that almost amounted to agony, I collected the instruments of life around me, that I might infuse a spark of being into the lifeless thing that lay at my feet.

claims.statement: Victor sees the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathes hard and a convulsive motion agitates its limbs.
claims.statement_id: Victor melihat mata kuning pudar makhluk itu terbuka; makhluk itu bernapas berat dan anggota tubuhnya digerakkan oleh gerak kejang.
claims.quote: I saw the dull yellow eye of the creature open; it breathed hard, and a convulsive motion agitated its limbs.

claims.statement: Victor describes the creature's limbs as in proportion and the features selected as beautiful, yet the yellow skin scarcely covers the muscles and arteries beneath, the hair is lustrous black and flowing, the teeth pearly white, and these only form a more horrid contrast with his watery eyes.
claims.statement_id: Victor menggambarkan anggota tubuh makhluk itu proporsional dan fiturnya dipilih agar indah, tetapi kulit kuningnya nyaris tidak menutupi otot dan arteri, rambutnya hitam mengilap dan terurai, giginya seputih mutiara, dan semua itu hanya menambah kontras mengerikan dengan matanya yang berair.
claims.quote: His limbs were in proportion, and I had selected his features as beautiful. Beautiful! Great God! His yellow skin scarcely covered the work of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a lustrous black, and flowing; his teeth of a pearly whiteness; but these luxuriances only formed a more horrid contrast with his watery eyes

claims.statement: Victor resolves, contrary to his first intention, to make the being of a gigantic stature, that is, about eight feet in height and proportionably large.
claims.statement_id: Victor memutuskan, berlawanan dengan niat semula, membuat makhluk itu bertubuh raksasa, yaitu sekitar delapan kaki tingginya dan besar secara proporsional.
claims.quote: I resolved, contrary to my first intention, to make the being of a gigantic stature, that is to say, about eight feet in height, and proportionably large.

claims.statement: Victor collects bones from charnel-houses and disturbs the tremendous secrets of the human frame; the dissecting room and the slaughter-house furnish many of his materials.
claims.statement_id: Victor mengumpulkan tulang dari rumah mayat dan mengganggu rahasia besar tubuh manusia; ruang bedah dan rumah jagal menyediakan banyak bahan karyanya.
claims.quote: I collected bones from charnel-houses and disturbed, with profane fingers, the tremendous secrets of the human frame. ... The dissecting room and the slaughter-house furnished many of my materials

claims.statement: Once his work is finished, the beauty of Victor's dream vanishes and breathless horror and disgust fill his heart.
claims.statement_id: Setelah karyanya selesai, keindahan mimpi Victor lenyap dan hatinya dipenuhi kengerian yang menyesakkan serta rasa jijik.
claims.quote: now that I had finished, the beauty of the dream vanished, and breathless horror and disgust filled my heart.

claims.statement: The creature says he was more agile than they and could subsist upon coarser diet, bore the extremes of heat and cold with less injury to his frame, and far exceeded their stature.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata ia lebih lincah daripada mereka, dapat hidup dengan makanan yang lebih kasar, tahan panas dan dingin dengan lebih sedikit kerusakan pada tubuhnya, dan jauh lebih tinggi.
claims.quote: I was more agile than they and could subsist upon coarser diet; I bore the extremes of heat and cold with less injury to my frame; my stature far exceeded theirs.

claims.statement: Victor sees a figure of a man advancing with superhuman speed, bounding over the crevices in the ice, whose stature seems to exceed that of man.
claims.statement_id: Victor melihat sosok seperti manusia mendekat dengan kecepatan di atas manusia, melompati celah-celah es, dan tingginya tampak melebihi manusia.
claims.quote: I suddenly beheld the figure of a man, at some distance, advancing towards me with superhuman speed. He bounded over the crevices in the ice, among which I had walked with caution; his stature, also, as he approached, seemed to exceed that of man.

claims.statement: Walton and his crew see a being with the shape of a man but apparently of gigantic stature sitting in a sledge and guiding the dogs.
claims.statement_id: Walton dan awak kapalnya melihat sosok berbentuk manusia tetapi tampak bertubuh raksasa duduk di kereta luncur dan mengemudikan anjing-anjingnya.
claims.quote: a being which had the shape of a man, but apparently of gigantic stature, sat in the sledge and guided the dogs.

claims.statement: The creature seizes books written in the language whose elements he acquired at the cottage: Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch's Lives, and the Sorrows of Werter.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu mengambil buku-buku yang ditulis dalam bahasa yang unsur-unsurnya telah ia pelajari di pondok, yaitu Paradise Lost, satu jilid Plutarch's Lives, dan Sorrows of Werter.
claims.quote: I eagerly seized the prize and returned with it to my hovel. Fortunately the books were written in the language, the elements of which I had acquired at the cottage; they consisted of Paradise Lost, a volume of Plutarch’s Lives, and the Sorrows of Werter.

claims.statement: The creature tells Frankenstein that he is his creature, who ought to be his Adam but is rather the fallen angel whom he drives from joy for no misdeed.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata kepada Frankenstein bahwa ia adalah ciptaannya, yang seharusnya menjadi Adam tetapi lebih seperti malaikat yang jatuh, yang diusir dari kegembiraan tanpa kesalahan.
claims.quote: Remember that I am thy creature; I ought to be thy Adam, but I am rather the fallen angel, whom thou drivest from joy for no misdeed.

claims.statement: The creature says he was benevolent and good, and that misery made him a fiend.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata bahwa ia dahulu baik hati dan baik, dan kesengsaraan membuatnya menjadi iblis.
claims.quote: I was benevolent and good; misery made me a fiend.

claims.statement: The creature says he is malicious because he is miserable, and asks whether he is not shunned and hated by all mankind.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata ia jahat karena ia sengsara, dan bertanya apakah ia tidak dijauhi dan dibenci seluruh umat manusia.
claims.quote: I am malicious because I am miserable. Am I not shunned and hated by all mankind?

claims.statement: The creature demands a creature of another sex, as hideous as himself, saying it is all he can receive and it shall content him.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu menuntut makhluk berjenis kelamin lain yang sama buruk rupanya, dan berkata bahwa hanya itu yang dapat ia terima dan itu akan memuaskannya.
claims.quote: I demand a creature of another sex, but as hideous as myself; the gratification is small, but it is all that I can receive, and it shall content me.

claims.statement: The creature recounts that he grasped a child's throat to silence him and in a moment the child lay dead at his feet.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu menceritakan bahwa ia mencengkeram leher seorang anak untuk membungkamnya dan dalam sekejap anak itu terbaring mati di kakinya.
claims.quote: I grasped his throat to silence him, and in a moment he lay dead at my feet.

claims.statement: The creature tells Victor that he goes, but reminds him that he will be with him on his wedding-night.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata kepada Victor bahwa ia pergi, tetapi mengingatkan bahwa ia akan bersama Victor pada malam pernikahannya.
claims.quote: It is well. I go; but remember, I shall be with you on your wedding-night.

claims.statement: The creature pledges to collect his funeral pile and consume his miserable frame to ashes so that its remains may afford no light to anyone who would create such another as he has been.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berjanji mengumpulkan tumpukan kayu pemakamannya dan membakar tubuh malangnya sampai menjadi abu agar sisa-sisanya tidak memberi petunjuk kepada orang lain yang ingin menciptakan makhluk seperti dirinya.
claims.quote: I shall collect my funeral pile and consume to ashes this miserable frame, that its remains may afford no light to any curious and unhallowed wretch who would create such another as I have been.

claims.statement: The creature says it is with considerable difficulty that he remembers the original era of his being; the events appear confused and indistinct, and a strange multiplicity of sensations seized him.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk itu berkata sulit mengingat awal keberadaannya; peristiwa masa itu tampak kabur, dan serangkaian sensasi aneh menguasainya.
claims.quote: It is with considerable difficulty that I remember the original era of my being; all the events of that period appear confused and indistinct. A strange multiplicity of sensations seized me

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia.com, the book was first published anonymously in 1818, came to be regarded as Shelley's masterpiece, and paved the way for horror classics such as Bram Stoker's Dracula and Robert Louis Stevenson's The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia.com, novel itu pertama kali terbit secara anonim pada 1818, dianggap sebagai mahakarya Shelley, dan membuka jalan bagi klasik horor seperti Dracula karya Bram Stoker dan The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde karya Robert Louis Stevenson.
claims.quote: First published anonymously in 1818, the book came to be regarded as Shelley's masterpiece and paved the way for such horror genre classics as Bram Stoker's Dracula and Robert Louis Stevenson's The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde.

claims.statement: Frankenstein is equal parts Gothic romance, science-fiction adventure, and horror story, has spawned numerous stage and screen adaptations, and has emerged as an icon of modern popular culture.
claims.statement_id: Frankenstein adalah campuran roman Gotik, petualangan fiksi ilmiah, dan kisah horor, melahirkan banyak adaptasi panggung dan layar serta menjadi ikon budaya populer modern.
claims.quote: Equal parts Gothic romance, science-fiction adventure, and horror story, Frankenstein has spawned numerous stage and screen adaptations, emerging as an icon of modern popular culture.

claims.statement: Doctor Frankenstein becomes fixated on the idea of creating a superior race and assembles a synthetic man from the body parts of corpses, imbued with the spark of life through galvanic electrical power; when the creature comes to life, the doctor is repulsed and flees.
claims.statement_id: Dokter Frankenstein terpaku pada gagasan menciptakan ras unggul dan merakit manusia sintetis dari bagian tubuh mayat, yang diberi percikan kehidupan lewat tenaga listrik galvanik; ketika makhluk itu hidup, sang dokter muak dan lari.
claims.quote: Doctor Frankenstein soon becomes fixated on the idea of creating a superior race and uses the body parts of corpses to assemble a synthetic man, imbued with the spark of life through galvanic electrical power. When the creature comes to life, the doctor is repulsed by it and flees

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia.com, in Greek mythology Prometheus steals fire from Zeus and gives it to mortals; like Prometheus, Frankenstein assumes godlike powers when he uncovers the secrets of creation and fabricates a new life.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia.com, dalam mitologi Yunani, Prometheus mencuri api dari Zeus dan memberikannya kepada manusia; seperti Prometheus, Frankenstein memperoleh kekuatan seperti dewa ketika menemukan rahasia penciptaan dan membuat kehidupan baru.
claims.quote: In Greek mythology, Prometheus steals fire from Zeus, the ruler of the heavens, and gives it to the mortals for the benefit of mankind. Like Prometheus, Frankenstein assumes godlike powers when he uncovers the secrets of creation and fabricates a new life.

claims.statement: According to Encyclopedia.com, having spent the winter and spring observing a poor but loving family, the creature teaches himself to speak.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia.com, setelah mengamati sebuah keluarga miskin tetapi penuh kasih selama musim dingin dan semi, sang makhluk mengajari dirinya berbicara.
claims.quote: Having spent the winter and spring observing a poor but loving family, the creature teaches himself to speak.

claims.statement: The creature tells Walton of his unbearable loneliness, expresses remorse for his actions, and leaves the ship to die alone on the ice.
claims.statement_id: Sang makhluk menceritakan kesepiannya yang tak tertahankan kepada Walton, menyatakan penyesalan atas perbuatannya, dan meninggalkan kapal untuk mati sendirian di atas es.
claims.quote: The creature tells Walton of his unbearable loneliness, expresses remorse for his actions, and leaves the ship to die alone on the ice.

claims.statement: The creature's attempt to approach the family is thwarted by his hideous appearance, and he begs Frankenstein to provide him with a mate.
claims.statement_id: Upaya sang makhluk mendekati keluarga itu digagalkan oleh penampilannya yang mengerikan, dan ia memohon kepada Frankenstein agar menyediakan pasangan baginya.
claims.quote: Yet his attempt to approach the family is thwarted by his hideous appearance. The creature begs Frankenstein to provide him with a mate

claims.statement: Frankenstein leaves home to study science at the University of Ingolstadt in Bavaria, Germany.
claims.statement_id: Frankenstein meninggalkan rumah untuk belajar sains di Universitas Ingolstadt di Bavaria, Jerman.
claims.quote: Frankenstein leaves home to study science at the University of Ingolstadt in Bavaria, Germany.

claims.statement: The novel adopts Frankenstein's perspective as he recounts his childhood in Geneva, Switzerland.
claims.statement_id: Novel mengambil sudut pandang Frankenstein saat ia menceritakan masa kecilnya di Jenewa, Swiss.
claims.quote: The novel adopts Frankenstein's perspective as he recounts his childhood in Geneva, Switzerland.

claims.statement: Frankenstein's monster, commonly referred to as Frankenstein, is a fictional character that first appeared in Mary Shelley's 1818 novel Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus as its main antagonist.
claims.statement_id: Monster Frankenstein, yang biasa disebut Frankenstein, adalah tokoh fiksi yang pertama kali muncul dalam novel Mary Shelley tahun 1818, Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, sebagai antagonis utamanya.
claims.quote: Frankenstein's monster, commonly referred to as Frankenstein, is a fictional character that first appeared in Mary Shelley's 1818 novel Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus as its main antagonist.

claims.statement: Mary Shelley's original novel does not give the character a specific name; Victor Frankenstein variously refers to his creation as the creature, fiend, spectre, dæmon, wretch, devil, thing, being, and ogre.
claims.statement_id: Novel asli Mary Shelley tidak memberi tokoh ini nama khusus; Victor Frankenstein menyebut ciptaannya dengan berbagai istilah: creature, fiend, spectre, dæmon, wretch, devil, thing, being, dan ogre.
claims.quote: Mary Shelley's original novel does not give the character a specific name. In the novel, Victor Frankenstein variously refers to his creation as the "creature", "fiend", "spectre", "dæmon", "wretch", "devil", "thing", "being", and "ogre".

claims.statement: Frankenstein's creation referred to himself as a "monster" at least once, as did the residents of a hamlet who saw the creature towards the end of the novel.
claims.statement_id: Ciptaan Frankenstein menyebut dirinya "monster" setidaknya satu kali, begitu pula penduduk sebuah dusun yang melihatnya menjelang akhir novel.
claims.quote: Frankenstein's creation referred to himself as a "monster" at least once, as did the residents of a hamlet who saw the creature towards the end of the novel.

claims.statement: Shelley's title compares the monster's creator, Victor Frankenstein, who later became the monster's namesake, to the mythological character Prometheus, who fashioned humans out of clay and gave them fire.
claims.statement_id: Judul karya Shelley membandingkan pencipta sang monster, Victor Frankenstein, yang kemudian menjadi asal nama sang monster, dengan tokoh mitologi Prometheus, yang membentuk manusia dari tanah liat dan memberi mereka api.
claims.quote: Shelley's title compares the monster's creator, Victor Frankenstein, who later became the monster's namesake, to the mythological character Prometheus, who fashioned humans out of clay and gave them fire.

claims.statement: According to the scholar Joseph Carroll, the monster occupies "a border territory between the characteristics that typically define protagonists and antagonists".
claims.statement_id: Menurut sarjana Joseph Carroll, sang monster menempati "wilayah perbatasan antara ciri-ciri yang lazimnya menentukan protagonis dan antagonis".
claims.quote: According to the scholar Joseph Carroll, the monster occupies "a border territory between the characteristics that typically define protagonists and antagonists".

claims.statement: The most popularly recognized version is Boris Karloff's portrayal of the monster in the 1930s films Frankenstein, Bride of Frankenstein, and Son of Frankenstein, though that incarnation bears little resemblance to the source material.
claims.statement_id: Versi yang paling dikenal luas adalah penampilan Boris Karloff sebagai sang monster dalam film-film 1930-an Frankenstein, Bride of Frankenstein, dan Son of Frankenstein, meskipun wujud itu sangat sedikit menyerupai sumber aslinya.
claims.quote: The most popularly recognized version is Boris Karloff's portrayal of the monster in the 1930s films Frankenstein, Bride of Frankenstein, and Son of Frankenstein, though that incarnation bears little resemblance to the source material.

claims.statement: Since Karloff's portrayal, the creature almost always appears as a towering, undead-like figure, often with a flat-topped angular head and bolts on his neck serving as electrical connectors or grotesque electrodes.
claims.statement_id: Sejak penampilan Karloff, sang makhluk hampir selalu tampil sebagai sosok menjulang mirip mayat hidup, sering berkepala datar bersudut dan berbaut di leher yang berfungsi sebagai penghubung listrik atau elektrode mengerikan.
claims.quote: Since Karloff's portrayal, the creature almost always appears as a towering, undead-like figure, often with a flat-topped angular head and bolts on his neck to serve as electrical connectors or grotesque electrodes.

claims.statement: Wikipedia states that, as opposed to the stiff-legged film version, in the novel the creature is described as much more flexible than a human.
claims.statement_id: Wikipedia menyatakan bahwa, berbeda dengan versi film yang berjalan kaku, dalam novel sang makhluk digambarkan jauh lebih lentur daripada manusia.
claims.quote: (as opposed to the novel, in which he is described as much more flexible than a human)

claims.statement: Victor Frankenstein builds the creature over a two-year period in the attic of his boarding house in Ingolstadt after discovering a scientific principle that allows him to create life from non-living matter.
claims.statement_id: Victor Frankenstein membangun makhluk itu selama dua tahun di loteng rumah pondokannya di Ingolstadt setelah menemukan prinsip ilmiah yang memungkinkannya menciptakan kehidupan dari benda tak hidup.
claims.quote: Victor Frankenstein builds the creature over a two-year period in the attic of his boarding house in Ingolstadt after discovering a scientific principle which allows him to create life from non-living matter.

claims.statement: Later the monster boards the ship but, finding Frankenstein dead, is overcome by grief and pledges to incinerate himself at the northernmost extremity of the globe; he then departs, never to be seen again.
claims.statement_id: Kemudian sang monster naik ke kapal, tetapi mendapati Frankenstein sudah mati, ia dikuasai duka dan berjanji membakar dirinya di "ujung paling utara dunia"; ia lalu pergi dan tidak pernah terlihat lagi.
claims.quote: Later, the monster boards the ship, but upon finding Frankenstein dead, is overcome by grief and pledges to incinerate himself at "the Northernmost extremity of the globe". He then departs, never to be seen again.

claims.statement: Within a decade of publication the creator's name, "Frankenstein", was used to refer to the creature, but it did not become firmly established until much later.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu dekade setelah terbit, nama sang pencipta, "Frankenstein", dipakai untuk menyebut makhluknya, tetapi pemakaian itu baru mapan jauh kemudian.
claims.quote: Within a decade of publication, the name of the creator, "Frankenstein", was used to refer to the creature, but it did not become firmly established until much later.

claims.statement: In 1823 Shelley herself attended a performance of Richard Brinsley Peake's Presumption, the first successful stage adaptation of her novel.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1823 Shelley sendiri menghadiri pertunjukan Presumption karya Richard Brinsley Peake, adaptasi panggung pertama yang sukses dari novelnya.
claims.quote: In 1823, Shelley herself attended a performance of Richard Brinsley Peake's Presumption, the first successful stage adaptation of her novel.

claims.statement: Shelley wrote to her friend Leigh Hunt that this nameless mode of naming the unnameable is rather good.
claims.statement_id: Shelley menulis kepada temannya Leigh Hunt bahwa cara menamai yang tidak bernama itu cukup bagus.
claims.quote: she wrote to her friend Leigh Hunt. "This nameless mode of naming the unnameable is rather good."

claims.statement: Frankenstein agrees and eventually constructs a female creature on a remote island in Orkney but, aghast at the possibility of creating a race of monsters, destroys it before it is complete.
claims.statement_id: Frankenstein setuju dan akhirnya membuat makhluk perempuan di sebuah pulau terpencil di Orkney, tetapi ngeri akan kemungkinan menciptakan ras monster, ia menghancurkannya sebelum selesai.
claims.quote: Frankenstein agrees, and eventually constructs a female creature on a remote island in Orkney, but aghast at the possibility of creating a race of monsters, destroys the female creature before it is complete.

claims.statement: After leaving his creator, the creature kills Victor's best friend Henry Clerval and later Frankenstein's bride Elizabeth Lavenza on their wedding night, whereupon Frankenstein's father dies of grief.
claims.statement_id: Setelah meninggalkan penciptanya, sang makhluk membunuh sahabat terbaik Victor, Henry Clerval, dan kemudian mempelai Frankenstein, Elizabeth Lavenza, pada malam pernikahan mereka, lalu ayah Frankenstein meninggal karena duka.
claims.quote: After leaving his creator, the creature goes on to kill Victor's best friend, Henry Clerval, and later kills Frankenstein's bride, Elizabeth Lavenza, on their wedding night, whereupon Frankenstein's father dies of grief.

claims.statement: The best-known image of Frankenstein's monster in popular culture derives from Boris Karloff's portrayal in the 1931 movie Frankenstein, with makeup applied and designed by Jack P. Pierce.
claims.statement_id: Citra sang monster yang paling dikenal dalam budaya populer berasal dari penampilan Boris Karloff dalam film Frankenstein 1931, dengan riasan yang diterapkan dan dirancang oleh Jack P. Pierce.
claims.quote: The best-known image of Frankenstein's monster in popular culture derives from Boris Karloff's portrayal in the 1931 movie Frankenstein, in which he wore makeup applied and designed by Jack P. Pierce

claims.statement: In the sequel Bride of Frankenstein (1935), the frame narration by a character representing Shelley's friend Lord Byron does refer to the monster as Frankenstein.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sekuel Bride of Frankenstein (1935), narasi pembingkai oleh tokoh yang mewakili teman Shelley, Lord Byron, menyebut sang monster sebagai Frankenstein.
claims.quote: However, in the sequel Bride of Frankenstein (1935), the frame narration by a character representing Shelley's friend Lord Byron does refer to the monster as Frankenstein.

claims.statement: In Dean Koontz's Frankenstein, first published in 2004, the creature is named "Deucalion", after the character from Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel Frankenstein karya Dean Koontz yang pertama kali terbit pada 2004, sang makhluk bernama "Deucalion", sesuai tokoh dari mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: For example, in Dean Koontz's Frankenstein, first published in 2004, the creature is named "Deucalion", after the character from Greek mythology

claims.statement: In the 2014 film I, Frankenstein, the Queen of the Gargoyles, Leonore, gives him the name "Adam" after understanding Victor never gave him one.
claims.statement_id: Dalam film I, Frankenstein (2014), Ratu Gargoyle Leonore memberinya nama "Adam" setelah memahami bahwa Victor tidak pernah memberinya nama.
claims.quote: Another example is the 2014 film I, Frankenstein, where the Queen of the Gargoyles Leonore gives him the name "Adam" after understanding Victor never gave him one.

claims.statement: A picture of the creature appeared in the 1831 edition.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah gambar sang makhluk muncul dalam edisi 1831.
claims.quote: A picture of the creature appeared in the 1831 edition.

claims.statement: The monster kills Victor's younger brother William upon learning of the boy's relation to his creator and frames Justine Moritz, a young woman who lives with the Frankensteins, as the culprit.
claims.statement_id: Sang monster membunuh adik Victor, William, setelah mengetahui hubungan anak itu dengan penciptanya, dan menuduh Justine Moritz, seorang perempuan yang tinggal bersama keluarga Frankenstein, sebagai pelakunya.
claims.quote: The monster kills Victor's younger brother William upon learning of the boy's relation to his creator and frames Justine Moritz, a young woman who lives with the Frankensteins, as the culprit
